items.title: Efficient Reconfiguration of Independent Transversals
items.summary: We study the reconfiguration of independent transversals in graphs with a prescribed vertex partition. Given a graph $G$ with a vertex partition $\mathcal{V}=(V_1,\ldots,V_m)$, an independent transversal is an independent set containing exactly one vertex from each part $V_i$ of $\mathcal{V}$. The reconfiguration problem concerns transforming one independent transversal into another through a sequence of local changes, while preserving the independent transversal property at every step. For any fixed $r\in\mathbb{N}$ and $ε>0$, we present a polynomial-time algorithm that, given an $r$-claw-free graph $G$ with a vertex partition $\mathcal{V}=(V_1,\ldots,V_m)$ and two independent transversals $S$ and $R$, either finds a polynomial-length reconfiguration path between $S$ and $R$, or identifies a nonempty set of partition classes $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathcal{V}$ such that the subgraph induced by their union admits a strong dominating set of size at most $(2+ε)|\mathcal{B}|$. Our result provides an algorithmic counterpart to recent connectivity results for the reconfiguration graph of all independent transversals, and establishes polynomial bounds on its diameter under suitable conditions. As a specific application, we obtain a polynomial-time algorithm for reconfiguring perfect matchings in $r$-uniform bipartite hypergraphs $H=(A,B,E)$, that either produces a polynomial-length reconfiguration path between two given perfect matchings or identifies a subset $S\subseteq A$ whose link hypergraph $E_S$ in $B$ has a small cover.

items.title: Extensibility and denseness of periodic monoid actions
items.summary: A monoid has the periodic approximation (PA) property if, for every full shift on a finite alphabet, finitely supported invariant probability measures are weak-* dense in the space of invariant Borel probability measures. We introduce the class of measure-theoretically extension-compatible (MEC) monoids, consisting of embeddable monoids for which every probability measure-preserving (p.m.p.) action admits an invertible p.m.p. extension. For an embeddable monoid $S$ with free $S$-group $(Γ,γ)$, we prove that the PA property implies MEC, and that the converse holds whenever $Γ$ has the PA property. We establish that every left reversible bicancellative monoid and every finitely generated free monoid is MEC, and deduce the PA property for left amenable monoids that are residually a finite group and for finitely generated free monoids. Moreover, for $S=\mathbb F_d^+$, we characterize the free $S$-group as the unique receiving $S$-group for which all fully supported invariant Markov measures on full shifts on finite alphabets admit invariant invertible extensions.

items.title: Score-based neural ordinary differential equations for reaction-diffusions
items.summary: A diffusion equation can be rewritten as a transport equation driven by the score function of the evolving density. Conventional probability-flow formulations, which move particles deterministically with this score-driven velocity, typically conserve total mass. In this work, we develop a Lagrangian method for reaction-diffusion equations in which each particle carries a position and a physical weight. The characteristic ODEs incorporate source terms into the evolution of the log-density and its gradient, while particle weights track changes in mass. We combine this representation with a learned velocity field and weighted particle training to approximate these dynamics. For non-increasing reaction rates, a relative-entropy inequality supports the mass-normalized self-consistency residual as the training objective. This objective can control the error of the induced density when the growth rate is bounded. The algorithm divides the time interval into short windows. In each window, a frozen velocity generates the particle data for a regression of the network velocity. We draw the particles from period-adapted initial sampling distributions and weight them in the loss partly by their predicted future mass, because the reaction can make regions with little initial mass important later. We numerically investigate the method on the Ornstein--Uhlenbeck (OU) equation with a linear source term, Fisher--KPP equations, and Wasserstein--Fisher--Rao gradient flows.

items.title: The SK model with a sparse variance profile: free energy and AMP-based magnetization estimation at high temperature
items.summary: A generalization of the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model for spin glasses is considered, in which the interaction matrix is endowed with a variance profile that has no particular structure and may be sparse. In the first part of the paper, an asymptotic equivalent of the free energy is derived at sufficiently high temperatures, regardless of the signature of the variance profile matrix. In the second part, the mean of the spin vector under the Gibbs measure is estimated using an Approximate Message Passing algorithm that generalizes the one used for the SK case. The dynamical approach of Adhikari et al (J Stat Phys 2021), originally developed for the classical SK model, is adapted to the present setting to obtain these results.

items.title: On four problems from the Kourovka Notebook: spectra, periodic automorphism groups, commutators, and operator simplicity
items.summary: We examine Problems 18.62(a), 18.63, 18.65, and 20.120 of the Kourovka Notebook. First, a family of semidirect products involving $\operatorname{PSL}_2(p^2)$ gives arbitrarily many pairwise nonisomorphic groups critical with respect to one simple-group spectrum, subject to explicit arithmetic congruences. Second, a completed-algebra construction using sparse torsion identities and a matrix Golod-Shafarevich-Vinberg inequality produces an infinite periodic group generated by two fixed-point-free automorphisms of order five of an abelian group. Third, we give a short matrix proof that the class of elements of order three in $\operatorname{PSL}_2(8)$ contradicts the assertion in Problem 18.65 as written. Finally, we spell out how P. Hall's 1962 wreath-power theorems answer Problem 20.120 under the usual normal-subgroup meaning of simplicity for a group with one distinguished automorphism. The four arguments have substantially different provenance. In particular, the last is a consequence of a known construction, not a priority claim. The two longer constructions are recorded in detail for independent mathematical scrutiny.

items.title: Applications of QR-based Vector-Valued Rational Approximation
items.summary: Several applications of the QR-AAA algorithm, a greedy scheme for vector-valued rational approximation, are presented. The focus is on demonstrating the flexibility and practical effectiveness of QR-AAA in a variety of computational settings, including Stokes flow computation, multivariate rational approximation, function extension, the development of novel quadrature methods and near-field approximation in the boundary element method.

items.title: An Obstruction to Realizing Aspherical $3$-Manifold Groups via Torus Surgery
items.summary: Let $Y$ be a closed, connected, oriented, aspherical $3$-manifold with fundamental group $π= π_1(Y)$ and positive first Betti number $β_1(Y) > 0$, and let $X_0 = Y \times S^1$. We prove that no torus surgery on $X_0$ along a torus-fibered $T^2$-knot $T \subseteq X_0$ can yield a $4$-manifold $X = X_{0; T, f}$ with fundamental group $π$. The obstruction combines the vanishing of the Euler characteristic of $X$ with a classifying-map argument showing that the unimodular intersection form on $H^2(X; \mathbb{Z})$ must admit an isotropic subgroup of rank $β_1(π)$, forcing $χ(X) \geq 2$. Along the way, we also present an independent geometric proof via covering space theory, the Sphere Theorem, and Scott's Core Theorem that the fundamental group of a closed aspherical $3$-manifold is torsion-free.

items.title: Mesh-Free Weak-Form Regression for Learning Interaction Kernels from Particle Trajectories
items.summary: We propose mesh-free weak-form regression for learning interaction kernels from noisy particle trajectories. Our method uses smooth test functions to avoid differentiating noisy data and empirical particle averages to avoid density reconstruction and spatial grids. We then fit sparse combinations of candidate functions, evaluating interaction terms on sampled particle pairs to avoid all-pair quadratic cost. By transferring identifiability from the mean-field limit, we prove high-probability coefficient error bounds that separate finite-particle, time-discretization, observation-noise, and pair-sampling errors, without grid-resolution or density-estimation terms. We evaluate one-dimensional (1D) Newtonian-repulsion, 2D predator-prey, and 10D distance-localized experiments. The numerical results show trends consistent with the theoretical coefficient-error bounds. Comparisons of weak and forward-difference formulations with LASSO, Ridge, and OLS show that weak LASSO gives the smallest coefficient and drift errors in the three nominal experiments.

items.title: Automorphism groups of solvable groups of finite abelian ranks
items.summary: This paper gives a new explicit construction of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebraic hull for virtually solvable groups $Γ$ of finite abelian ranks, taking into account the spectrum $S$ of the group $Γ$. As an application, we make a detailed study of the structure of $Aut(Γ)$ in the finitely generated case and show that a number of natural subgroups are $S$-arithmetic under the condition that $Fitt(Γ)$ is $S$-arithmetic. We then proceed by demonstrating that $Out(Γ)$ has a $S$-arithmetic image in the group of algebraic outer automorphisms of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebraic hull. We finish by discussing further applications of the $\mathbb{Q}$-algebraic hull towards an open conjecture by Nekrashevych and Pete and topological fixed point theory.

items.title: Range Failure, Resolvent Growth, and Resonance in Partially Dissipative Systems
items.summary: We analyze resonance for partially dissipative systems, $\dot u=Au+f(t)$, where $A$ generates a strongly stable semigroup $S(t)$ on a Hilbert space $H$. {Resonance is} the phenomenon whereby a bounded, time-periodic $f$ yields an unbounded $u$, classically occurring when $A$ has imaginary eigenvalues. In infinite dimensions, however, several other resonance notions, introduced here, may occur. Classically, {$T$-periodic solvability} is equivalent to a range condition: $\mathcal{R}(I-S(T))=H$. We describe a hierarchy of range failures, and demonstrate how the growth rate of~$||(A-iωI)^{-1}||_H$ dictates a regularity gap between $u$ and $f$. For super-polynomial growth, that gap can be infinite. We demonstrate this phenomenon and its equivalence to the existence of smooth resonant forces. The theory is motivated by a well-studied hyperbolic-parabolic system, which is a simplification of fluid-solid interactions. Our main result shows that, for a carefully constructed geometry, the PDE system exhibits smooth-forcing resonance for a dense set of periods. The geometry sharply violates geometric conditions for which finite regularity losses were shown previously.

items.title: Learning observable propagation with sparse local moments
items.summary: We propose a unified framework for predicting local moment dynamics in high-dimensional many-body systems from short-time trajectories. Thanks to the locality of the dynamics, we construct the transition moment matrices by projecting the Markov operator onto low-order connected-cluster basis functions supported near the target observable. Exploiting the spatial decay of time-lagged correlations, {these matrices} can be approximated in sparse-plus-low-rank form using trajectory samples, with computational cost scaling linearly in the system dimension and the number of trajectories. The learning error can be further reduced by correcting the memory effect induced by the Galerkin projection. We numerically demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in extrapolating the dynamics of various many-body systems, including Langevin and Glauber dynamics for classical systems as well as Lindblad dynamics for open quantum systems. In addition, for a class of single-site Glauber dynamics, we establish error bounds for sparse-plus-low-rank compression and uniform-in-time bounds for connected-cluster approximation and observable propagation with compressed transition moment matrices.

items.title: Nesting in additive manufacturing using quantum annealing
items.summary: Nesting in powder bed fusion (PBF), an additive manufacturing (AM) process, determines the positions and orientations of parts within the build space and influences build height and build time. As the number of parts and feasible placements increases, the nesting problem becomes computationally demanding. Exact approaches are limited to small problem sizes as computational effort increases rapidly with the problem size, while heuristic and metaheuristic approaches involve a trade-off between solution quality and computation time. Quantum annealing (QA) offers an alternative for solving combinatorial optimization problems, but its application to nesting in AM remains largely unexplored. This paper presents a QA-based approach for nesting in AM to investigate its feasibility and its scaling behavior across three problem sizes. An iterative binary quadratic model based approach (IBQM) is developed to minimize build height while considering the geometric characteristics of AM parts. Geometric abstraction, iterative decomposition, and variable pruning are applied to address the computational complexity of the nesting problem. The approach is evaluated using three cases with increasing problem sizes and compared to a classical approach combining tabu search and simulated annealing (TBSA). Compared with TBSA, IBQM reduces the build height of the original parts by up to 13.32% and the computation time by up to 74.27%.

items.title: Maxwell's equations with thin wires in critical scaling
items.summary: We derive effective equations for a situation in which electromagnetic waves hit an array of very thin wires. We study two cases, perfectly conducting wires and highly conducting wires, and investigate in both the critical scaling of the parameters. The electric field $E^η$ and the magnetic field $H^η$ satisfy the time-harmonic Maxwell equations, and the small parameter $η>0$ is the spacing of the wires. A non-critical scaling of the wires implies either that the wires have no effect or that the tangential component of the limiting electric field in the direction of the wires vanishes along the effective interface. In the critical scaling, we observe an interesting effect: The wires act as oscillators and there is a relation between the electric field in longitudinal direction and the jump of the magnetic field in transversal direction involving second derivatives of a flux quantity.

items.title: A rational model for the fiberwise THH transfer I: Sullivan algebras
items.summary: Given a map $f$ of fibrations over a space $B$ such that the fiber of $f$ is simply connected and finitely dominated, we prove that its fiberwise THH transfer, considered as a map of parametrized spectra over $B$, is rationally modeled by the Hochschild homology transfer of a Sullivan model of $f$. The proof goes in two steps. Firstly, we use the machinery of higher categorical traces to show that the fiberwise THH transfer can be computed internally to parametrized spectra. Secondly, we model the resulting description rationally using work of Braunack-Mayer, who proved that parametrized spectra can be modeled by modules over Sullivan algebras. In Part II, we will use our result to obtain a rational model of the Becker-Gottlieb transfer, and for applications to manifold topology.

items.title: Recovering the Euclidean Geometry of High-Dimensional Data Under Heterogeneous Noise
items.summary: Pairwise Euclidean distances provide a simple geometric representation of high-dimensional data and underlie many data analysis methods, including clustering, visualization, and manifold learning. However, in real-world applications, these distances can be severely corrupted by heterogeneous noise, where different data points are subject to different, and potentially large, noise levels. Such noise distorts the distances inhomogeneously, leading to a misrepresentation of the underlying data geometry. In this work, we ask whether the underlying clean Euclidean geometry can nevertheless be recovered from the corrupted pairwise distances. We answer this question affirmatively, showing that, perhaps surprisingly, such recovery is possible across a broad class of high-dimensional settings with underlying low-dimensional geometry, even when the noise magnitudes vary substantially across observations. We develop a principled approach for recovering the clean pairwise distances, without prior knowledge of either the clean data structure or the noise distribution, and establish probabilistic recovery guarantees. In particular, the recovery error converges to zero at polynomial rates as the feature dimension and dataset size increase simultaneously. Experiments on synthetic datasets demonstrate accurate recovery of the Euclidean geometry in challenging regimes and improved robustness of downstream methods that rely on pairwise distances. When applied to real single-cell RNA sequencing data, our method reliably recovers local neighborhood structure, enabling accurate nearest-neighbor identification used in many downstream analyses.

items.title: Express Language Modeling
items.summary: We introduce a new tool, Express, for converting a non-causal attention approximation into a causal approximation with matching approximation guarantees. When combined with the state-of-the-art Thinformer approximation, Express improves upon the best known causal attention guarantees, delivering $\log^{3/2}(n)/s$ approximation error with only $O(s)$ memory and $O(s^2 \log^2(n))$ compression overhead for a sequence of length $n$. We pair these developments with an efficient I/O-aware Triton implementation, demonstrate substantial speedups over FlashAttention 2, and use Express to overcome four resource bottlenecks in the language modeling pipeline: long-context prefill, KV cache compression, long-form memory-constrained decoding, and long-form compute-constrained decoding.

items.title: A quotient formula for the Behrend function
items.summary: The Behrend function is essential in enumerative geometry. However, computing it, even in zero dimension, has been a highly subtle and mysterious matter since its introduction in the 2000s. We present a quotient formula for the Behrend function of any closed $r$-dimensional affine scheme $X^r \subset \mathbb{A}^N$, evaluated at a singular point, where $0\leq r \leq N-1$. In particular, if the scheme is monomial, we associate parallelepipeds to it and interpret the Behrend function as simple volume information about them. The results here, in particular, recover the recent results of Graffeo-Ricolfi for the zero-dimensional case in 2D in \cite{Graffeo-Ricolfi}, and also the more recent result of Polini-Sammartan-Ulrich on the zero-dimensional case in \cite{PSU26}.

items.title: Thresholds of the Polya Szego inequality for the fractional logarithmic p-Laplacian
items.summary: We establish three surprising features of the Polya Szego principle for the full signed energy of the fractional logarithmic p-Laplacian. First, the energy doesn't not decrease under rearrangement for all admissible functions. Second, the sharp threshold for Polarization and Schwarz rearrangements are different. Third, for Steiner rearrangement, the threshold in 1 dimension and N dimensions is not the same. Additionally the dimension doesn't appear in the formula.

items.title: Balancing-based model reduction for output-constrained optimal control of switched linear systems
items.summary: We develop a balanced-truncation (BT) framework for model-order reduction of optimal control problems governed by switched linear systems, with quadratic tracking costs, convex input constraints, and Moreau--Yosida-regularized output constraints. For general Petrov--Galerkin reduced models, we derive an a posteriori bound for the error in the optimal value function, and combine it with BT-based estimates of the dynamical-system reduction error. We show that BT preserves the duality structure underlying the first-order optimality conditions, making first-reduce-then-optimize and first-optimize-then-reduce equivalent. Consequently, reducing the forward system also reduces the associated optimality system, leading to a certified, online-efficient, and online-adaptive approximation of the parameterized solution operator. The reduced model can therefore be reused across different regularization parameters, constraint sets, switching signals, and reference trajectories.

items.title: Dynamic Assortment Optimization Under Arbitrary Demand Distributions: The Uniform Price Setting
items.summary: We study the joint optimization of assortment and inventory when products are identically priced and the total demand (number of customers) is uncertain. A seller chooses initial inventories before customers arrive and every customer buys her preferred product among those still in stock according to a choice model known to the seller. The objective is to maximize the (expected) total sales, subject to a capacity constraint. We give a $(1-1/e)^2$-approximation under any ranking-based choice model and a $(1-1/e-\varepsilon)$-approximation under the Markov chain choice model, where $\varepsilon$ is a tunable parameter that trades off runtime with approximation guarantee. Our guarantees hold for arbitrary demand distributions and do not require the ubiquitous Increasing Failure Rate (IFR) assumption. In fact, our results also improve on the state-of-the-art approximations for IFR demand distributions. Key to our results is the discovery of hidden submodularity in these problems and the development of efficient procedures to evaluate (or approximate) the objective values. Specifically, we uncover a novel connection to online bipartite matching (for ranking-based models) and use stochastic coupling arguments (for the Markov chain choice model) to reduce the problems to instances of constrained submodular maximization. This opens the door to applying the vast algorithmic machinery for submodular maximization to our problem setting, leading, for example, to natural generalizations beyond cardinality constraint where no approximation results were previously known.

items.title: Construction of entropies for cross-diffusion systems
items.summary: The analysis of cross-diffusion systems with nonsymmetric and indefinite diffusion matrices often relies on the existence of entropies, that is, Lyapunov functionals whose dissipation often yields gradient estimates. We propose a general strategy for constructing entropies for two-species cross-diffusion systems, based on the assumption that the mobility matrix is symmetric, in accordance with Onsager's reciprocal relations. The symmetry condition leads to a linear hyperbolic equation in two variables, which can be reformulated as a linear transport system along the eigendirections of the diffusion matrix, related to the approach of Jenssen and Kogan for hyperbolic conservation laws. Positive solutions to this system yield a family of entropies parametrized by two arbitrary functions of one variable. Sufficient conditions for their existence on (possibly unbounded) characteristic rectangles are given, the mechanisms that may prevent the existence of an entropy are identified, and systems without any entropy structure are presented. The general construction recovers known entropies for models arising in physics and biology and provides new ones. For systems with an arbitrary number of components, we derive sufficient conditions for the existence of separable entropies and give a rank criterion for the uniqueness of entropies (up to affine functions). Cross-diffusion systems without symmetry of the mobility matrix are also discussed.

items.title: Stability of crystalline measures under random perturbations
items.summary: In this paper, we study random perturbations and the diffraction properties of translation-bounded crystalline measures. Under a non-vanishing assumption on the known perturbation factor, we prove that, almost surely, any realization of the perturbed measure preserves sufficient structural information to allow the full recovery of the original measure. Previous works have only considered crystalline measures with uniformly discrete supports and equal-mass atoms. Our general setting includes many important crystalline measures that were excluded until now. To treat this broader setting, we adopt a different framework. In this work, we model the perturbation as a random measure rather than as a random set. In particular, this leads us to consider not only perturbations of the support, but also perturbations of the atoms' masses. On the other hand, using elementary techniques of Fourier analysis, we prove that any translation-bounded crystalline measure has a diffraction measure, and we explicitly compute its diffraction.

items.title: Decreasing Filtrations, $C_{2}$-Algebra and Twisted Modules
items.summary: We investigate a question posed by Gaberdiel and Gannon (2009) concerning the relationship between $C_{2}$-algebras and twisted modules. To each twisted module $W$ of a vertex algebra $V$, we first associate a decreasing sequence of subspaces $\bigl\{E_{n}^{T}(W)\bigr\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ and demonstrate that the associated graded vector space $\mathrm{gr}_{\mathcal{E}}^{T}(W)$ is a twisted module of vertex Poisson algebra $\mathrm{gr}_{\mathcal{E}}^{T}(V)$. We introduce another decreasing sequence of subspaces $\bigl\{C_{n}^{T}(W)\bigr\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq2}}$ and establish a connection between $\bigl\{E_{n}^{T}(W)\bigr\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ and $\bigl\{C_{n}^{T}(W)\bigr\}_{n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq2}}$. By utilizing the twisted module $\mathrm{gr}_{\mathcal{E}}^{T}(W)$ of vertex Poisson algebra $\mathrm{gr}_{\mathcal{E}}^{T}(V)$, we prove that for any twisted module $W$ of a vertex algebra $V$, $C_{2}$-cofiniteness implies $C_{n}$-cofiniteness for all $n\geq 2$. Furthermore, we employ $\mathrm{gr}_{\mathcal{E}}^{T}(W)$ to study generating subspaces of $\frac{1}{T}\mathbb{N}$-graded twisted modules of lower truncated $\mathbb{Z}$-graded vertex algebras.

items.title: The random KKM mapping principle and its applications
items.summary: Based on the recently developed random Brouwer fixed point theorem and the theory of stable compactness, we establish a random Knaster--Kuratowski--Mazurkiewicz (KKM) mapping principle in Hausdorff topological $L^0$-modules. As consequences of this principle, we obtain several results on fixed points, minimax problems, variational inequalities, and conditional games. These results solve a large class of noncompact problems in random functional analysis and its applications.

items.title: Full range of infinite point blow-up exponents for the critical generalized KdV equation
items.summary: For the quintic, mass critical generalized Korteweg-de Vries equation, for any $ν\in (\frac{1}{2}, 1)$, we prove the existence of solutions in the energy space that blow up in finite time $T>0$ with the blow-up rate $\|\partial_x u(t)\|_{L^2} \sim (T-t)^{-ν}$ (infinite point blow-up). These solutions are constructed arbitrarily close to the family of solitons and correspond to the concentration of a soliton traveling at $+\infty$ in space as $t\uparrow T$. This complements the previous results obtained in the work of Martel, Merle, Raphaël in 2015 on infinite point exotic blow-up, which were valid under the technical restriction $ν>\frac {11}{13}$. The value $ν=\frac 12$ corresponds to a critical case to be treated elsewhere. At the technical level, we implement a modification of the virial-energy functional, to allow all $ν> \frac 12$ and simplify the proof of energy estimates.

items.title: Finitary Cartesian closed varieties and semigroup actions
items.summary: We build on some ideas of Richard Garner. Let $M$ be a monoid and $B$ a Boolean algebra. A matched pair $[B|M]$ consists of $B$ and $M$ satisfying some axioms introduced by Garner. He then showed that every such matched pair determines a Boolean left restriction monoid $S = S[B|M]$. In this paper, we show that the data of a $[B|M]$-set, an action of a matched pair, may be encoded by means of what we call a factorizable Boolean supported action by $S$. This means that the category of $[B|M]$-sets is equivalent to the category of factorizable Boolean supported actions of $S$. We deduce, as a result of Garner's work, that every non-degenerate finitary Cartesian closed variety is equivalent to the category of factorizable Boolean supported actions of some Boolean left restriction monoid $S$.

items.title: Ahlfors--Weill Extension, Asymptotically Conformal Curves and Epstein--Poincaré Surfaces
items.summary: The Ahlfors--Weill construction explicitly extends a univalent function $f$ with Schwarzian norm less than $1/2$ to a quasiconformal homeomorphism of the Riemann sphere, an extension that can be understood geometrically through Epstein surfaces. For asymptotically conformal curves, the uniformization map can be extended to a larger disk, and Loewner theory can be used to verify that this extension is quasiconformal. In this paper, we construct a local quasireflection with such an extension. Using this local quasireflection, we modify classical estimates of Ahlfors and show that domains bounded by asymptotically conformal curves have asymptotically similar hyperbolic and quasihyperbolic metrics. Furthermore, by combining these estimates with a geometric reinterpretation of the extension through Epstein surfaces, we show that the Epstein-Poincaré surfaces of the complementary domains are arbitrarily close to one another near the curve.

items.title: Strongly Monotone Central Path Equations for Quadratic Cone Programs
items.summary: We introduce a canonical central path for the homogeneous embedding of quadratic cone programs, defined by strongly monotone equations whose modulus is the barrier parameter. We prove that the path exists uniquely, is smooth, and lies on a sphere of fixed radius. Under mild regularity assumptions, its limit points recover optimal solutions or certificates of infeasibility. Exploiting the fact that the embedding operator has a closed-form resolvent, we derive Josephy-Newton steps that retain the nonlinear embedding equations and linearize only the complementarity conditions. Each step reduces to quasi-definite linear system solves and a scalar quadratic. Using this, we derive a new predictor-corrector interior-point method with a surrogate formulation that allows the predictor and corrector to share a single sparse factorization. We provide an open-source implementation, cpo3, for linear and quadratic programs. On 675 instances from eight benchmark collections, with presolve and crossover disabled, cpo3 achieves the highest verified solve count (631) and the lowest penalized shifted geometric mean runtime among the tested open-source and commercial solvers. It is the only tested solver to solve all 138 Maros-Meszaros instances to high accuracy. Moreover, we establish Euclidean and local-norm error bounds that motivate a warm-start heuristic for the proposed algorithm, yielding up to 2.3x median runtime speedup over cold starts on perturbed Netlib and Maros-Meszaros problems.

items.title: Minimal Systems of Binomial Generators for the Ideals of Certain Monomial Curves
items.summary: Let $a, b$ and $n > 1$ be three positive integers such that $a$ and $\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} b^j$ are relatively prime. In this paper, we prove that the toric ideal $I$ associated to the submonoid of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by $\{\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} b^j\} \cup \{\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} b^j + a\, \sum_{j=0}^{i-2} b^j \mid i = 2, \ldots, n\}$ is determinantal. Moreover, we prove that for $n > 3$, the ideal $I$ has a unique minimal system of generators if and only if $a < b-1$.

items.title: Slowly travelling infinite point blow-up for the critical generalized KdV equation
items.summary: We study the finite time blow up phenomenon for the quintic, mass critical gKdV equation. We prove the existence of a class of solutions $U$ with infinite point, finite time blow up behavior, at the particular blow up rate $$\|\partial_x U(t)\|_{L^2} \sim (T-t)^{-ν}\quad \text{as} \quad t \uparrow T,$$ where $ν= \frac 12$, $T$ is the blow up time and where the travel speed of the blow up bubble is logarithmic. Therefore, we call this behaviour slowly travelling infinite point blow up. The special blow up rate $ν=\frac 12$ is a threshold which separates finite and infinite point bubbling. In a previous work arXiv:2511.13538, the author constructed other infinite point blow up solutions for the continuum of rates $ν\in(\frac 12,1)$, using polynomial tails in the space variable and extending the results in arXiv:1209.2510, restricted to $ν> \frac{11}{13}$. However, that work suggested a change of the tail for the threshold case. In the present paper, we consider an exponentially decaying tail on the right in space. As in arXiv:2511.13538, the initial data can be taken arbitrarily close to the ground state in $H^1$. From a technical perspective, in addition to the change of tail, we have to adapt the energy-virial functional to the presence of the exponential tail, by modifying a scaling term used to control the right-hand side of the blow up solution.

items.title: Stability Certification for Approximate Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
items.summary: Neural-network approximations of nonlinear model predictive control can reduce online computational costs, but ensuring constraint satisfaction and closed-loop stability remains challenging. We propose a framework in which convex optimisation is used to restore feasibility under suitable local assumptions, while bounds on the corrected controller's cost suboptimality provide sufficient conditions for practical closed-loop stability. To assess these conditions over a compact set of initial states, we investigate a branch-and-bound approach based on convex relaxations of the nonlinear dynamics, with probabilistic guarantees established through scenario optimisation. The proposed approach represents a step towards combining the computational efficiency of approximate nonlinear model predictive control with systematic methods for restoring feasibility and assessing stability.

items.title: Costate-Conditioned Dynamic Programming for Parallel-in-Time Solution of Equality-Constrained Optimal Control Problems
items.summary: Gradient based trajectory optimisation algorithms spend most of their per-iteration time on a structured Newton--KKT system. The system corresponds to an equality-constrained linear-quadratic optimal control problem and dedicated Riccati-type solvers exhibit linear complexity in the horizon length. Parallel-in-time algorithms exhibit the potential to reduce the complexity to logarithmic in the horizon by distributing several subtrajectories over multiple cores and then stitch together the results by means of an associative scan. Existing exact formulations condition each subtrajectory on its terminal state. Each subproblem then carries the reachability to that terminal state explicitly as constraint rows. The associated reachability decision however is ill-conditioned for weakly actuated systems. In this work we condition each subtrajectory on the terminal costate instead. The resulting subproblems can now be computed by a free-end Riccati recursion without reachability carrying rows. This approach effectively compensates for the ill-conditioning of weakly actuated systems but requires additional bookkeeping with Lagrangian multipliers when stitching together the various subproblems. Numerically the method reproduces a direct solution of the primal-dual Newton-KKT system to $10^{-12}$ in relative terms, on a weakly controllable chain of masses. The accurracy rivals that of a sequential recursion, whereas terminal-state conditioning loses up to six digits or fails. Operation counts on a problem with 64 subtrajectories and a horizon of 4096 stages gives a speed-up of 26 compared with a sequential solve.

items.title: An annihilation-number Caro-Wei bound: a TxGraffiti conjecture and an independence-number bracket
items.summary: Computable independence bounds give intervals that can be compared by containment or by their worst-case endpoint ratios. For positive maximum degree $Δ$, the Caro-Wei sum $W$ bounds the independence number from below, while $(Δ+1)W/2$ bounds it from above. A second interval has the Havel-Hakimi residue as its lower endpoint and the annihilation number as its upper endpoint. This note proves that the annihilation number does not exceed the Caro-Wei upper endpoint. This upper bound is sharp, with equality for regular graphs of positive degree and even order. Since the residue is at least $W$, this upper bound places the residue-annihilation interval inside the Caro-Wei interval. Both endpoints can improve strictly on one graph, although the sharp worst-case endpoint ratio remains unchanged, even for connected graphs. The annihilation-number bound also proves a conjectured lower estimate based on the annihilation number and residue for every connected graph with at least three vertices. Equality in this estimate holds for exactly eight graph types, while the single edge violates it. For maximum degree at least three, however, the estimate never exceeds the residue, even without connectedness.

items.title: Color Refinement Distinguishes Connected Rooted Outerplanar Graphs
items.summary: Color refinement, also known as the $1$-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm ($1$-WL), is a classical near-linear-time heuristic for graph isomorphism, which also captures the expressive power of message-passing graph neural networks. A long line of work asks on which graph classes $1$-WL, or its higher-dimensional variant $k$-WL, identifies every graph; the least such $k$ is the WL-dimension of the class. Planar graphs have WL-dimension at most $3$ (Kiefer, Ponomarenko and Schweitzer, 2019), and whether $2$-WL already distinguishes all planar graphs is a central open problem. We bring new insight on this question for outerplanar graphs, whose WL-dimension is $2$. We show that color refinement, i.e. 1-WL, distinguishes connected rooted outerplanar graphs: two non-isomorphic such graphs receive different stable colorings once a single vertex, the root, is individualized. The root is necessary, as there are non-isomorphic $2$-connected outerplanar graphs that color refinement does not distinguish. Our result extends to pseudo-rooted graphs, in which the stable coloring merely contains a singleton color class, and to non-connected graphs whose components all contain such a class. Consequently, the $(1,1)$-WL test of Rattan and Seppelt (2023) distinguishes all outerplanar graphs. We proceed by inversion: we reconstruct a connected rooted outerplanar graph, up to isomorphism, from its color graph, the weighted quotient of the graph by its stable color classes, together with its root color. The reconstruction runs in time linear in the output size and is canonical, which yields a near-linear-time canonization algorithm for these graphs. Our main tool is a dichotomy lemma, formalized in Rocq: in a rooted outerplanar graph with an equitable coloring, every block either receives pairwise distinct colors or admits a color-preserving mirror symmetry fixing its vertex closest to the root.

items.title: From Diagonal Coloring to Proper Vertex Labelings Distinguishing Adjacent Facial Sums
items.summary: In this paper we study proper vertex labelings of 3-connected plane graphs that give distinct boundary-vertex sums to faces sharing an edge. Let $λ(G)$ be the least $k$ for which labels from $\{0,\ldots,k\}$ suffice, and let $\laml(G)$ be its arbitrary-real-list counterpart. Our two main results are an eight-element list theorem for fullerenes and the universal bound $λ(G)\le708587$ for all 3-connected plane graphs. We establish structural nine- and eight-color bounds, classify triangulations whose vertices of degree at least five form an independent set, and determine their exact diagonal chromatic numbers. We also prove closure under triangular sums for $q\ge7$ diagonal colors, with an optimal uniform threshold. For cubic 3-connected plane graphs we obtain $λ\le14$, improving to $λ\le9$ in the bipartite case.

items.title: Self-Interpretations and Krají{č}ek-Theories
items.summary: We study self-interpretations of theories and their connection to Krajíček-theories. Our two main results are the following. Firstly, if the self-interpretations of a theory form a group in the category ${\sf INT}_3$ of theories and interpretations, then the theory is a Krajíček-theory. Secondly, a sequential theory is a Krajíček-theory iff all its self-interpretations are initial. Here initiality of the interpretation $K$ means roughly that its internal interpretations of the weak theory ${\sf S}^1_2$ are initial in all interpretations of ${\sf S}^1_2$.

items.title: Fourier Harmonics and Pentagonal Rigidity in the Planar Ulam Floating Body Problem
items.summary: We give a new proof that the disk is the only strictly convex planar body floating in equilibrium in every orientation at perimetral densities $σ=1/5$ and $σ=2/5$. The proof uses the Fourier harmonics of the chord-angle function and the closure relations of the associated pentagonal carousel. Their combination gives inequalities that force the body to be a disk.

items.title: Convergence rate of observables in the Marcus-Lushnikov process toward Smoluchowski with singular homogeneous kernels
items.summary: We study the approximation of the Smoluchowski coagulation equation by the Marcus--Lushnikov process with $N$ initial particles for the singular family of kernels $K\_α(x,y)=x^{-α}+y^{-α}, α> 0$. For regular mean-field particle systems, pathwise fluctuations are naturally expected on the scale $N^{-1/2}$, whereas sufficiently smooth observables may exhibit a weak error of order $N^{-1}$ after averaging. The singularity of $K\_α$ at the origin makes it unclear whether this second-order mechanism survives. We prove that it does: for a class of sufficiently regular nonlinear functionals of the empirical measure, we establish a weak error of order $N^{-1}$ on finite time intervals. The main mechanism is a regularization produced by the singular dynamics itself. Small clusters coagulate at increasingly large rates, which generates exponential moments in the singular variable $x^{-α}$ and yields a rapid escape from the singularity at zero. We exploit this phenomenon through a Wasserstein-type distance adapted to $x^{-α}$, together with weighted total variation estimates used to construct and control the derivative of the Smoluchowski flow.

items.title: A commuting operator self-test for exact entanglement embezzlement
items.summary: We show that the optimal commuting operator correlation for a variant of Coladangelo's two-player generalized nonlocal game, based on the embezzlement of entanglement, is a commuting operator self-test. Our result gives the first correlation self-test for an exact entanglement embezzlement protocol in the commuting operator framework. Because the unique optimal correlation necessitates the exact embezzlement of entanglement, the correlation is unrealizable using quantum tensor-product models, even if the local spaces are allowed to be infinite dimensional. Our proof relies on Harris' unique abstract state characterization of exact embezzlement of entanglement involving Cuntz algebras.

items.title: The $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction for pro-graded Huber pairs
items.summary: Inspired by the theory of pro-graded adic rings developed recently by Ishizuka and Yoshikawa, we introduce and study the notions of a pro-graded Huber ring and a pro-graded Huber pair \begin{equation*}((\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}), \mathcal{A}^{+}),\end{equation*}which capture the intuition of a complete Huber ring (or Huber pair) equipped with a dense graded subring. Using these notions, we define and study an analog \begin{equation*}\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}, \mathcal{A}^{+})\end{equation*}of the $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction from algebraic geometry in the realm of adic spaces, without restricting our attention to adic spaces satisfying any Noetherian or finite-type assumptions. We consider gradings both by $\mathbb{Z}$ and by $\mathbb{Z}[1/p]$ for a fixed prime number $p$, so our $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction recovers both classical examples such as usual adic projective space $\mathbb{P}_{K}^{n,\textrm{ad}}$ and infinite-type, perfectoid examples such as perfectoid projective space $\mathbb{P}_{K}^{n,\textrm{perfd}}$. Using GAGA, we prove that the adic analytification of any projective variety $X$ over a nonarchimedean field $K$ can be described as the adic $\operatorname{Proj}$ of a suitable pro-graded affinoid algebra $\mathcal{A}$. Moreover, we prove that in this case $\dim X=\dim \mathcal{A}-1$. We also relate our adic $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction to formal models.

items.title: Guerra Interpolation and Optimal Transport: Kantorovich Bounds, Brenier Maps and the Replicon
items.summary: Since Guerra's work, mean-field spin glasses have been studied through Hamilton--Jacobi equations. Here, using the Curie--Weiss and the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick models as prototypical examples, we show that his celebrated interpolation method is itself an optimal transport computation. After a linear change of variables the finite-$N$ pressure becomes an action $u$ with $\partial_t u = -A/2$ and $\partial_x u = -B$, where $B^2 \le A$, so $u$ is a classical subsolution of $\partial_t u+\frac12(\partial_x u)^2 \le 0$. Integrating along a straight segment gives Guerra's sum rule, and dropping its remainder makes $u(0,\cdot)$ and $u(t,\cdot)$ an admissible pair for the dual Kantorovich problem with quadratic cost. For the Curie--Weiss model and $t > 0$, $T_t(y) = y-t\tanh y$ is an optimal transport map from every source with finite first moment if and only if $t \le 1$, and the Kantorovich potentials are the limiting pressures. For the replica-symmetric Sherrington--Kirkpatrick model, the cavity map is injective on the physical half-line and the curvature of its Brenier potential is the longitudinal eigenvalue, which exceeds the replicon eigenvalue $Λ_{\mathrm{AT}}$: transport of Dirac masses does not detect the de Almeida--Thouless line. The replicon appears along the $\mathcal{W}_2$ geodesic that splits a Dirac mass into two atoms, as the second variation of a second-order surrogate of the two-atom Parisi functional. From a Dirac initial datum, Guerra's $K$-step bound takes Hopf--Lax form, and the Parisi formula becomes a Hopf--Lax formula over atomic measures. With a $\mathcal{W}_1$-Lipschitz bound for its initial datum, proved by comparing Cole--Hopf layers, we let $K\to\infty$ and recover at Dirac data the Hopf--Lax form of the Parisi formula due to Mourrat and to Mourrat and Panchenko, with a rate for equal-mass approximations.

items.title: The BCC Lattice Maximizes the First Positive Neumann Eigenvalue among 3D Lattice Voronoi Cells
items.summary: It is shown that, among three-dimensional lattices of fixed covolume, the body-centered cubic lattice maximizes the first positive Neumann eigenvalue of its Voronoi cell uniquely, up to orthogonal transformations.

items.title: Normalized ground state solutions to the nonlinear Born--Infeld problem
items.summary: We study normalized solutions to the Born--Infeld problem \begin{equation*} -{\rm div}\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right)+μu=f(u)\ \hbox{ in }\mathbb{R}^N,\qquad \int_{\mathbb{R}^N}|u|^2\,dx=2m^2, \end{equation*} $N\ge3$, where $m>0$ is prescribed and $μ>0$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplier. The nonlinearity $f$ is assumed to be superlinear at infinity, with no upper restriction on its growth, and to behave like $|s|^{p-2}s$ near zero, with $2<p<2^*$. Following a Lagrangian approach, we relate the action ground state level $a(μ)$ of the prescribed frequency problem to the masses of its ground states by means of one-sided derivative formulas, which lead to the existence of normalized solutions. A distinctive feature of the Born--Infeld operator is that the gradient constraint makes the energy bounded from below on every mass sphere, even in the $L^2$-supercritical case. For $2+4/N\le p<2^*$ we obtain a threshold $c_*>0$ such that normalized action ground states exist for $m^2>c_*$, and none exist for $m^2<c_*$. In the $L^2$-subcritical case they exist for every $m^2>0$. We prove that every action ground state has constant sign and is radial up to a translation.

items.title: The roads taken in the directed landscape
items.summary: Every finite-length path in the directed landscape spends almost all of its time on geodesics. More precisely, let G be the union of the interiors of all geodesics. We prove that, almost surely, every path of finite landscape length lies in G outside a set of times of Hausdorff dimension at most 57/61. We also construct finite-length paths whose exceptional set has dimension at least 1/3. The proof combines quantitative bounds on nearly optimal detours, stochastic domination of the environment outside a geodesic, and a three-geodesic disjointness estimate.

items.title: Quadratic APN Functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with a Self-Equivalence of Prime Order
items.summary: Almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ have the lowest possible differential uniformity. The only known APN permutation in even dimension, in dimension six, is equivalent to a quadratic APN function with a nontrivial linear self-equivalence; no APN permutation is known for even $n \geq 8$. In a published collection of about 3.8 million quadratic APN classes of dimension eight, at most 0.34% have a nontrivial linear self-equivalence. In dimension ten, the 25 literature classes considered here all have one. We study all quadratic APN functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with such a self-equivalence, which usually confines them to a much smaller linear space. Up to conjugacy and power similarity, self-equivalences of prime order have 299 types. We settle 298 of them. Elementary lemmas exclude 280 types, and exhaustive searches confirm this for 242 of them. The other 18 types are settled by exhaustive searches with exact equivalence certificates. Up to extended affine equivalence, the 298 types contain 29 classes of quadratic APN functions, four of them new. This also classifies the quadratic APN functions with coefficients in a subfield. Exactly 24 classes contain one with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_4$, and all 3 that contain one with coefficients in $\mathbb{F}_{32}$ are among them. The open type consists of the quadratic canonical triplicate functions. They correspond to maximum additive Hermitian rank-distance codes. Three different searches find only the invariants of 16 classes, all among the 29. We conjecture there are no others. No quadratic APN function in the 298 settled types is Carlet-Charpin-Zinoviev equivalent to a permutation.

items.title: Linear Response for Bernoulli Convolutions
items.summary: Let $μ_λ$ be the Bernoulli convolution measure with parameter $λ\in(0,1)$. We study the regularity of the function %We prove that $h=h_φ:λ\mapsto \int_{\mathbb{R}}φ(x)\,dμ_λ(x)$ for Hölder observables $φ$. We describe sufficient conditions for both smoothness and non smoothness of this function. In particular, we show that for almost every function with respect to certain Wiener like measures on $C[0,1]$, $h_φ$ exhibits a phase transition: it is almost nowhere differentiable for small $λ$ and it is almost everywhere differentiable for large $λ.$

items.title: The Moduli of Canonical Threefolds of Minimum Volume
items.summary: We determine the moduli space of complex projective canonical threefolds of volume $1/420$. It consists of an irreducible rational component of dimension $33$ and two isolated points, represented by the explicitly constructed rigid threefolds Vega and Altair.

items.title: Squared Bessel particle systems with weak repulsion
items.summary: We study squared Bessel particle systems with repulsion parameter $κ>0$ and dimension parameter $δ\in\mathbb R$. We prove that the singular equation has a unique global strong solution for every initial state in the closed Weyl chamber, including states with coinciding particles. The solutions have locally integrable interaction terms and spend zero Lebesgue time at pairwise collisions. We also consider the equation in which the interaction terms are set to zero at collisions. At certain integer values of $δ$, this equation admits infinitely many solution laws from suitable initial configurations. In these solutions, a block of particles can remain at zero for any prescribed time before being released. For positive initial states, we determine when zero is reached and when particles enter the negative half-line. From distinct initial positions, collisions occur almost surely for $0<κ<1$ and do not occur for $κ\ge1$. Collisions of three or more particles are excluded away from zero. We give an example of a triple collision at zero. We obtain two-sided bounds for the tails of the first-zero and first-collision times. The bounds give matching powers for the first-zero time when it is finite, and for the first-collision time in nonnegative systems when $0<κ<1$.

items.title: Quantitative high-contrast homogenisation of composite media with highly anisotropic fibres
items.summary: This work concerns a non-uniformly elliptic second-order differential operator with periodic coefficients that describes a composite medium formed by a periodic array of highly anisotropic cylindrical fibres set in an isotropic matrix. The ratio of transverse to axial conductivity in the fibres is linked to the period of the coefficients through a `critical' high-contrast scaling, and the axial conductivity is allowed to vary along the fibres. As the period $\varepsilon$ tends to zero, ellipticity degenerates in the directions transverse to the fibres. We are concerned with the resolvent of this operator in the small-$\varepsilon$ limit. For fibres with constant axial conductivity, the two-scale limit of such problems was identified by Cherednichenko, Smyshlyaev and Zhikov (Proceedings of the Royal Society of Edinburgh: Section A Mathematics 136(1), 87--114 (2006)), and a full two-scale asymptotic expansion, with remainder estimates for smooth right-hand sides, was constructed by Cherednichenko (Asymptotic Analysis 49(1--2), 39--59 (2006)). In the non-constant axial conductivity setting, considered here, we approximate the resolvent in terms of the two-scale limit operator and prove that the error is order $\varepsilon$ in the operator norm, uniformly over right-hand sides in the unit ball of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$; we also obtain order-$\varepsilon$ estimates for the reciprocals of the spectral band functions. This work builds on results announced, without proof, for fibres with circular cross-section in Cooper and Kamotski (Direct and Inverse Problems with Applications: Extended Abstracts of the 2024 GAP Center Summer School, pp.~69--75, Birkhäuser (2026)).

items.title: Cover times of random recursive trees and linear preferential attachment trees
items.summary: We study the cover times of uniform random recursive trees and linear preferential attachment trees, including the negative-parameter models corresponding to random $d$-ary increasing trees. We prove explicit limits in probability and expectation when the cover times are rescaled by $n (\log n)^2$. In particular, for the uniform random recursive tree the cover time is close to $e n (\log n)^2$ with high probability.

items.title: Online Switching Control as Learning with Experts
items.summary: This paper addresses the problem of online switching control for discrete-time nonlinear systems where a controller is sequentially selected from a finite set of candidates. The goal is to generate an adaptive sequence of controllers to minimize the cumulative cost under unknown disturbances and cost functions. Specifically, we consider a full-information feedback setting where realized disturbance effects and cost functions are available after each selection. Using counterfactual costs computed from historical data, we reduce the online switching control problem to the experts problem with switching costs. Then, we propose an adaptive switching algorithm based on the Hedge algorithm with a switching suppression mechanism. Notably, the proposed algorithm achieves an expected regret of $O(\sqrt{T\log N})$, where $T$ is the time horizon and $N$ is the number of candidate controllers, while ensuring uniform boundedness of the state. This matches the optimal regret order for the standard experts problem.

items.title: A Parametric Active-Set Algorithm for Solving Monotone Generalized Nash Equilibrium Problems
items.summary: We present a fast active-set algorithm for the solution of monotone linear-quadratic generalized Nash equilibrium problems (GNEPs) with shared affine inequality and equality constraints. The algorithm, which we call gPAQ, is an adaptation of the parametric active-set method proposed by Best (1996) and extended in qpOASES by Ferreau et al. (2014) to solve convex quadratic programs. Under strong monotonicity, we show that the same active-set strategy applies. We handle the case of merely monotone problems by using gPAQ as the inner solver within proximal-point iterations. To solve strongly monotone convex nonlinear GNEPs, we propose a Newton-type iterative scheme, which we call gPAN, which iteratively linearizes the nonlinear problem and solves the resulting LQ-GNEP subproblems using gPAQ. We show in numerical examples that the proposed algorithms are significantly faster than existing methods.

items.title: Cohomology and Deformation of Leibniz Superalgebras
items.summary: In this article, we give a characterization of Leibniz superalgebras. We study cohomology theory of Leibniz superalgebras. Using the cohomology we study the formal deformation theory of Leibniz superalgebras. We do some cohomology computation in lower dimensions. We establish a one to one correspondence between extensions of a Leibniz superalgebra and its cohomology group in dimension 2.

items.title: Rational Solutions of Abel Differential Equations
items.summary: We study the rational solutions of the Abel equation $x'=A(t)x^3+B(t)x^2$ where $A$ and $B \in \mathbb{C}[t]$. We prove that if $°(A)$ is even or $°(B)>(°(A)-1)/2$ then the equation has at most two rational solutions. For any other case, an upper bound on the number of rational solutions is obtained. Moreover, we prove that if there are more than $(°(A)+1)/2$ rational solutions then the equation admits a Darboux first integral.

items.title: Quantifying Dependence Effects on $k$-out-of-$n$ Reliability Relative to the Independent Benchmark
items.summary: Understanding how dependence among component lifetimes affects the reliability of redundant systems is a central problem in reliability engineering. In this paper, we develop a framework for quantifying the impact of multivariate dependence on $k$-out-of-$n$ system reliability relative to the independent benchmark. Using an orthogonal Legendre expansion of the copula density, we derive an exact decomposition that separates the dependence structure from the system architecture. This representation identifies how individual dependence contributions are transmitted to system reliability through explicit structural weights. An application to multivariate Farlie-Gumbel-Morgenstern copulas demonstrates that higher-order dependence can produce distinct reliability effects even when all bivariate copulas remain unchanged. Our findings provide a systematic approach to quantifying and interpreting the effects of multivariate dependence on the reliability of redundant systems.

items.title: Smooth plane curves with a unique outer Galois point and their automorphism groups
items.summary: We consider smooth plane curves $\mathcal{X}$ of degree $d\geq4$, defined over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $0$, that possess a unique outer Galois point. This geometric condition forces the curve to be a cyclic covering of the projective line, and ensures that its automorphism group fits into a specific theoretical framework. For each possible non-cyclic reduced automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}_{\operatorname{red}}(\mathcal{X})$, we fully characterize the defining equation of $\mathcal{X}$ and the precise structure of its full automorphism group $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathcal{X})$. This comprehensive analysis not only identifies the exact form of the equation for each automorphism type but also establishes the detailed criteria under which these scenarios can occur, thereby offering a complete classification of defining equations for smooth plane curves with a unique outer Galois point and a non-cyclic reduced automorphism group.

items.title: Tilting theory on continuous quivers (I) maximal rigid and tilting subcategories
items.summary: Let $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$ be the category of finitely generated persistence modules on the interval $\mathbb I\subseteq\mathbb R$. We study the maximal rigid subcategories of $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$. Maximal rigid interval consistent subcategories are classified via tilting modules over the corresponding discrete type $A$ quiver. We compare several related notions, (weak) tilting and maximal rigidity, in both the context of hereditary abelian categories with enough projective objects and $\mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$ and prove that every maximal rigid interval consistent subcategory is weak tilting and every maximal rigid consistent below subcategory is tilting. In addition, any maximal rigid subcategory $\mathbf T\subseteq \mathrm{rep}(\mathbb I)$, not necessarily being interval consistent, satisfies $\mathbf T^{\perp_1}=\mathop {Gen}(\mathbf T)$. We also establish a continuous analogue of Ingalls-Thomas's bijection by showing a bijection between integrally supported maximal rigid consistent below subcategories and integrally generated torsion classes.

items.title: Enumeration of Cospectral Graphs with Respect to the Average Flow Matrix
items.summary: A graph is said to be determined by the spectrum of a graph-associated matrix if no nonisomorphic graph shares the same spectrum with it. In this paper, we introduce the average flow matrix of a connected graph and study its spectral properties. We investigate its effectiveness in distinguishing graphs by carrying out a computational enumeration of connected graphs having a cospectral mate with respect to this matrix up to order 10. Our computations show that every connected graph on at most 10 vertices is determined by the spectrum of the average flow matrix. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first graph-associated matrix for which the spectrum distinguishes all connected graphs of order at most 10.

items.title: The Column-Diamond Resolution over Quadratic Monomial Rings
items.summary: We study infinite minimal free resolutions of modules $M = R/(x_{i_1},\ldots,x_{i_m})$ over quadratic monomial rings $R = k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]/I$. We introduce the Column-Diamond construction, a recursive diagrammatic procedure that builds an explicit free resolution of $M$ from columns and diamonds determined by the quadratic generators of $I$. We prove that this resolution is exact and minimal. As an application, the Betti numbers of $M$ are counted by valid words in a graph associated to $I$, which yields a combinatorial rational formula for the Poincaré series.

items.title: The variety of $2$-dimensional algebras over an algebraically closed field
items.summary: The work is devoted to the variety of $2$-dimensional algebras over an algebraically closed field. Firstly, we classify such algebras modulo isomorphism. Then we describe the degenerations and the closures of principal algebra series in the variety under consideration. Finally, we apply our results to obtain analogous descriptions for the subvarieties of flexible and bicommutative algebras. In particular, we describe rigid algebras and irreducible components for these subvarieties.

items.title: Regularity of critical immersions for scale-invariant curvature energies in even dimensions
items.summary: For immersions of a closed $2h$-dimensional manifold $Σ$ into $\mathbb R^m$, we consider curvature energies that are invariant under ambient isometries and dilations, with the principal term $\int_Σ \big|\nabla^{(h-1)} \vec{\mathrm{I\!I}}\big|_g^2\,d\text{vol}_g$ and lower-order submanifold invariants. Following the four-dimensional approach developed in joint work with Bernard, Martino, and Rivière, we prove that every weak critical immersion in the natural Sobolev class $W^{h+1,2}$, whose induced metric and its inverse have $L^\infty$ coefficients, is real-analytic in harmonic coordinates. The proof combines geometric conservation laws, structural identities, and elliptic estimates with critical Sobolev coefficients to obtain Morrey decay and bootstrap to full regularity.

items.title: Optimal MM* bounds for convex bodies
items.summary: Let $K\subset\R^n$ be a convex body in isotropic position. We prove the optimal mean-width estimate \[ M^*(K)\leq C\sqrt{n\log n}. \] The main new ingredient is a geometric inequality relating the Gaussian mean of the support function to its mean under the uniform measure on $K$, obtained through a heat-flow argument. Combined with the Gaussian-log-concave comparison of Eldan and Lehec and the newly available dimension-free bound on the third-moment parameter $κ_n$, this yields the result. The boundedness of $κ_n$ also makes the mean-norm estimate of Bizeul and Klartag sharp. Combining both estimates yields \[ M(K)M^*(K)\leq C\log n, \] extending Pisier's $MM^*$ estimate to non-symmetric convex bodies and to the isotropic position.

items.title: Logics vs doctrines, a mirror symmetry
items.summary: We study the relationship between doctrines, encoding 2-categories of theories in predicate logic, and fragments of geometric logic, defined through Kan injectivity in the 2-category of topoi. After a brief historical account of the notion of doctrine, we propose our working definition. Our main result then establishes a Galois connection between doctrines and subgeometric logics. This connection suggests a mirror symmetry between the world of doctrines and the world of logics, in which constructions and results on either side admit counterparts on the other. We develop this symmetry through constructions of syntactic categories and classifying topoi in both settings, recovering the familiar examples from categorical logic. We prove paired Diaconescu-type theorems and give symmetric descriptions of the two closure operators induced by the Galois connection. Finally, we characterise when passing from a doctrine to its closure induces a reflection between the corresponding 2-categories of algebras, and we relate this reflection to conceptual completeness.

items.title: Matrix ultraproducts have trivial fundamental group
items.summary: We prove that every tracial ultraproduct $\prod_{\mathcal{U}} M_n(\mathbb{C})$ of matrix algebras has trivial fundamental group. In particular, this establishes that there are uncountably many nonisomorphic matrix ultraproducts, answering a question of Sorin Popa. We actually prove the stronger result that every matrix ultraproduct has trivial first-order fundamental group and thus our techniques are model-theoretic in nature.

items.title: On Borwein polynomials with multiple roots outside the unit disk
items.summary: A Borwein polynomial has coefficients in ${-1,0,1}$ and nonzero constant and leading coefficients. We seek Borwein polynomials having a multiple root outside the unit disk. To this end, we consider the powers $L^2$ and $L^3$ of Lehmer's polynomial $L$, which has a real root $τ>1$. Since $L$ has exceptionally small Mahler measure, the theorem of Bombieri and Vaaler guarantees the existence of Borwein multiples of these powers. Such multiples have $τ$ as a root of multiplicity at least 2 and 3, respectively. Mossinghoff (2003, Algorithm 3, p. 323) constructed examples that, under the substitution $x\mapsto -x$, yield such multiples. The main contribution of this paper is to determine the least possible degrees of Borwein multiples of $L^2$ and $L^3$, with and without symmetry restrictions on their coefficients, and to describe their degree spectra. For $L^2$, the minimum degree is 34 without symmetry restrictions, 38 among self-reciprocal multiples, and 41 among antireciprocal multiples. For $L^3$, the corresponding minimum degrees are 115, 115, and 117. We determine the complete degree spectra for $L^2$ and, for $L^3$, classify the degrees from 115 to 150 for which self-reciprocal or antireciprocal Borwein multiples exist, giving an explicit example for each admissible degree in each symmetry class. Further constructions yield Borwein multiples of $L^3$ in every degree $D\geq 215$, with both symmetry types for every $D\geq 231$.

items.title: Sturm-Liouville problems on graphs with Robin boundary conditions
items.summary: We study characteristic functions and describe asymptotics of the eigenvalues for the spectral Sturm-Liouville problem on graphs equipped with Robin-Kirhhoff boundary conditions. Also, we show how to recover the coefficients in the Robin conditions for the quantum graphs provided the shape of the graphs and some Robin eigenvalues are known.

items.title: Boundary Behavior of Bisectional Curvatures for Weighted Bergman Metrics
items.summary: This paper investigates the asymptotic boundary behavior of the holomorphic bisectional curvature for weighted Bergman metrics. By characterizing extremal functions via $L^2$-orthogonal projections, we establish an explicit formula for the weighted bisectional curvature. Utilizing the squeezing function, we then obtain quantitative upper and lower bounds for the curvature on bounded pseudoconvex domains. Furthermore, we prove that at strongly pseudoconvex boundary points, the bisectional curvature asymptotically coincides with that of the unit ball. As an application, these results provide a streamlined and unified proof for the known asymptotic behavior of the bisectional curvature of the Kähler-Einstein metric.

items.title: All coupling Anderson localization in the quantum kicked rotor model
items.summary: In this paper, we study $$\mathscr{H}=λΔ+\tanπ(θ+n^2α)δ_{n,n'},\ n\in\Bbb Z$$ and prove its Anderson localization for all $λ>0$ and Lebesgue almost every (a.e.) $(α, θ)\in\Bbb T^2$. This conforms in the full measure sense the main assumption of Fishman-Grempel-Prange [{\it Phys. Rev. Lett.} 49(8), 509--512 (1982)] in the study of the quantum suppression of chaos: The pseudo-randomness of the sequence $\{\tanπ(θ+n^2α)\}_{n\in\Bbb Z}$ (for $α\in\Bbb T\setminus \Bbb Q$) should result in all coupling Anderson localization for $H$ similar to that for the one-dimensional Anderson model. Our proof is based on nonperturbative Green's function estimates approach using Cayley transform, quadratic Weyl sum estimate and Rellich function analysis.

items.title: Non-abelian Hodge correspondence for semistable parabolic connections on curves in positive characteristic
items.summary: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. We establish a non-abelian Hodge correspondence between semistable parabolic connections on $C$ and semistable parabolic Higgs bundles on its Frobenius twist $C'$, allowing arbitrary prescribed residue eigenvalues, parabolic weights and filtration types. The relationship between the parabolic weights and residue eigenvalues on the two sides is encoded in a table analogous to Simpson's table. We obtain this result by extending the notion of "very good regular connections" to incorporate a residue-dependent degree condition, and by developing a Cartier descent formalism for parabolic connections. Working with filtered sheaves, we obtain a particularly clean description of this Cartier descent formalism that potentially extends to higher dimensional varieties.

items.title: Hierarchical Interactions in Mobility Networks: A Model-Free Feedback Approach
items.summary: Urban mobility systems are large-scale networked systems whose performance emerges from hierarchically coupled decisions of public authorities, competing mobility operators, and travelers. Existing approaches to policy design either collapse one of these levels or assume that the authority can model and differentiate through the equilibrium responses of operators and travelers. In this paper, we model policy design as a tri-level game on a multimodal network, in which a municipality sets taxes, licenses, and integration subsidies, a public transport and a taxi operator compete on prices and service supply, and heterogeneous travelers reach a stochastic user equilibrium. We prove that the traveler equilibrium is unique and continuously differentiable in the operator strategies, that the variational inequality characterizing operator equilibria admits a solution for every policy, and that the resulting tri-level game admits a Stackelberg equilibrium. Building on this structure, we design a model-free hierarchical controller in which the municipality and the operators update their decisions from zeroth-order evaluations of observed equilibrium outcomes. On the Zurich multimodal network, operator equilibria computed from different initializations differ by a median of 0.3% in the municipal objective. On a grid of 3,125 policies, only those that subsidize transfers between public transport and taxis benefit both operators, and 24 of them also lower travel costs without degrading the municipal objective. Finally, the controller matches the best policies of three black-box optimizers and terminates at the most consistent policies across runs.

items.title: Nuclear dimension of uniform Roe algebras
items.summary: We prove that for every discrete metric space $X$ of bounded geometry with Yu's Property A, the uniform Roe algebra $C^*_u(X)$ has nuclear dimension at most one. This answers in the negative a long-standing question of Winter and Zacharias on whether the nuclear dimension of $C^*_u(X)$ always equals the asymptotic dimension of $X$. Consequently, $dim_{nuc} C^*_u(X)\in\{0,1,\infty\}$ for every discrete metric space $X$, with or without bounded geometry.

items.title: Finding accurate eigenvalues and eigenvectors of positive semi-definite matrices given a subspace
items.summary: We revisit a classical problem in numerical linear algebra: given a $k$-dimensional subspace $\mathcal{Q}$ with orthonormal basis $Q$ that approximates the leading eigenspace of an $n\times n$ positive semi-definite matrix $A$, the goal is to extract high-accuracy eigenvalues. The Rayleigh-Ritz (RR) method is the standard algorithm for the task, which has been shown to be optimal in several ways (when $A$ is symmetric, not necessarily positive semi-definite $A\succeq 0$). In this paper, we show that when $A\succeq 0$, alternative methods can outperform RR, including Nystr{ö}m and one-sided projected SVD, while having the same computational complexity; that is, the main cost is in computing $AQ$, plus an $O(nk^2)$ term. In particular, we advocate the use of Nystr{ö}m's method, quantitatively showing that the approximate leading eigenvalues have better accuracy than RR, and the improvement can be arbitrarily large. The significant accuracy improvement occurs for the first $i$ eigenvalues if $λ_i \gg λ_{k+1}$ and uniformly for all $k$ eigenvalues if $λ_k \gg λ_{k+1}$. This theoretical observation can be extended to the case where we extract $k$ leading eigenvalues from a larger-dimensional subspace. A similar improvement is numerically observed for the purpose of approximating the leading eigenvectors. In contrast, when the target eigenvalues are the trailing ones, the situation is reversed, and the Nystr{ö}m method performs poorly; we suggest a remedy based on a shift for this situation.

items.title: Kronecker Approximations of Covariance Matrices for Solving Inverse Problems
items.summary: Inverse problems arise in many applications where the task is to recover unknown parameters from indirect or noisy observations. In contrast to forward problems, where outputs are directly computed from known inputs, inverse problems are designed to infer the underlying variables from the observed effect. Inverse problems are often ill-posed, so regularization is needed to compute reasonable solutions. One form of regularization incorporates prior knowledge about the unknown parameters in the form of prior distributions. However, in many settings, large prior covariance matrices pose computational bottlenecks for solving inverse problems. To address this, we study approximations of large covariance matrices via structured Kronecker-Toeplitz products and demonstrate how these approximations can be used to solve inverse problems. We exploit the Block-Toeplitz-Toeplitz-Block structure induced by the covariance kernel to construct compact approximations that are orders of magnitude cheaper to store and invert. These approximations are deployed as prior covariance surrogates in Bayesian inverse problems solved via generalized hybrid iterative methods. We demonstrate that the Kronecker-Toeplitz approximation attains lower relative approximation error than existing matrix approximations, exhibits rapid error decay with rank, and enables efficient matrix-vector products. Applications to 2D seismic tomography reconstruction problems illustrate the practical utility of these methods.

items.title: Syzygy matrices and higher extensions over string algebras
items.summary: Over a finite-dimensional string algebra, higher extension dimensions may eventually vanish, become periodic, or grow without bound. We show how their behaviour can be read from a finite directed graph. Second syzygies split into uniserial modules from a finite family; their syzygies define a nonnegative integer matrix, so higher extension dimensions become weighted counts of walks. Only the part of the graph relevant to the chosen pair of modules contributes. This gives four growth regimes: eventual vanishing, periodicity, quasi-polynomial growth, and exponential growth. We derive the construction from projective covers, give explicit extension formulas over truncated cycles, and illustrate the growth regimes with examples.

items.title: Composition of Near-Planar Infrastructure Network Instances with Certified Skewness Bounds
items.summary: Computational studies of optimization problems on infrastructure networks may require more suitable instances than are available. We propose a method to obtain additional instances by extracting and joining connected parts of existing networks, reusing their topology and parameters. Many infrastructure networks are near-planar, so added connections should preserve this property. We measure near-planarity by skewness, the minimum number of edges whose removal makes a graph planar.
