We derive bounds on the additional skewness caused by joining and give sufficient conditions under which none is added, and propose the corresponding strategy. We evaluate our approach on 100 sets of network parts extracted from each of PGLib-OPF and SNDlib. Within time limits, we show that no skewness is added for about half of the resulting power transmission networks and all considered telecommunication networks. Our method gives smaller mean upper bounds on added skewness than baselines that select vertices randomly, in order of decreasing degree, or using a Kamada--Kawai layout. Extraction and composition may also make the resulting optimization instances infeasible. To reduce this risk, we solve a simpler, tractable variant of the intended optimization problem during generation and restart if it is infeasible. On the generated instances, we solve security-constrained optimal transmission switching and survivable network design problems in full, demonstrating that the instances vary in computational difficulty with runtimes ranging from seconds to hours. The method thus extends the available benchmark sets with instances that inherit source data, have known skewness bounds, and cover a range of computational difficulty.

items.title: Integrated Topology and Redispatch Optimization of Real-World Power Transmission Systems using Branch-and-Benders-Cut
items.summary: Transmission system operators can reduce congestion management costs by jointly optimizing network topology, generator redispatch, and transformer settings. The large number of switching decisions, detailed operational constraints, and security requirements under outages make this problem computationally demanding. We present a full mixed-integer linear programming formulation that combines line switching, substation reconfiguration, generator commitment and redispatch, and transformer settings with operational requirements. We solve the problem using an exact branch-and-Benders-cut algorithm. We integrate specialized subproblem solution methods, subproblem selection, cut filtering, partial decomposition, and techniques for enforcing network connectivity. A sequential switching heuristic provides initial solutions for the exact solve. An extensive computational study on 130 synthetic instances demonstrates substantial reductions in solution time compared with standard Benders decomposition and shows how heuristic warmstarting improves solution quality, especially when more switching actions are allowed. Results on real transmission networks illustrate how joint topology and redispatch decisions identify effective switching actions that sequential approaches can miss. Selected solutions generated by our approach were presented to system operators and subsequently checked using alternating current power flow calculations. All seven discussed solutions passed a first operator assessment, indicating the practical potential of the integrated approach.

items.title: Arithmetical and set-theoretic semantics of the logic of problems and propositions
items.summary: Kolmogorov interpreted intuitionistic logic as a calculus of problems and later remarked that a complete treatment should deal with problems and propositions together. Melikhov's logic HC is such a joint two-sorted system: it combines classical propositions with intuitionistic problems by means of two modalities, the problem !A (``find a proof of the proposition A'') and the proposition phi (``the problem phi has a solution''). We give the language of HC a formal semantics in which the modalities are read literally: solutions of !A are proofs of A in a fixed formal theory, ?phi states that phi has a solution, and the connectives on problems are interpreted as in Kleene realizability. Three variants are studied: the arithmetical semantics I (provability in PA), its external version E (truth in the standard model), and the set-theoretic semantics B over ZF, where problem variables are ``black boxes'' and a quantifier Pi over them is available. Validity is defined as the existence of a computable uniform solution. We determine which schemes are valid, build calculi HCI, HCE, HCB sound with respect to the three semantics, and derive Lob's scheme from the fixed-point lemma inside the common core of our calculi and HC. The propositional fragments of HCI and HCE are exactly the provability logics GL and GLS; the positive modality-free fragment of valid problems is intuitionistic logic, while the full modality-free fragment lies strictly above it (Rose's formula is valid, Scott's principle is not). We compare the calculi with HC, which turns out to be incompatible with fixed points, prove independence results and list open questions.

items.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
items.summary: We study the Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem on an acute spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, the equation is \[ h\,\varphi(\ell/h)\,\barσ_k(\nabla^2h+hσ)=f, \qquad \nabla_μh=\cotθ\,h, \] where $\ell$ is the support function of the unit capillary spherical cap. For $1\le k\le n-1$, this includes the capillary Christoffel--Minkowski and capillary $L_p$ Christoffel--Minkowski problems; the same density formally recovers the capillary Orlicz--Minkowski endpoint when $k=n$. We organize the theory in five parts. After recalling the elementary symmetric functions and the capillary support-function formalism, we review the capillary Orlicz--Brunn--Minkowski framework and introduce the intermediate-order Orlicz $k$-mixed functional and its Euler--Lagrange equation. In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(t):=\frac{t\varphi'(t)}{\varphi(t)}\ge k+1+δ, \] we derive uniform $C^0$, $C^1$ and $C^2$ estimates for positive $k$-admissible solutions. The same supercritical index produces a strictly coercive second variation and a spectral gap for the linearized Neumann operator. These facts lead to existence and uniqueness by a continuity method, quantitative stability of the solution map in both the datum and the Orlicz weight, and an open perturbative class of strictly convex non-power solutions. Under an additional capillary Orlicz-convexity condition on the datum, a full-rank argument upgrades the global admissible solution to a strictly convex capillary support function.

items.title: From Butson Hadamard switching to graph switching and back
items.summary: Switching is a local operation that preserves specified properties of a combinatorial object. It has been used to derive constructions of inequivalent Hadamard matrices and nonisomorphic cospectral graphs. In this paper we investigate the relation between these constructions for real and Butson Hadamard matrices. We show that, while equivalent matrices have isomorphic associated graphs, the converse can fail for Butson matrices. We prove that a character decomposition determines the graph spectrum from the singular values of entrywise powers. For prime phase, we also observe that the spectrum depends only on the order and phase; for composite phase, a switching preserving the Butson property can change it. We show that Orrick's closed-quadruple and Hall-set switchings correspond to Wang-Qiu-Hu switching, up to graph isomorphism. Going in the other direction, we characterise when the Godsil-McKay and Wang-Qiu-Hu reflections preserve the Butson property and give phase-multiplicity conditions for the corresponding graph switchings. Finally we also relate block switching to cyclic graph switching under a phase-balance condition, automatic at prime phase. These results provide a basis for transferring tools and techniques between matrix switching and graph switching.

items.title: On the dynamics of N classical particles interacting with a complex environment
items.summary: The interactions of a particle with its environment eventually lead to the damping of its motion. This phenomenom is well understood when considering a single particle exchanging energy with the environment. The situation is definitely more complex when many particles are considered: the energy dissipation mechanisms are not clear whenever particles create a common well in which they keep interacting. In this framework, we identify the equilibrium solutions, that consist in clusters of particles at rest, and we establish their spectral stability. We show that the mean position/velocity pair is damped exponentially fast at the linearized level. Coming back to the non linear problem, we can show, at least in some simplified cases, that the dissipation mechanisms also involve far slower rates, that explain the difficulty in observing the relaxation behavior on the individual trajectories.

items.title: Transforming local positivity: from minimal valuations to irrational Seshadri constants
items.summary: We explain how a valuative Nagata type statement proposed by Dumnicki, Harbourne, Küronya, Roé and Szemberg on a polarised surface $(S, H)$ implies maximality (and hence often irrationality) of Seshadri constants on simple cyclic covers. As sample applications we show that very general degree two K3 surfaces and very general hypersurfaces in $\mathbb P^3$ of degree $6$, $8$ or $d\geq 10$ have irrational Seshadri constant at a very general point, unless $d$ is a square.

items.title: The Capillary Dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Problem
items.summary:
We study a capillary dual Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski problem on a spherical cap. For $2\le k\le n$, $1<p<k+1$, and $0<θ<π/2$, we consider \[ σ_k(
abla^2h+hσ) = f(ξ)h^{p-1} rac{ρ^{k+1}}{\varphi(ρ)}, \qquad ρ=(h^2+|
abla h|^2)^{1/2}, \] with the capillary Robin condition $
abla_μh=\cotθ\,h$. Assuming that $f$ is positive, smooth and horizontally even, $g=f^{-1/(p+k-1)}$ satisfies the capillary spherical-convexity and boundary compatibility conditions, and $H(r)=\varphi(r)/r^p$ is strictly increasing and proper with $Q_\varphi(r)\le k+1$, we prove the existence of a smooth, positive, horizontally even solution that is strictly capillary convex. The proof uses an Orlicz homotopy, uniform a priori estimates, a viscosity constant-rank argument when $k<n$, global oblique regularity, and degree theory.

items.title: Porosity in Diophantine approximation
items.summary: We provide a general framework for obtaining upper bounds on the packing dimension of certain sets arising from Diophantine approximation using the notion of porosity from geometric measure theory. In particular, the framework relies on showing that such sets are mean porous, as introduced by Koskela and Rohde (Math. Ann., 1997). As applications of our framework we show that: For $\varepsilon>0$ sufficiently small, the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing codimension comparable to $\varepsilon^{d}$ up to multiplicative constant. Any $C^{2}$ submanifold of $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ with bounded first and second partial derivatives intersected with the set of $d$-dimensional $\varepsilon$-badly approximable points has packing dimension strictly less than the dimension of the submanifold. For any matrix $A\in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ satisfying certain Diophantine conditions, the set of points that avoid the $\varepsilon \|\mathbf{q}\|_{\infty}^{-\frac{n}{m}}$-neighbourhood of the orbit $\{A\mathbf{q} \mod \mathbb{Z}^{m}:\mathbf{q} \in \mathbb{Z}^{n}\}$ has packing codimension greater than $C_{A} \varepsilon^{m}$ for $C_{A}$ a constant depending on $A$ and $m$ only. \end{itemize}

items.title: Explicit strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs using a new graph parameter
items.summary: A strong blocking set is a set of points in a finite projective space that intersects every hyperplane of the space in a spanning set of the hyperplane. These objects have been studied both in finite geometry and coding theory due to their equivalence with minimal codes. We give an explicit construction of strong blocking sets using expander graphs that improves the explicit construction of Alon et al. (Noga Alon, Anurag Bishnoi, Shagnik Das, Alessandro Neri, Strong blocking sets and minimal codes from expander graphs. Transactions of the American Mathematical Society ) by introducing a new geometrically motivated graph parameter that is better suited for this problem. Using this approach, we improve the constant $C$ in the explicit construction of a strong blocking set of size $C (q+1) k$ in the $(k - 1)$-dimensional projective space over $\mathbb{F}_q$ for every prime power $q \geq 7$.

items.title: On non-vanishing of the first Hochschild cohomology of blocks
items.summary: Let $B$ be a block of a finite group algebra $kG$, where $k$ is an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$. Inspired by the result of Fleischmann, Janiszczak and Lempken that $\mathrm{HH}^1(kG) \not=0$ when $p$ divides the order of $G$, Linckelmann conjectured that $\mathrm{HH}^1(B)\not= 0$ when $B$ has non-trivial defect. By developing the methods of Briggs, Rubio y Degrassi and the author, we give a fusion theoretic criterion for non-vanishing, proving the conjecture holds for all blocks of abelian defect. Further, we show the criterion holds for all blocks at $p > 5$, proving the conjecture for all such primes

items.title: Kobayashi-Hitchin Correspondence on Equivariant and Basic Bundles
items.summary: Let $(X,J,ω)$ be a compact complex manifold with Gauduchon metric and $G$ a Lie group acting on $X$ by holomorphic isometries. We give an explicit proof of the existence of a $G$-invariant Hermitian-Einstein metric on a $G$-polystable $G$-equivariant holomorphic vector bundle adapting the proof of Lübke-Teleman. We see that if $G$ is a connected complex Lie group with the bijective exponential map and the action of $G$ on $X$ is locally free, then our existence theorem is equivalent to the existence of a basic Hermitian-Einstein metric on a basic polystable basic holomorphic vector bundle on $X$ foliated by the foliation generated by the $G$-action. As an application, we can say that the foliated Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence on a Sasakian manifold $S$ is a $\mathbb{C}$-equivariant Kobayashi-Hitchin correspondence on the Vaisman manifold $S\times S^1$.

items.title: Eigenvalues of locally positive semidefinite matrices: Non-convexity and Geometry
items.summary: A real symmetric matrix is called $d$-locally positive semidefinite if all of its $d \times d$ principal submatrices are positive semidefinite. We investigate the spectral geometry of $d$-locally positive semidefinite matrices. The set of vectors of eigenvalues of $d$-locally positive semidefinite matrices of size $n \times n$ is fully understood and known to be convex when $d \in \{1,n-1,n\}$ \cite{blekherman2022hyperbolic}. In the smallest remaining case $n=4, d=2$, non-convexity of the set of vectors of eigenvalues was proved in \cite{kozhasov2023eigenvalues}, but even in this case the full description was unknown. We provide a basic semialgebraic description of the set of vectors of eigenvalues for $n=4, d=2$ by establishing a Fischer-type inequality for $2$-locally positive semidefinite matrices of size $4 \times 4$. We prove non-convexity for all $n \geq 4$ and $2 \leq d \leq n - 2$. For $d=2$ we prove a natural linear inequality on a linear slice of eigenvalues of locally positive semidefinite matrices which is tight at exactly two points. This gives a stronger proof of non-convexity in this case. For $d \in \{2, n - 2\}$, analyzing this slice involves solving certain non-smooth and non-convex min-max point configuration problems in the complex plane, which could be of independent interest. Similar problems were considered in \cite{nesterenko2024submatrices,sengupta2026submatrices} in the context of matrix decomposition and approximation.

items.title: Nondegeneracy of the bubble for a fourth-order Liouville boundary problem
items.summary: We establish the nondegeneracy of the bubble for \[ Δ^2u=0\quad \text{in }\mathbb R^4_+,\qquad \partial_tu=0,\quad \partial_tΔu=e^{24π^2u} \quad \text{on }\partial\mathbb R^4_+. \] Using Fourier analysis, stereographic projection and a removable-singularity argument, we classify the weighted $L^2$ boundary kernel without assuming boundedness of the boundary solution. This determines the bounded half-space kernel. Both kernels are generated by dilation and tangential translations. We further obtain sharp estimates for the projected spherical inverse.

items.title: Symplectic Cuts and Moment Polyptychs of Hypertoric Varieties
items.summary: We study compact symplectic cuts of hypertoric varieties and characterise their smoothness. When the defining arrangement has a non-empty bounded base region, the fibre-rotation action has a proper moment map and gives compact Kähler orbifold cuts at regular levels. For a smooth hypertoric manifold, an outer-chamber cut, taken above the largest critical value of this moment map, is smooth if and only if the manifold is the cotangent bundle of its distinguished compact toric subvariety; that subvariety is then a product of projective spaces, and every positive level is regular with a smooth cut. If the compact core of a smooth hypertoric manifold is reducible, every outer-chamber cut has a boundary point with non-trivial cyclic isotropy and a singular coarse local quotient, whereas every cut below the smallest positive critical value is smooth. We introduce the moment polyptych, assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and recover the residual fixed points, tangent weights, and finite local groups from its edges and labelled lattice data. Restriction to arrangement flats is compatible with cutting and supplies the lower-dimensional models used in these calculations. The resulting local data are applied to equivariant quantisation in the companion paper (arXiv:2611.14090).

items.title: Real-Space-RG for the drawups and drawdowns of run-and-tumble trajectories: universality classes for models with space-dependent velocities and switching rates
items.summary: For one-dimensional run-and-tumble processes with the two velocities $v_{\pm}(x)$ and the two switching rates $γ_{\pm}(x)$, a given stochastic trajectory is an alternating sequence of local minima and local maxima corresponding to the switching events between the ballistic motions with velocities $v_{\pm}(x) $ in the two directions. The renormalized trajectory at scale $Γ$ is obtained by keeping only the alternating sequence of local minima and local maxima that are separated by drawups and drawdowns of amplitude bigger than $Γ$. Its statistical properties can be analyzed via the generalization of the previous work arxiv:2611.04853 concerning diffusion processes involving arbitrary diffusion coefficients $D(x)$ and Ito forces $F_I(x)$. The main result is that the scale function $s(x)$ of diffusion processes that depends only on the ratio $\frac{F_I(x)}{D(x) } $ is replaced by a pair of scale functions $s_{\pm}(x)$ that depend only on the two ratios $\frac{γ_+( x ) }{v_+( x )}$ and $\frac{γ_-( x ) }{v_-( x )}$. This pair of scale functions $s_{\pm}(x)$ govern the exit probabilities from an interval and determine the universality classes of the renormalized trajectories: all run-and-tumble processes with the same two ratios $\frac{γ_+( x ) }{v_+( x )}$ and $\frac{γ_-( x ) }{v_-( x )}$ share the same statistics of renormalized trajectories. This general framework is illustrated with examples that are compared to their diffusive counterparts : uniform symmetric and asymmetric processes on the whole line $x \in]-\infty,+\infty[$, geometric process on the half-line $x \in]0,+\infty[$, and an exponential functional of the telegraph process with a normalizable steady state.

items.title: Inverse energy transfer for 2D Navier--Stokes near a self-similar vortex collapse
items.summary: We prove inverse energy transfer for the two-dimensional Navier--Stokes equations near a self-similar three-vortex collapse, confirming the 1979 prediction of Novikov and Sedov. Nonlinear interactions transfer kinetic energy from high to low frequencies over a common time interval that shrinks to the collapse time as the viscosity tends to zero. We prove that the net nonlinear transfer over this interval converges to the same positive constant across an expanding range of frequency cutoffs, with quantitative error bounds uniform in the cutoff.

items.title: On the Parameterized Complexity of Grundy Domination and Zero Forcing Problems
items.summary: We consider two different problem families that deal with domination in graphs. On the one hand, we focus on dominating sequences. In such a sequence, every vertex dominates some vertex of the graph that was not dominated by any earlier vertex in the sequence. The problem of finding the longest dominating sequence is known as $\mathsf{Grundy~Domination}$. Depending on whether the closed or the open neighborhoods are used for domination, there are three other versions of this problem: $\mathsf{Grundy~Total~Domination}$, $\mathsf{L\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$, and $\mathsf{Z\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$. We show that all four problem variants are $\mathsf{W[1]}$-complete when parameterized by the solution size. On the other hand, we consider the family of zero forcing problems which form the parametric duals of the Grundy domination problems. In these problems, one looks for the smallest set of vertices initially colored blue such that certain color change rules are able to color all other vertices blue. It has been shown that the dual of $\mathsf{Z\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$, known as $\mathsf{Zero~Forcing~Set}$, is in $\mathsf{FPT}$ when parameterized by the treewidth or the solution size. We extend the treewidth result to the other three variants of zero forcing and their respective Grundy domination problems. Our algorithm also implies an $\mathsf{FPT}$ algorithm for $\mathsf{Grundy~Domination}$ when parameterized by the number of vertices that are not in the dominating sequence. In contrast, we show that $\mathsf{L\text{-}Grundy~Domination}$ is $\mathsf{W[1]}$-hard for that parameter.

items.title: The algebraic and geometric classification of nilpotent binary Lie algebras
items.summary: The paper is devoted to give the complete algebraic classification of nilpotent binary Lie algebras of dimension $\leq 6$ over an arbitrary base field ${\mathbb{F}}$ of characteristic not $2$ and the complete geometric classification of nilpotent binary Lie algebras of dimension $6$ over $\mathbb C.$ As an application, we have the algebraic and geometric classification of nilpotent anticommutative $\mathfrak{CD}$-algebras of dimension $\leq 6.$

items.title: Atlas-DeePC: Learning Behavioral Atlases for Predictive Control
items.summary: Data-enabled Predictive Control (DeePC) uses linear combinations of recorded input-output trajectories to compute control actions without a parametric model. For nonlinear systems, these linear combinations may not satisfy the system dynamics, and the computational cost grows with dataset size. We propose Atlas-DeePC, which approximates the behavior of a dynamical system using a collection of low-dimensional subspaces, termed a behavioral atlas, to enable computationally efficient prediction and control. The atlas is constructed offline by clustering the data and fitting a subspace to each cluster. Online, the controller selects the subspace that best matches recent measurements and solves a predictive control problem parameterized by its orthonormal basis. A graph-based reference planner complements the controller by providing intermediate references across operating regions. We illustrate Atlas-DeePC on a planar robotic manipulator, where it achieves higher success rates and substantially lower online computation times than the compared controllers based on online data selection. An additional benchmark of an autonomous racing task is also included. The project website provides code and demonstrations https://dianjin-frederick.github.io/Atlas-DeePC/

items.title: The Capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski Flows
items.summary: We study a capillary Orlicz--Christoffel--Minkowski flow on a non-obtuse spherical cap for $1\le k\le n-1$: \[ \partial_t h= \frac{h^2\varphi(\ell/h)}{f}\, \barσ_k(\nabla^2h+hσ)-h, \qquad \nabla_μh=\cotθ\,h. \] In the supercritical regime \[ a_\varphi(s)=\frac{s\varphi'(s)}{\varphi(s)} \ge k+1+δ, \qquad s a_\varphi'(s)\ge0, \] we obtain time-uniform $C^0$ and $C^1$ estimates and a closed scalar equation for the speed ratio. A dynamic Orlicz square-completion identity, combined with inverse-concavity, yields a viscosity estimate for the minimum principal radius. Under a strict dynamic Orlicz-convexity condition and \[ \frac{f_μ}{f}\ge\frac{n-k}{n}\cotθ, \] we prove time-uniform two-sided principal-radius bounds on every smooth existence interval for $0<θ\leπ/2$ and deduce long-time existence and smooth convergence to a stationary solution. The boundary regularity step uses a quantitative interior concave estimate through Neumann reflection and a concave uniformly elliptic extension. Under the weaker condition $(f\ell^{k-1})_μ\ge0$, strict convexity is preserved on every smooth existence interval. For $k=1$, the transformed scalar equation is uniformly parabolic for every $0<θ<π$. Classical parabolic estimates then give an all-angle scalar flow theorem, without asserting geometric convexity preservation in the obtuse range.

items.title: Einstein contact metrics with integrable CR structure
items.summary: We prove that every compact Einstein contact metric manifold of dimension at least $5$ with integrable associated CR structure is Sasakian. We show that without the assumption of compactness this result does not hold: namely, for every odd dimension at least $5$, we construct an explicit noncompact Einstein contact metric manifold, with integrable CR-structure, which is not Sasakian.

items.title: Short quadratic exponential sums with primes in major arcs
items.summary: Using the second moment of Dirichlet $L$-functions on the critical line over the major arcs ${\mathfrak M}({\mathscr L}^b)$, with $τ=y^3x^{-1}{\mathscr L}^{-b_1}$, and excluding a small neighborhood of the centers of these arcs, i.e., those $α$ satisfying $|α-\frac{a}{q}|>(8πy^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{1-\frac{\scriptstyle1}{\scriptstyle{9-4\sqrt{2}}}}{\mathscr L}^{c_2}$, where $c_2=\frac{2A+24+(\sqrt{2}-1)b_1}{2\sqrt{2}-1}$, we obtain the estimate $$ S_2(α;x,y)=\sum_{x-y<n\le x}Λ(n)e(αn^2)\ll y\,{\mathscr L}^{-A}. $$ Moreover, in a small neighborhood of the center of the major arcs, defined by $|α-\frac{a}{q}|\le(8πy^2)^{-1}$, for $y\ge x^{\frac{\scriptstyle5}{\scriptstyle8}}{\mathscr L}^{1,5A+0,25b+18}$, an asymptotic formula with a remainder term is obtained for $S_2(α;x,y)$, where $A$, $b_1$, and $b$ are arbitrary fixed positive constants, and ${\mathscr L}=\ln xq$.

items.title: Equivariant resolution of singularities for $T$-varieties in positive characteristic
items.summary: Let the ground field be algebraically closed of positive characteristic. We prove that every variety endowed with an algebraic torus action whose general orbits have codimension at most three admits an equivariant resolution of singularities. The proof combines the description of such varieties in terms of proper polyhedral divisors and divisorial fans, the existence of log resolutions in dimension at most three, and the resolution of toroidal embeddings established by Kempf, Knudsen, Mumford and Saint-Donat.

items.title: ParetoM$^3$: Learning on the Pareto Set under Preference Guidance via Min-Max-Min Optimization
items.summary: Learning across multiple inherently conflicting objectives requires selecting desirable trade-offs from the Pareto set. In this work, we study preference-guided multi-objective optimization, where a predefined preference function is minimized over the weak Pareto set of multiple nonconvex objectives. Leveraging a merit function that vanishes on the weak Pareto set, we propose a penalty-based min-max-min formulation, termed the M$^3$ problem, which unifies preference optimization and the enforcement of weak Pareto optimality in a single objective. We further develop ParetoM$^3$, a single-loop first-order algorithm for computing stationary solutions of the resulting M$^3$ problem. Under a local Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz assumption, we prove that ParetoM$^3$ finds an $ε$-stationary point of the M$^3$ problem that is also approximately weakly Pareto optimal for the original multi-objective problem when the penalty parameter is sufficiently large, with explicit non-asymptotic convergence rates. We also show that this stationarity notion recovers existing optimality criteria, including approximate preference stationarity and approximate Karush-Kuhn-Tucker conditions, under the same assumptions used in prior works. Experiments on a synthetic benchmark, image classification, regression, and math reasoning demonstrate that ParetoM$^3$ reliably attains preferred weak Pareto optimal solutions while achieving strong practical performance. Code is available at https://github.com/tpgoodboy/ParetoM3.

items.title: What is... An Exceptional Set Estimate?
items.summary: Exceptional set estimates are a fundamental topic of interest in projection theory. We introduce the topic through discrete geometry, and use this perspective to motivate some key results in the realm of geometric measure theory. To appear in the "What is?" series in the Notices of the AMS.

items.title: Semiadditive Alternating Powers and Twisted Power Operations
items.summary: We study a class of representations of symmetric groups in higher semiadditive categories. For these representations in $\mathrm{Mod}^{\wedge}_{E_n}$, the transchromatic character of Hopkins--Kuhn--Ravenel and Stapleton is recovered as a sequence of monoidal characters on suitable categorifications, giving an explicit algorithm for its computation, and relating it to the iterated monoidal character in $(\infty,n)$-categories. These representations also give rise to notions of alternating powers and power operations in semiadditive categories, extending the classical alternating powers and $λ$-operations in $\mathrm{K}$-theory. We provide explicit computations in both the chromatic and higher categorical settings at low heights.

items.title: Group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations
items.summary: Applying the method of furcate splitting, we carry out the complete group classification of a class of generalized Korteweg-de Vries equations. This class includes the Korteweg-de Vries, modified Korteweg-de Vries and Harry Dym equations, as well as the Rosenau-Hyman compacton equations. The equivalence group of the class is computed in two independent ways, by the advanced version of the direct method and by the megaideal-based version of the algebraic method. As a by-product, we construct the automorphism group of the equivalence algebra and all its megaideals, whose number is infinite. We also find all additional point equivalences between the classification cases. The maximal Lie invariance algebras of equations from the class are of dimensions from two to five, and all the corresponding Lie-symmetry extensions are regular except those for the equations similar to the Harry Dym equation, which are singular and are the only ones of the maximal dimension five. Finally, we classify the conservation laws of equations from the class with characteristics of nonpositive order.

items.title: Supercuspidal, discrete, and elliptic densities for reductive groups over non-archimedean local fields
items.summary: Let $G$ be the group of points of a connected reductive group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of arbitrary characteristic, with residue field of size $q$. For a principal congruence tower $K_n$ attached to a Lie algebra lattice $\mathcal{L}$, the supercuspidal and discrete series proportions of the Plancherel mass of the $K_n$-fixed vectors both converge, with error $O(q^{-n/4})$, to the probability that a Haar-random form in the dual lattice $Λ=\mathcal{L}^\vee$ is elliptic. For $\mathrm{GL}_d$, the supercuspidal limit confirms a prediction of Howe. This probability is positive, and we characterize when it is one. More generally, outside a union of congruence cells of total mass $O(q^{-n/4})$, each cell determines a common Levi class for the supercuspidal and discrete series supports of every tempered representation containing its character. The limiting mass of each class is the probability that a Haar-random form in $Λ$ lies in the corresponding stratum. The proof combines finite Fourier analysis, quantitative estimates for parabolic incidence maps, and a Jacquet-module argument that detects unitary exponents.

items.title: Triadic structures in multislice networks
items.summary: Networks provide a popular representation of complex data. Often, different types of relational measurements are taken on the same subjects. Such data can be represented as a multislice network, a collection of networks on the same set of nodes, with connections between nodes of different layers. For the analysis of multislice networks, we take inspiration from the analysis of simple networks, for which small subgraphs (motifs) have proven to be useful; motifs are even seen as building blocks of complex networks. A particular instance of a motif is a triangle, and while triangle counts are well understood for simple network models such as Erdős-Rényi random graphs, with i.i.d. distributed edges, even for simple multislice network models little is known about triangle counts. Here we address this issue by extending the analysis of triadic structures to multislice Erdős-Rényi networks. Again taking inspiration from the analysis of sparse Erdős-Rényi random graphs, we show that the distribution of triangles across multiple layers in a multislice Erdős-Rényi network can be well approximated by an appropriate Poisson distribution. This theoretical result opens the door to statistical goodness of fit tests for multislice networks.

items.title: Simultaneous recovery of elastic and viscous coefficients in a Kelvin-Voigt equation
items.summary: In this paper, we study the simultaneous recovery of a spatially dependent elastic coefficient and a time- and space-dependent viscosity coefficient in a scalar Kelvin-Voigt equation. We prove that the displacement-to-traction map over any fixed time interval uniquely determines both coefficients, provided that the Riemannian metric induced by the viscosity is simple at each time. In the velocity formulation, the elastic term gives rise to a Volterra memory term involving second-order spatial derivatives, with a corresponding memory contribution to the boundary traction. We first determine all normal derivatives of both coefficients at the boundary using highly oscillatory boundary data. We then construct exact parabolic exponential solutions in the presence of memory and determine the viscosity by boundary rigidity. With the viscosity determined, an approximate identity argument reduces recovery of the elastic coefficient to injectivity of the scalar geodesic ray transform. Finally, numerical experiments illustrate a regularized finite-dimensional reconstruction of both coefficients from finitely many moments of the displacement-to-traction map.

items.title: Dimension-free Fourier restriction inequalities
items.summary: Let ${{\bf R}_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}}}(p\to q)$ denote the best constant for the $L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)\to L^q(\mathbb{S}^{d-1})$ Fourier restriction inequality to the unit sphere $\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, and let ${\bf R}_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}} (p\to q;\textrm{rad})$ denote the corresponding constant for radial functions. We investigate the asymptotic behavior of the operator norms ${{\bf R}_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}}}(p\to q)$ and ${\bf R}_{\mathbb{S}^{d-1}} (p\to q;\textrm{rad})$ as the dimension $d$ tends to infinity. We further establish a dimension-free endpoint Stein-Tomas inequality for radial functions, together with the corresponding estimate for general functions which we prove with an $O(d^{1/2})$ dependence. Our methods rely on a uniform two-sided refinement of Stempak's asymptotic $L^p$ estimate of Bessel functions.

items.title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
items.summary: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent. Moreover, the expectation values of such links are determined by their Milnor invariants. We also study the properties of Chern-Simons theories with nilpotent Lie groups and draw parallels with those of the Dijkgraaf-Witten theories. Finally, we conjecture, using the Lazard correspondence, a relation between expectation values of line operators in the two types of theories, and test it in examples.

items.title: Optimal polynomial decay and nonlinear stabilization for an indirectly damped wave-MGT system
items.summary: We study a conservative wave equation coupled to a dissipative Moore--Gibson--Thompson equation by a zero-order interaction that is symmetric in augmented variables. A general modal proposition relates the exact resolvent and semigroup asymptotic constants through an asymptotically unitary diagonalization. Its application to this system yields the optimal fourth-order resolvent estimate and the exact linear decay constants. These estimates lead to nonlinear stabilization from small regular initial data. On smooth bounded domains, a weighted composition estimate that accommodates a singular third derivative of the source at zero gives the optimal state rate $t^{-3/4}$ and energy rate $t^{-3/2}$ for power and logarithmic sources. In dimension three, the result includes $f(u)=|u|^q u$ with $3/2<q<2$ and $f(u)=|u|^{γ-2}u\log|u|$ with $7/2<γ<4$, within the source ranges of the companion general-source theory. Dimension-dependent extensions hold through dimension seven in the same data space, and in arbitrary dimension with higher regularity and a higher order of vanishing at zero. A lower-regularity graph-norm theorem and a conditional transfer theorem for general sources are also proved. Each nonlinear small-data decay exponent is optimal among uniform estimates with the stated dependence on the initial-data norm.

items.title: Periodic orbits of quadratic polynomials of periods six and seven
items.summary: The dynamics of quadratic polynomials is commonly studied by using the family of maps f_{c}(x) = x^{2} + c, where c include C. In this paper we form equations of periodic orbits of periods six and seven on a new (u,v)-plane and consider also the corresponding equations on the (x,y)-plane. The new (u,v)-model produces equations for the periods six and seven with significantly lower degree than the ones obtained by the previous models which enables us to find their solutions.

items.title: Prescribed-Vertex Rainbow Cycle Spectra in Graph Systems under a Local Ore Condition
items.summary: Let $\GraphSys=(G_1,\ldots,G_n)$ be a system of graphs on a common $n$-vertex set, put $δ(v)=\min_i d_{G_i}(v)$ and $E_\cap=\bigcap_i E(G_i)$, and write $d^c$ for rainbow distance. Assume that each $G_i$ is $2$-connected and that $d^c(u,v)\le2$ and $δ(u)+δ(v)<n$ imply $uv\in E_\cap$. We prove that either every prescribed vertex belongs to a rainbow cycle of every length $4,\ldots,n$, or all members coincide with the balanced complete bipartite graph. The non-exceptional systems are also rainbow pancyclic. Under the stronger local cutoff $4n/3-1$, every vertex additionally lies on a rainbow triangle, yielding rainbow vertex-pancyclicity; the cutoff is sharp in the stated congruence class. The proofs use prescribed-color detours, root-preserving neighborhood separation, and a rigidity theorem for missing rooted lengths.

items.title: The Leibniz adjunction in homotopy type theory, with an application to simplicial type theory
items.summary: Simplicial type theory extends homotopy type theory and equips types with a notion of directed morphisms. A Segal type is defined to be a type in which these directed morphisms can be composed. We show that all higher coherences can be stated and derived if simplicial type theory is taken to be homotopy type theory with a postulated interval type. In technical terms, this means that if a type has unique fillers for $(2,1)$-horns, it has unique fillers for all inner $(n,k)$-horns. This generalizes a result of Riehl and Shulman for the case $n = 3, k \in \{1, 2\}$. Our main technical tool is the Leibniz adjunction: the pushout-product is left adjoint to the pullback-hom in the wild category of types. While this adjunction is well known for ordinary categories, it is much more involved for higher categories, and the fact that it can be proved for the wild category of types (a higher category without stated higher coherences) is non-trivial. We make profitable use of the equivalence between the wild category of maps and that of families. We have formalized the results in Cubical Agda.

items.title: Causal and conditional tail coefficients: asymptotics, inference and graph recovery
items.summary: The causal tail coefficient (CTC) measures the influence of an extreme value of one variable on another variable and has been proposed as a tool for causal discovery in heavy-tailed models. Despite its popularity, the asymptotic behavior of its empirical counterpart has not been well understood. We develop an asymptotic theory for the rank-based CTC estimator with an intermediate threshold under nonparametric conditions that are satisfied by all standard copula models. A key observation is that the CTC is determined by the mean of a conditional tail limit distribution, which clarifies its interpretation and determines the asymptotic variance of the estimator. We establish joint asymptotic normality for the entire CTC matrix and prove consistency of a multiplier bootstrap for simultaneous inference. For heavy-tailed linear and recursive max-linear structural equation models, we show that the CTC equals one if and only if the first variable is an ancestor of the second, which leads to confidence graphs for the ancestral graph with asymptotic coverage guarantees. All results extend to general conditional tail coefficients, defined as further functionals of the conditional tail limit distribution. A simulation study and an application to dietary intake data illustrate the methods.

items.title: Motivic Invariants of Automorphisms and the Plane Cremona Group
items.summary: Recent work of Campbell and Zakharevich studies the $K$-theory spectrum of varieties. In previous work, the second author constructs a derived version of the $\mathbb{A}^1$-Euler characteristic, giving a map out of this spectrum. We analyse the morphism that the derived $\mathbb{A}^1$-Euler characteristic induces out of $K_1(\mathrm{Var}_k)$. We obtain an explicit description of this map, which encodes information about automorphisms of varieties. We use Hermitian $K$-theory to obtain a geometric description for part of this morphism in terms of Hodge cohomology. This allows us to obtain structural results about the group $K_1(\mathrm{Var}_k)$. As an application, we use the $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$-equivariant minimal model programme for surfaces to construct an arithmetic invariant of a large class of involutions in the plane Cremona group. We use this to construct two non-conjugate de Jonquières involutions with isomorphic positive genus fixed curves over any perfect field $k$ of characteristic not $2$ with at least 6 elements which admits a quadratic extension.

items.title: Neyman Orthogonalized Specification Tests for Conditional Tail Index Models
items.summary: We develop specification tests for parametric conditional tail index models of heavy-tailed distributions. The tests are based on a projected empirical process that removes the first-order effect of estimating the null parameter. Within the conditional Hall class, we identify conditions under which projection also eliminates the leading Pareto approximation bias in the test process, permitting lower thresholds while preserving asymptotically correct size. We establish the validity of the tests via multiplier bootstrap and characterize power against fixed and local alternatives. For log-linear models, bootstrap validity extends to settings in which covariates of observations above a common threshold concentrate and the smallest eigenvalue of the information matrix tends to zero. We further propose a novel threshold selection rule based on an estimate of the Pareto approximation bias after projection. The rule uses the estimated bias to determine whether a reference threshold can be lowered to retain more observations, with potential gains in power. The finite sample performance of the tests is examined through simulations and a real data application.

items.title: The Chabauty--Kim dimension inequality via noncommutative Iwasawa theory
items.summary: We establish Kim's conjectural dimension inequality for smooth projective geometrically connected curves $C/\mathbb{Q}$ of genus at least two with a rational basepoint. For every odd prime $p$ of good reduction, we prove that $$\mathrm{dim} H_f^1(G_{\mathbb{Q},Σ},U_n^\mathrm{ét}) < \mathrm{dim}(U_n^{\mathrm{dR}}/F^0)$$ for all sufficiently large $n$, where $U_n^\mathrm{ét}$ and $U_n^\mathrm{dR}$ are the $n$'th lower central series truncations of the $\mathbb{Q}_p$-pro-unipotent geometric étale, and de Rham fundamental groups of $C$, and $Σ$ is any finite set of places containing $p$, $\infty$, and the primes of bad reduction. Inspired by Coates and Kim's work on curves with CM Jacobians, we use noncommutative Iwasawa theory to bound second Galois cohomology through dimensions of kernels of certain Iwasawa operators, acting on finite dimensional representations of the ambient generalized symplectic group. We establish bounds for these kernels in terms of the highest weight and dimension of the ambient symplectic representation. No restriction is imposed on the Jacobian's geometric endomorphism ring or its Tate-module Galois image. Consequently, the Chabauty--Kim loci are finite at all sufficiently large levels, recovering the Mordell theorem over $\mathbb{Q}$ through the Chabauty--Kim method.

items.title: On weakly m-convex sets, m=1,...,n-1, in n-dimensional Euclidean spaces
items.summary: We study general topological properties of open and closed weakly $m$-convex sets, $m=1,\ldots, n-1$, in the real $n$-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geqslant2$. An open set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is called weakly $m$-convex if, through every boundary point of the set, there passes an $m$-dimensional plane that does not intersect the set. A closed set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is weakly $m$-convex if it can be approximated from the outside by a countably decreasing family of open weakly $m$-convex sets. The set of all points in the complement of a given subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ through each of which every $m$-dimensional plane intersects the subset is called the $m$-nonconvexity-point set corresponding to the given subset. We prove that the nonempty $m$-nonconvexity-point set corresponding to an open weakly $m$-convex set is itself open and weakly $m$-convex, and that the interior of every closed weakly $m$-convex set with nonempty interior is weakly $m$-convex for every $m=1,\ldots, n-1$.

items.title: Frobenius and perfection in framed motives
items.summary: We develop explicit Frobenius and perfection arguments for framed motives over imperfect fields. In positive characteristic, power framing homotopies and local framed transfers make relative Frobenius invertible after inverting the characteristic. Descent through successive Frobenius twists then gives a proof of strict homotopy invariance for homotopy invariant quasi-stable additive framed presheaves and identifies the canonical comparison with the perfect closure as a stable Nisnevich local equivalence of framed motives. We extend the comparison to E-framed motives for every motivic Thom spectrum E. It also yields the cancellation theorem and the cone theorem. For commutative symmetric Thom ring spectra, we identify triangulated categories of effective E-framed motives and effective E-modules and prove perfection invariance of these triangulated categories. All comparisons are made after inverting the exponential characteristic.

items.title: A Superfast Direct Solver for Type-III Inverse Nonuniform Discrete Fourier Transform
items.summary: Various fields in scientific computing require the use of the nonuniform discrete Fourier transform (NUDFT) and its inversion. In [H. Wilber, E. N. Epperly, and A. H. Barnett, SIAM J. Sci. Comput., 47 (2025), pp. A1702-A1732], the authors proposed a direct inversion method for the type-II NUDFT, which achieves quasi-linear complexity by approximating the type-II NUDFT matrix as a product of a hierarchical semiseparable (HSS) matrix and a DFT matrix. In this article, we propose a novel superfast direct inversion method for type-III NUDFT. The proposed method approximates the type-III NUDFT matrix as a product of a type-II NUDFT matrix and an HSS matrix. This decomposition enables both the forward application and the backward inversion to be accomplished with quasi-linear complexity. The fast inversion can serve as a high-accuracy direct solver or as an efficient preconditioner. Additionally, we provide an error bound for the approximation when the sample points are independent and identically distributed uniform random variables and the frequencies are perturbed continuous integers. Numerical results are presented to verify the relevant theoretical properties and demonstrate the efficiency of the proposed methods.

items.title: Consensus-Based Optimization of Path-Integral Free Energy for Model Predictive Control
items.summary: We propose CBO-MPPI, a sampling-based predictive controller that applies consensus-based optimization (CBO) to the free energy underlying model predictive path integral control (MPPI). Under hard constraints, this objective rewards sampling neighborhoods containing feasible, low-cost trajectories under perturbation. Standard MPPI performs a local stochastic search by updating one nominal control sequence from Gaussian perturbations around it. In CBO-MPPI, we estimate the free energy at multiple nominal centers from local rollouts. These estimates define a shared consensus that guides drift and diffusion, and the final selected center supplies an MPPI weighted-mean output. For the associated mean-field model, we establish well-posedness and, under additional assumptions, convergence toward a free-energy minimizer. In simulations of obstacle navigation, pendulum swing-up, and planar-arm manipulation under equal rollout budgets, at high temperatures, CBO-MPPI attains lower free energy than MPPI and multi-start MPPI and maintains greater obstacle clearance than CBO-MPC.

items.title: Limit groups with respect to Thompson's group $F$ and other hereditarily separating groups
items.summary: We prove that a limit group over Thompson's group $F$ cannot be an HNN-extension of $F$ with finitely generated associated subgroup. On the other hand we give an example of an $F$-limit group which is a centralized HNN-extenstions of $F$. We also study relatively limit groups with respect to $F$ and some other known groups of homeomorphisms of topological spaces. This paper revises and extends some results of the second author from arXiv:1308.6330.

items.title: The extremal process of a cascading family of branching Brownian motion
items.summary: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the extremal process of a cascading family of branching Brownian motions. This is a particle system on the real line such that each particle has a type in addition to his position. Particles of type $1$ move on the real line according to Brownian motions and branch at rate $1$ into two children of type $1$. Furthermore, at rate $α$, they give birth to children too of type $2$. Particles of type $2$ move according to standard Brownian motion and branch at rate $1$, but cannot give birth to descendants of type $1$. We obtain the asymptotic behaviour of the extremal process of particles of type $2$.

items.title: Non-monotone clustering and energetic regime switching in aggregation-diffusion systems
items.summary: We investigate transient clustering dynamics in nonlocal aggregation-diffusion systems from an energetic perspective. Starting from a stochastic interacting particle system, we study the associated macroscopic McKean-Vlasov equation on the torus and use its Wasserstein gradient-flow structure to analyse the competition between interaction-driven aggregation and entropy-driven diffusion. Through numerical experiments for locally attractive interaction kernels, we observe non-monotone clustering behaviour in intuitive geometric observables: in particular, the density peak height may first increase and subsequently decrease along trajectories converging to equilibrium. Using the decomposition of the free energy as a diagnostic, we identify alternating aggregation- and diffusion-dominated regimes underlying these transient dynamics. We investigate to what extent transitions between these regimes are related to the evolution of geometric observables, such as the peak height. Our results illustrate how non-monotone transient clustering can arise even in a dissipative gradient-flow system and highlight the complementary information provided by geometric clustering observables and the free-energy-based regime classification.

items.title: Extending indoor airborne infection risk modelling to 3D, with local surface deposition
items.summary: Mathematical models of indoor airborne disease transmission often rely on simplifying assumptions to reduce computational cost. In particular, aerosol concentrations may be assumed uniform across room height, allowing a two-dimensional (2D) formulation, while particle deposition on surfaces is represented by a first-order removal term acting throughout the computational domain. Here, we investigate how these assumptions affect predictions of airborne infection risk. We extend the Viral Infection Risk Indoor Simulator (VIRIS) [Xue et al. 2024] by developing a three-dimensional (3D) reaction-diffusion formulation in which aerosol deposition is represented by local removal at surfaces through a Robin boundary condition. We compare the original VIRIS framework with the extended model (VIRIS-3D-L) across three indoor spaces of increasing architectural and people-movement complexity: a courtroom, a care home and a supermarket. Across all three settings, the original 2D formulation with global removal predicts lower infection risks than the 3D formulation with local deposition, with differences of up to 50%. The predictions of VIRIS-3D-L also show encouraging agreement with observations from a documented courtroom outbreak previously used to validate VIRIS. Although computation time increases by approximately a factor of four on average, simulations remain feasible on a standard laptop, taking between 7 minutes and just over two hours. These findings suggest that VIRIS-3D-L offers a more physically realistic framework for assessing indoor airborne infection risk without prohibitive computational costs, while the original VIRIS remains useful when rapid simulations are required.

items.title: Periodic orbits 1-5 of quadratic polynomials on a new coordinate plane
items.summary: While iterating the quadratic polynomial f_{c}(x)=x^{2}+c the degree of the iterates grows very rapidly, and therefore solving the equations corresponding to periodic orbits becomes very difficult even for periodic orbits with a low period. In this work we present a new iteration model by introducing a change of variables into an (u,v)-plane, which changes situation drastically. As an excellent example of this we can compare equations of orbits period four on (x,c)- and (u,v)-planes. In the latter case, this equation is of degree two with respect to u and it can be solved explicitly. In former case the corresponding equation ((((x^{2}+c)^{2}+c)^{2}+c)^{2}+c-x)/((x^{2}+c)^{2}+c-x)=0 is of degree 12 and it is thus much more difficult to solve.

items.title: Superdecomposable Incidence and Complete Path Algebras
items.summary: Generalizing the setting of the second author's work from 2007, we characterize quivers $Q$ for which the dual algebra $R$ of the path coalgebra of $Q$, equivalently the complete path algebra, has no nonzero uniform right ideals: this happens exactly when every vertex of $Q$ can reach a vertex emitting at least two distinct arrows. Equivalently, the injective hull $E(R)$ of the right regular module is superdecomposable. These conditions are also equivalent to the path coalgebra having no nonzero hollow factor modules as a left module over its dual algebra. We also characterize nonempty locally finite posets whose incidence algebras have superdecomposable injective hulls of their right regular modules: this happens exactly when no principal up-set is upward directed.

items.title: Infinite Index Identities for Argyres-Douglas Theories and Graded Vector Space Isomorphisms for VOAs
items.summary: Supersymmetric indices provide stringent tests of dualities between superconformal field theories (SCFTs). We establish infinite families of Schur-index identities among four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Argyres-Douglas (AD) theories, with the logarithms of their fugacities related linearly. These identities connect theories with markedly different physical properties without requiring infrared duality, while still implying simple relations among their central charges and flavor levels. Through the SCFT/VOA correspondence, they become character identities for the associated affine and $W$-algebras. One broad family relates $D_p(G)$ and $(A_{(h+1)(p-1)},G)$ theories, corresponding to affine and principal $W$-algebras at boundary admissible levels. At the level of the underlying state spaces, these character identities suggest that the corresponding VOAs are related by graded vector space isomorphisms, which are weaker than full VOA isomorphisms. We explicitly construct such a graded isomorphism between the VOAs associated with $(A_1,A_{4p-3})$ and $(A_1,D_{2p})$. We also show the correspondence for universal affine and principal $W$-algebras and test its compatibility with their simple quotients by matching the lowest-degree null states. We establish analogous character identities for certain non-vacuum modules in concrete examples and conjecture a broader extension. Finally, beyond the SCFT/VOA correspondence, we discover similar identities between level-one affine and Virasoro algebras, whose further generalizations point toward a new spectral level-rank duality in WZW models.

items.title: Set-indexed and multiple sums in high dimensions
items.summary: We consider multiple and set-indexed sums of random vectors taking values in Euclidean space of growing dimension. It is shown that, when viewed as finite metric spaces, the sets of values of such sums converge in probability. The limit is identified as a generalization of the Wiener spiral, which appears as the high-dimensional limit of single-index sums.

items.title: Stability theorems for $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets
items.summary: We establish stability results for internal homs of $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets, a framework motivated by nerves of Frobenius monoids in the category of relations. Rotations are modelled through edge witnesses and horn-filling conditions, without requiring unique fillers. For $\varepsilon$-fibrant objects $X$ and $Y$, we prove that the internal hom $\mathrm{Fun}(X,Y)$ satisfies the $\varepsilon$-coherence conditions and admits fillers for all $\varepsilon$-horns of dimension at least two. Its subobject consisting of simplices whose vertices correspond to $η$-edge-preserving maps is $\varepsilon$-fibrant. We also introduce $η\varepsilon$-simplicial sets by adding explicit $η$-witnesses and prove that the internal hom of two $η\varepsilon$-fibrant objects is again $η\varepsilon$-fibrant. Our proofs use adjunctions relating $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets and paracyclic sets. We characterise the $\varepsilon$-horn filling property by requiring the corresponding counit to be a trivial Kan fibration. Consequently, for every object satisfying this property, coherent choices of rotations of each simplex form a contractible Kan complex.

items.title: The Möbius function of factorizations with a simple prime factor
items.summary: The poset of factorizations of a positive integer $n$ (ordered by refinement) is known to have a very irregular Möbius function. We prove that this function becomes completely explicit whenever $n$ is divisible by a prime $q$ to the first power only ($q^2 \nmid n$). Specifically, between a factorization with $k$ factors and $n$ itself, the Möbius function is given by $(-1)^{k-1}$ multiplied by the number of ways to order the factors that are not divisible by $q$. As a consequence, the sum of the absolute values of the Möbius function over this interval equals twice the number of ordered factorizations of $n/q$.

items.title: Graphs attaining Haemers' toughness bound
items.summary: Haemers \cite{Haemers2020} conjectured that every connected noncomplete graph $G$ satisfies $t(G)\geqslantμ_2/(μ_n-δ)$, where $t(G)$ is the toughness of $G$, $μ_2$ and $μ_n$ are its algebraic connectivity and Laplacian spectral radius, and $δ$ is its minimum degree. Greaves and Zhu \cite{GreavesZhu2026} recently proved this conjecture, leaving the equality case open. We characterize all graphs attaining equality: a graph attains equality if and only if its complement has a complete component whose order is at least the Laplacian spectral radius of every other component. Equivalently, its algebraic connectivity and independence number sum to its order. We also determine all vertex cuts attaining the toughness, and show that for regular graphs, the equality graphs are exactly the complete multipartite graphs with parts of equal size.

items.title: Entropic quantum error correction for independent and correlated amplitude damping errors
items.summary: The idea of using quantum entropy for quantum error correction (QEC) has existed for a long time. However, its computational complexity has limited its practical use: even a $[[4,1]]$ code for standard independent amplitude damping errors involves a $256\times 256$ Hermitian matrix, so the approach scales poorly as the codeword length increases. For correlated errors, the situation is even worse. In this paper, we show that, by using the insights developed in our previous paper and exploiting certain structures of quantum conditional mutual information, we can solve these problems exactly by hand, using only $2\times 2$ unitary matrices. By examining the entropy, we identify the leakage channels and the amount of leakage exactly, then define the recovery map accordingly. The rules defining our recovery map are simple, intuitive, and computationally inexpensive: for independent errors, it is based on 16 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions; for correlated errors, it is based on 6 explicitly given orthonormal vectors and 6 instructions. Our method sacrifices little in terms of performance: for the widely used entanglement fidelity, our simple QEC recovery map achieves a sharp result; for the worst-case fidelity, the best result is about $9\%$ better than ours; for correlated errors, there are no comparable results for short codewords. Among the known techniques, our recovery map is the first non-global one. The calculations use elementary linear algebra and calculus, and is presented in great detail.

items.title: Representing in Low rank II: Virtual structure and Isomorphism problem
items.summary: We group theoretically characterise the finite groups $G$ and number fields $F$ such that all $F$-representations of reduced degree at least $2$ are so-called exceptional. If $G$ is not a $2$-group, we obtain a full classification. Secondly, we determine whether such groups are uniquely determined by their group algebra $FG$. In particular, we obtain an instance of the virtual structure problem of Kleinert and answer the rational isomorphism problem for such groups.

items.title: On the periodicity of meromorphic functions of the form $ff^{(k)}$
items.summary: For a non-entire meromorphic function $f$ and an integer $k$, we will show that whenever $ff^{(k)}$ is periodic so is $f$. This result gives an affirmative answer to a significant class of the so called generalized Yang's conjecture.

items.title: Cartesian products of groups as quantum metric spaces
items.summary: We provide a new class of finitely generated groups whose word-length functions give rise to compact quantum metric spaces. Kaad's recent theory of matrix compact quantum metric spaces is instrumental in obtaining this new class, and along the way we also show that any length function on an amenable group which gives rise to a compact quantum metric space in fact gives rise to a matrix compact quantum metric space, and that the corresponding result is false for the free group on two generators.

items.title: Counting Lattice Points in Translations: Uniqueness and Existence Results
items.summary: Generalizing a recent theorem by Higashitani et al. (Comb. Theory 2025), it is shown that a convex body $K$ is uniquely described up to integer translation by the function $\mathrm{t}_K(v) = |(K-v)\cap\mathbb{Z}^n|$, $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$. For a lattice polytope $P$ the function $\mathrm{t}_P$ is decomposed into homogeneous components $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$, similar to the Ehrhart polynomial. It is shown that the functions $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$ are simultaneous eigenfunctions of a family of linear operators introduced by Kubert and Lang in (Math. Z. 1976) and that, conversely, the linear spaces of piecewise constant eigenfunctions are generated by the respective coefficients $\mathrm{t}_{P,i}$. A structure theorem for the simultaneous eigenspace corresponding to the $(n-1)$st coefficient in the decomposition of $\mathrm{t}_P$ is obtained. This leads to an explicit description of the set of functions $\mathrm{t}_P$, where $P$ ranges over all lattice polygons, as well as to inequalities for the number of lattice points in dilated and translated lattice polytopes.

items.title: Sample complexity and scalability of adaptive-sampling trust-region methods for zeroth-order stochastic optimization --- Part~II: a new pathwise analysis with randomized subspaces
items.summary: Stochastic trust-region methods are usually analyzed in expectation or with high probability: the guarantee is about the law of the algorithm, not about the run in hand. This paper analyzes the adaptive sampling stochastic trust-region method ASTRO-DF (which is the reuse variant ASTRA-R in Part I) in random subspaces along almost every sample path. The route has one probabilistic ingredient, the accuracy of the common-random-number estimates at the adaptive sample size, uniformly over the trust region; Part~I established it by chaining, here it is obtained at the stopping time by optional stopping and converted, by the first Borel--Cantelli lemma, into an accuracy that holds from a random index on, after which the deterministic trust-region argument applies. We prove almost sure convergence and almost sure iteration and sample complexity of orders $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(dε^{-2})$ and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(d^2ε^{-4})$, with a subspace dimension growing logarithmically; we show that at a fixed subspace dimension the eventual-accuracy argument yields $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(ε^{-2-\mathcal{O}(1/p)})$ iterations and $\tilde{\mathcal{O}}(ε^{-4-\mathcal{O}(1/p)})$ samples; we show that the random index after which the rates hold cannot be too large and has an explicit, rapidly decaying tail. Compared with the supermartingale route, the pathwise route needs no lower bound on the per-iteration probability of a good iteration, no coupling between the trust-region expansion factor and the sketch, and no moment condition on the summed squared radii.

items.title: Safety Certificates for Systems under Attack via Stackelberg Set Games
items.summary: We study a Stackelberg set selection game for linear systems subject to bounded disturbances and additive attacks. The defender selects the vector parameter of a polytopic safe set template; the attacker, after observing this choice, selects the vector parameter of an admissible attack set. The payoff is a signed, facet-normalised invariance margin that tests invariance exactly and quantifies either the available contraction or the facet inflation needed when invariance fails. Both controlled and robust controlled invariance are treated, corresponding to different information patterns for the control input. Exploiting the structure of parameterised polyhedra, we show that within each validity region the margin is concave in the attack parameter, which reduces the follower minimisation to finitely many extreme parameters. The complete max--min game is then solved by a finite family of LPs, one per defender validity region, each enforcing all attacker regions under a common defender decision and guaranteed margin. The framework handles hard state constraints and additional costs related to the safe set size, and recovers optimal set parameters together with state and attack realisations that activate the certificate. A load frequency control example under false data injection illustrates the construction, the validity decomposition, and the two information patterns.

items.title: Bias-Optimal Bounds for Stochastic Gradient Descent
items.summary: The non-asymptotic analysis of Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) typically yields bounds that decompose into a bias term and a variance term. In this work, we focus on the bias component and study the extent to which SGD can match the optimal convergence behavior of deterministic gradient descent. Assuming only (strong) convexity and smoothness of the objective, we derive new bounds for the full range of constant step-sizes $γL \in (0,2)$. This includes critical and large step-size regimes that were previously unexplored without additional variance assumptions, in both the convex and strongly convex cases. Those bounds are bias-optimal, in the sense that the bias term coincides with the worst-case rate of gradient descent, for all non-critical step-sizes. For critical step-sizes, we show that no bounds can be obtained with an optimal bias term, but that this optimal bias can be approximated arbitrarily closely. As an immediate application, we provide new complexity bounds for the Stochastic Proximal algorithm, without the need of regularity assumptions.

items.title: Equidistribution of Gross lattices of supersingular elliptic curves
items.summary: For a prime $p$, we consider two important families of integral quadratic lattices associated to isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}$, the lattices of endomorphisms of trace zero, and the Gross lattices of endomorphisms. We prove effective equidistribution of the shapes of these lattices as $p\to\infty$ through primes, in the arithmetic locally symmetric space of unimodular lattices up to isometry. As an application, we obtain, as $p\to\infty$, the asymptotic distribution of successive minima of these lattices. These results are proved using tools from homogeneous dynamics, in particular, the key dynamical input is a recent adelic equidistribution theorem due to Einsiedler, Margulis, Mohammadi, and Venkatesh.

items.title: An entropy-stable splitting strategy for a hyperbolic dispersive shallow-water model on unstructured meshes
items.summary: This paper presents an entropy-stable splitting strategy for the numerical solution of a hyperbolic approximation of the Serre--Green--Naghdi (SGN) model, leading to an efficient solver for dispersive water waves on unstructured meshes. The model was introduced by Escalante et al. (2019) and justified shortly thereafter by Richard (2021) as an asymptotic model of the free-surface Euler equations under a weak compressibility assumption. While the parent model includes full topography terms and enhanced dispersive properties, the present study focuses on its mild-slope form without enhanced dispersion, which retains an exact energy equation, the cornerstone of the stability analysis. The splitting yields a shallow-water subsystem with two passive scalars, governed by the \textit{slow} gravity waves, and an acoustic subsystem carrying the dispersive effects, governed by the \textit{fast} acoustic waves. The gravity step adapts an existing entropy-stable scheme, while an original scheme is derived for the acoustic step; both dissipate the energy at the discrete level, under local fully discrete stability criteria on general unstructured meshes. Complementary linear analyses select the low-dissipation calibration of the gravity step used in the computations, outside the scope of the nonlinear estimate. The acoustic step, which requires no global linear solve, is sub-iterated after each gravity time step; the resulting solver is three to six times more expensive than a classical shallow-water solver, depending on the chosen acoustic speed. Numerical validations, ranging from academic benchmarks to a realistic coastal configuration, highlight the properties of the approach and pave the way for operational use.

items.title: Holonomy groupoids of singular subalgebroids in the non-integrable case
items.summary: The holonomy groupoid of a singular foliation was constructed by Androulidakis and Skandalis around 2006. The construction was later extended to singular subalgebroids of an integrable Lie algebroid, upon a choice of integrating Lie groupoid. In this work, we extend the construction of the holonomy groupoid even further, by allowing for non-integrable Lie algebroids. To do so, we make a choice of integrating local Lie groupoid $G$. When the Mal'cev completion $AC(G)$ is smooth, our construction recovers the holonomy groupoid associated with the Lie groupoid $AC(G)$. Furthermore, our holonomy groupoid has an associated $*$-algebra. We present examples in which the holonomy groupoid is realized as a quotient of the transformation groupoid of a Lie group action.

items.title: Transverse Analytic Envelopes and the Baum--Bott Rationality Conjecture
items.summary: We study holomorphic first integrals near singular leaves through transverse analytic envelopes. For diagonal actions these are normal toric quotients, and complete semiglobal integrability along singular orbits with independent support weights is equivalent to maximal resonance rank and finite monodromy. For commuting fields in convergent simultaneous Poincaré--Dulac normal form, induced derivations determine the first-integral algebra. Labelled quotients and logarithmic residues reconstruct weights at maximal rank; Grassmannians describe the ambiguity otherwise. Polynomial examples show losses invisible to prescribed finite jets. For the Baum--Bott rationality conjecture, we prove rationality and an explicit residue formula for smooth compact singular components with product charts and a common invertible semisimple transverse linear part of maximal resonance rank. Equivariant cohomology gives higher-degree vanishing for affine diagonal torus actions, including intersecting singular strata.

items.title: The Brualdi--Hoffman--Turán problem for odd wheels: Resolving a conjecture of Yu, Li and Peng
items.summary: This paper addresses the Brualdi--Hoffman--Turán problem, which asks for the maximum adjacency spectral radius over graphs with a fixed number of edges that forbid a prescribed subgraph. We settle an open conjecture due to Yu, Li and Peng for odd wheel graphs $W_{2k+1}$. A striking dichotomy appears in the extremal configurations: the forbidden-$W_5$ case and the general case $k\ge 3$ rely on identical stability and dense-core reductions but produce completely different extremal graphs. For sufficiently large size $m$, we derive sharp spectral inequalities and give complete characterizations for graphs achieving equality. Our approach combines the edge-spectral stability theorem with the dense-core method and residual-function analysis. Beyond solving the target conjecture, the developed framework provides a systematic approach for edge-spectral Turán problems and implies several known results for odd cycles, friendship graphs and odd fans. Directions for future research on edge-spectral supersaturation are also discussed.

items.title: Well-posedness for Wright--Fisher SPDEs with measurable drift
items.summary: We prove weak existence and uniqueness in law of $[0,1]$-valued solutions for a class of scalar stochastic heat equations with measurable drifts $b : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$, driven by Wright--Fisher noise. The only assumptions we require on the drift are Borel-measurability, and the one-way inequalities $-Cu\leq b(u)\leq C(1-u)$ for some $C<\infty$, compatible with the necessary condition $b(1)\leq 0\leq b(0)$. These are vastly more general conditions than were previously available. Our proof relies on a stochastic duality between the solution of the stochastic heat equation, and a voting scheme running along the graph of a branching-coalescing particle system, generalising the class of drifts for which a dual process is available. Our results and their proof put the regularisation-by-noise result of Barnes, Mytnik and Sun, and its explanation, on a much more general footing.

items.title: Sharp Finite-Time Blow-Up for Unforced Axisymmetric Euler Without Swirl via Multiscale Data
items.summary: For the unforced Euler equations, we construct a compactly supported initial vorticity within the class of axisymmetric flows without swirl, whose solution blows up in finite time. The initial vorticity belongs simultaneously to every Hölder space $C^α$, $α<1/3$. This is sharp given that global regularity is known when $α=1/3$ in the case of axisymmetric flows without swirl. Previous constructions by Shkoller \cite{Shk26}, Chen \cite{Chen26I,Chen26II}, and Shao--Wei--Zhang--Zhang \cite{SWZZ26} establish blow-up for each prescribed exponent $α$ in the same sharp range. Our construction achieves simultaneous membership in all these spaces. In addition, our construction is short. Our proof uses multiscale initial data, in the spirit of Kim--Jeong~\cite{KJ22}, Córdoba--Martínez-Zoroa--Zheng~\cite{CMZZ25}, and Bang--Cheskidov~\cite{BC26}. The blow-up mechanism is a forward cascade through successively smaller scales. A main difficulty in approaching the critical exponent $1/3$ is caused by large self-deformation. Our main idea to overcome this difficulty is to obtain a lower bound for strain at the stationary non-smooth point by using angular redistribution. A related outstanding open problem is to establish an unforced Euler blow-up from smooth data in the case of axisymmetric flows with swirl. A recent multiscale construction by OpenAI for the unforced Euler equations is, however, non-axisymmetric. Although we work in the no-swirl class, the axisymmetric multiscale mechanism developed here may offer a possible route toward the still-open problem of axisymmetric smooth blow-up.
