We prove that the quotient of a monoid in $\Rel$ by a dimensionality is again a monoid. We prove that polygroupoids (and hence hypergroups) are exactly the symmetric $†$-Frobenius structures in $\Rel$. We use this characterization to prove that the quotient of a polygroupoid by a dimensionality that preserves the inverse is a polygroupoid.

items.title: A Spectral Proximal DC Algorithm with Nonmonotone Line Search and Extrapolation
items.summary: The paper proposes a novel proximal difference-of-convex (DC) algorithmic framework to solve general nonconvex, nonsmooth optimization problems. The basic pBBDCA method combines Barzilai-Borwein (BB) parameter selection with a nonmonotone directional line search, requiring only one proximal solve per iteration. We also develop two extrapolated variants using restart and safeguarding mechanisms. The global convergence of the proposed framework is rigorously established under the Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz property. Numerical experiments on the SCAD-regularized least squares problem and graph Ginzburg-Landau image segmentation models demonstrate that the proposed methods achieve highly competitive efficiency and accuracy.

items.title: Additive cubes are avoidable over $\{0,1,2,3\}$, $\{0,1,4\}$ and $\{0,2,5\}$
items.summary: We prove that additive cubes are avoidable over the alphabet $\{0,1,2,3\}$, thereby solving a long-standing question initiated by Pirillo and Varricchio in 1994. By extending the reduction and spectral machinery of Cassaigne, Currie, Schaeffer, and Shallit (2014), we prove that the search for additive cubes in such morphic images reduces to a finite graph traversal. We exhibit eight explicit morphisms from $\{0,1,3,4\}^*$ to $\{0,1,2,3\}^*$ of length 3 whose images on the Cassaigne \textit{et al.} infinite word contain no additive cubes.

items.title: Transferability of Error Bounds and the Kurdyka-Łojasiewicz Property under $C^1$ Partial Smoothness
items.summary: This work studies how a generalized error bound (GEB) property in the ambient Euclidean space transfers to the active manifold under $C^1$ partial smoothness. The GEB generalizes the standard error bound, which upper bounds the distance to a subset of critical points using first-order stationarity residuals, by allowing the distance to be composed with a gauge function. In the ambient space, these residuals are measured by the subdifferential or the slope of the original function, while on the manifold they are measured by the Riemannian gradient or the slope of the restricted function. We develop complementary geometric and metric analyses to show that the ambient and manifold GEBs are equivalent with the same gauge function. The geometric argument shows that the projection of the subdifferential onto the tangent space coincides with the Riemannian gradient, while the metric approach combines slope estimates, identifiability, and a new uniform linear-growth result for $C^1$ manifolds. We further extend our analysis to establish the analogous equivalence for the Kurdyka--Łojasiewicz (KL) property, with the same desingularizer, and separately characterize their connections with the GEB. Finally, for regularized optimization, we relate subdifferential and proximal error bounds, thereby placing the previously established equivalence between proximal and manifold error bounds for $\ell_1$-regularization within a broader framework.

items.title: Essential spectrum of singularly perturbed Dirac operators on bounded domains
items.summary: In this paper self-adjoint Dirac operators on bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $\mathbb{R}^3$ with elliptic boundary conditions perturbed by singular $δ$-shell potentials supported on compact curves or surfaces are considered. While the unperturbed operator has purely discrete spectrum, it is shown that certain critical values of the interaction strengths lead to the appearance of essential spectrum. More precisely, each connected component of the interaction support, where the coupling constants have such critical values, produces in dimension two a point and in dimension three even a closed interval in the essential spectrum, where the size of the latter depends on the geometry and the coupling constants.

items.title: On character conductors and Sylow p-subgroups
items.summary: Let $P\in\operatorname{Syl}_p(G)$, where $G$ is a finite group and $p$ is a prime, and let $χ\in\operatorname{Irr}(G)$. In 2024, I. M. Isaacs and G. Navarro asked whether the degree of $\mathbb{Q}_{p^f}$ over $\mathbb{Q}_p(χ_P)$ is always at most the $p$-part $χ(1)_p$ of $χ(1)$, where $p^f$ is the $p$-part of the conductor of $χ$ and $f\geq1$. Here $\mathbb{Q}_n=\mathbb{Q}(e^{2πi/n})$ is the $n$th cyclotomic field, $χ_P$ is the restriction of $χ$ to $P$, and $\mathbb{Q}_p(χ_P)$ is the field generated over $\mathbb{Q}_p$ by the values of $χ_P$. We prove that this inequality holds for $p$-solvable groups.

items.title: The Exact Stabilization Time of Self-Stabilizing Coloring: Mean, Variance, and Distribution
items.summary: The worst-case stabilization time of a self-stabilizing algorithm usually says little about its typical behavior beyond the order of magnitude. This paper revisits the classical self-stabilizing $Delta+1$ coloring algorithm with vertices activated at random, one at a time (the random central daemon). Considering the number of color changes as a random variable, we study its mean, variance and, on several families of graphs, its exact distribution. The analysis rests on a reduction: a vertex changes color, at most once, exactly when it is not a local maximum of a uniformly random labeling of the vertices, maxima being taken among the neighbors that share its initial color (the monochrome initial configuration is the slowest case). What can be predicted depends on what is known of the graph. The degree distribution (the view at distance one) gives the mean. The variance needs the view at distance two, in particular the triangles, and the full law needs the whole graph. We give closed-form results, from monochrome and from uniformly random initial configurations, on paths, cycles, random trees, Erdős-R{é}nyi graphs and bipartite random graphs. From a monochrome start, the mean stays within a factor two of the worst case, whereas the variance ranges from zero (disjoint cliques) to order $n^2$ (the star on $n$ vertices)..

items.title: The Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment: classical and quantum optimization approaches
items.summary: Efficient railway rolling stock management requires the coordinated planning of train-unit assignment, shunting movements, track occupation, service operations, and workforce allocation. These interdependent decisions give rise to a challenging combinatorial optimization problem, particularly as the size of the fleet and the planning horizon increase. This paper introduces the Train Unit Shunting Problem with Service Scheduling and Workforce Assignment, a mixed-integer linear programming formulation that integrates these operational decisions within a unified optimization framework. To improve computational tractability, a preprocessing procedure is developed to reduce the size of the resulting model. The proposed approach is evaluated through computational experiments on instances of increasing size and under different objective-function weight and cost configurations. Classical optimization experiments using Gurobi show that filtering method reduces the number of decision variables and constraints, while its impact on computational time varies across instances. In addition, a constrained quadratic model representation is investigated using D-Wave's hybrid quantum-classical optimization solver.

items.title: Surface-to-Volume Homogenization of NonLinear Steklov Eigencouples with NonHomogeneous Orlicz Growth in Perforated Domains
items.summary: We study normalized principal Steklov eigencouples on periodically perforated domains when both the bulk energy and the boundary normalization have general, possibly nonhomogeneous, Orlicz growth. The surface term on the hole boundaries carries the critical surface-to-volume scaling. For each fixed mass level, the constrained minima converge along the whole family, while selected minimizers, fluxes and Lagrange multipliers converge along subsequences to the corresponding objects of a homogenized problem. In the limit, the bulk operator is given by a convex cell problem, and the boundary term becomes a volume term weighted by the total surface density of the reference hole. The key tool is a strong approximation of the microscopic traces by cell averages, measured in the scaled surface modular.

items.title: Every obstruction to noncontextual hidden variables is finite: well-founded refutations in infinitary real-valued logic
items.summary: We study the obstructions to noncontextual hidden variables when quantum probability is described in full, by the complete lattice of closed subspaces of a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space together with its countably additive measures. We give such a description in infinitary real-valued logic, the infinitary extension of Keisler's model theory of general structures; the countable suprema and infima of this logic express the completeness of the lattice and the countable additivity of the measures. The standard models of our axioms represent exactly the density-operator measures of Gleason's theorem. The axioms are closed conditions, non-strict inequalities between the values of sentences and rational numbers. The expressive power afforded by infinitary sentences comes at the price of compactness. The hypothesis that at each hidden state every event receives the value 0 or 1, whatever the context of measurement, contradicts the axioms, yet it is consistent with every finite subset of them. The obstructions nevertheless remain finite. We prove that in this logic a countable set of closed conditions is inconsistent if and only if a well-founded tree whose branches end in finite contradictions refutes it; for the hypothesis above, every such tree has an infinitely branching node. The finiteness theorem is therefore maximal: a hidden-variable hypothesis expressed by countably many closed conditions is inconsistent with the axioms, and thus an obstruction, exactly when such a tree refutes the hypothesis together with the axioms. The same language defines, uniformly across standard models, exactly the $σ$-projective sets of probabilities, and all these results are proved in ZFC.

items.title: On Sparsity and Sub-Gaussianity in the Johnson-Lindenstrauss Lemma
items.summary: We provide a simple proof of the Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma for sub-Gaussian variables. We extend the analysis to identify how sparse projections can be, and what the cost of sparsity is on the target dimension. The Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma is the theoretical core of the dimensionality reduction methods based on random projections. While its original formulation involves matrices with Gaussian entries, the computational cost of random projections can be drastically reduced by the use of simpler variables, especially if they vanish with a high probability. In this paper, we propose a simple and elementary analysis of random projections under classical assumptions that emphasizes the key role of sub-Gaussianity. Furthermore, we show how to extend it to sparse projections, emphasizing the limits induced by the sparsity of the data itself.

items.title: Universal TT- and TQ-relations via centrally extended q-Onsager algebra
items.summary: Let $A_q$ be the alternating central extension of the q-Onsager algebra, a comodule algebra over the quantum loop algebra of $sl_2$. We classify one-dimensional representations of $A_q$, and show that spin-j K-operators constructed in arXiv:2301.00781 act as K-matrices previously obtained in the literature. Using these K-operators and K-matrices, we construct universal spin-j transfer matrices generating commutative subalgebras in $A_q$. Within a technical conjecture, we derive their fusion hierarchy, the so-called universal TT-relations. On spin-chain representations of $A_q$, we show how the universal transfer matrices evaluate to spin-chain transfer matrices, and as a result we get explicit TT-relations for all values of spins for auxiliary and quantum spaces, any inhomogeneities, and general integrable boundary conditions. In particular, we derive previously conjectured TT-relations. Using the TT-relations, we show that n-th local conserved quantities of the spin-j chains of length N are polynomials of total degree 4Njn in two non-local operators of the q-Onsager algebra. As a result, we give an algorithm of explicit calculation of all local conserved quantities in terms of spin operators. Furthermore, using the universal TT-relations we derive exchange relations between spin-j Hamiltonians and the two non-local operators showing non-trivial symmetries for special boundary conditions, that they commute with all Hamiltonian densities. As another application of our universal TT-relations we propose universal T-system, Y-system and universal TQ-relations for $A_q$, and as a result, universal TQ for the q-Onsager algebra. For diagonal boundary conditions, we also obtain universal TT- and TQ-relations for a degenerate version of $A_q$ known as centrally extended augmented q-Onsager algebra. We finally discuss implications of our results for generalized Gibbs ensemble construction.

items.title: On reality of eigenvalues of banded block Toeplitz matrices
items.summary: We formulate and partially prove a general conjecture providing necessary and sufficient conditions for the reality of the asymptotic spectrum of an arbitrary real banded block Toeplitz matrix. Additionally we present numerical experiments supporting it. This conjecture is a direct generalization of the already existing one in the case of banded Toeplitz matrices.

items.title: Face lattices of polytopes and bipolar polytopes
items.summary: We show that the face lattice of every convex polytope $Q$ is, on the combinatorial level, the vertex set of a polytope one dimension higher: the faces of $Q$ are the vertices of a \emph{bipolar polytope} $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$, and the intervals of the face lattice are its faces. Here a bipolar polytope is a polytope with two distinguished vertices, the poles, such that every facet contains exactly one of them and an intersection property holds. The vertices of every bipolar polytope carry a lattice order whose intervals are the faces, and this lattice is the face lattice of the vertex figure at either pole; conversely, every atomistic and coatomistic lattice that is an abstract polytope arises in this way. Geometrically, the polar of the Cayley polytope of $Q$ and $Q^\circ$ is a convex realization of $W(\mathcal{F}(Q))$ whenever the normal fan and the face fan of $Q$ satisfy a certain interval condition; this holds for cubes and cross-polytopes and for suitable realizations of all polytopes of dimension at most three. Finally, every combinatorial type of $3$-polytope has a realization that decomposes into convex bipolar polytopes, one for each vertex.

items.title: De Rham logarithmic classes and Tate conjecture
items.summary: We introduce the definition of De Rham logarithmic classes. We show that the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle of a smooth algebraic variety over a field of characteristic zero is logarithmic and conversely that a logarithmic class of bidegree $(d,d)$ is the De Rham class of an algebraic cycle (of codimension $d$). We also give for smooth algebraic varieties over a $p$-adic field an analytic version of this result. We deduce from the analytic case the Tate conjecture for smooth projective varieties over fields of finite type over $\mathbb Q$.

items.title: Lower bounds on ranks of universal quadratic forms through geometry-of-numbers
items.summary: We obtain lower bounds for the ranks of universal forms over totally real cubic fields using techniques from geometry-of-numbers and the parametrisation of cubic rings by binary cubics due to Delone--Faddeev. Additionally, our methods give lower bounds for totally real primitive fields of any degree with codifferent generated by a totally positive element.

items.title: Equivariant Cleft Extensions and Singular Equivalences
items.summary: We study the equivariant lifting of cleft extensions of abelian categories and its impact on singularity categories. Specifically, we establish the framework for lifting a cleft extension to a G-equivariant cleft extension. Furthermore, we prove that a restriction functor associated to a cleft extension induces a singular equivalence if and only if its equivariant counterpart does. As a concrete application, we demonstrate that the skew group ring of a $G$-equivariant $θ$-extension is isomorphic to a $\widehatθ$-extension of the base skew group ring, allowing us to lift singular equivalences for these structures.

items.title: Common values of linear recurrences related to Ankeny-Brauer-Chowla polynomials
items.summary: Let $P_u(X)=XQ(X)(X-u)+1$, where $Q(X)\in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ is monic, separabel, has constant term $\pm 1$, and degree $q\ge 1$. Denote $(A_n(u))$ the linear recursive sequence having characteristic polynomial $P_u(X)$ and initial terms $A_0,\ldots,A_{q+1}\in \mathbb{Z}$ such that at least one of them is non-zero. Then there exist effectively computable constants $n_0,u_0$ depending only on $Q(X)$ and $\max\{|A_0|,\ldots, |A_{q+1}|\}$ such that if $|A_n(u)| = |A_m(u)|$ holds for some integers $u,n,m$ with $u>u_0$ and $n\not=m$ then $\max\{

items.title: Thales's theorem in higher dimensions
items.summary: In the Euclidean plane, Thales's theorem is equivalent to the statement that a quadrilateral with two opposite right angles has a circumscribed circle. We generalize the latter to higher dimensions: a convex polytope with two distinguished vertices, the \emph{poles}, such that the faces spanned by the two poles are perpendicular, is inscribed in the sphere whose diameter joins its poles. These \emph{orthogonally bipolar} polytopes are exactly the bipolar polytopes of a companion paper that arise as cutouts by orthogonal projections. As an application we show that for a polytope $P$ and a point $B$, the balls with diameters $[V,B]$, $V$ a vertex of $P$, cover $P$, and that the power diagram of their boundary spheres refines this covering to a tiling. Further, we investigate the properties of orthogonally bipolar polytopes, their characterization, and their application to tilings: in dimension three, the cutouts of $P$ by the orthogonal projections of $B$ onto its faces tile $P$ by orthogonally bipolar polytopes exactly when every such projection lies in the relative interior of its face. Finally, we propose an interpretation of the topic in political science.

items.title: Markov Decision Processes of the Third Kind: Learning Distributions by Policy Gradient Descent
items.summary: The goal of this paper is to analyze distributional Markov Decision Processes as a class of control problems in which the objective is to learn policies that steer the distribution of a cumulative reward toward a prescribed target law, rather than optimizing an expected value or a risk functional. To solve the resulting distributional control problem, we propose a policy-gradient algorithm based on neural-network parameterizations of randomized Markov policies, defined on an augmented state space and a sample-based evaluation of the characteristic-function loss. Under mild regularity and growth assumptions, we prove convergence of the algorithm to stationary points using stochastic approximation techniques. Several numerical experiments illustrate the ability of the method to match complex target distributions, recover classical optimal policies when they exist, and reveal intrinsic non-uniqueness phenomena specific to distributional control.

items.title: Fluctuations in the non-linear supersymmetric hyperbolic sigma model with hierarchical interactions
items.summary: We consider a class of non-linear supersymmetric hyperbolic sigma models on a hierarchical lattice. We prove that the hyperbolic distance between the superspin at any vertex and a reference superspin has asymptotically small fluctuations for large enough interactions, uniformly in the size of the graph and in the choice of the vertex. This can be viewed as a spontaneous breaking of the Lorentz boost symmetry.

items.title: Auto-conditioned Gradient Descent Methods for Multiobjective Optimization
items.summary: This paper proposes two linesearch-free algorithms based on steepest descent methods for smooth multiobjective optimization: auto-conditioned steepest descent method for multiobjective optimization (AC-SDM) and auto-conditioned normalized gradient descent method for multiobjective optimization (AC-NGDM). Both algorithms estimate the local Lipschitz constant from the function values and the first-order information obtained in previous iterations. AC-SDM uses a shared estimate of the Lipschitz constant to construct a scaled steepest descent direction. For AC-NGDM, we use each function's local Lipschitz estimate to normalize the gradient of the corresponding function and construct the descent direction. We prove that every accumulation point of any sequence generated by both algorithms is a Pareto critical point. We also establish convergence rates of $O(1/\sqrt{k})$ for nonconvex objectives and $O(1/k)$ for convex objectives. Numerical results on several test problems demonstrate that AC-SDM and AC-NGDM require fewer iterations and less CPU time than the multiobjective steepest descent method with an Armijo line search and a max-type nonmonotone line search.

items.title: Ideal MHD below the classical well-posedness threshold
items.summary: We establish local existence and uniqueness of solutions for the ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamics system posed on $[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^n$ with $n\ge2$ and initial conditions given by a nonzero constant magnetic field $\mathbf{B}_0$ and arbitrary divergence-free velocity $v_0\in H^s$, in the range $(n+1)/2<s\le n/2+1$. The proof uses a Lagrangian wave--Hodge reformulation and exploits an Alfvén null--structure hidden in the pressure forcing. This work builds on Zhang \cite{Zhang2026} and provides a bridge from the Lagrangian theory to the Eulerian Cauchy problem. In particular, the constructed solutions are induced by a bi-Lipschitz and volume-preserving map.

items.title: A narrow band method for non-causal discretizations of anisotropic eikonal equations, with adaptive width, sub-and super-solution construction, and quasi-linear complexity
items.summary: We describe a narrow band method for numerically solving anisotropic eikonal equations, and more generally static first order Hamilton-Jacobi equations with possibly non-convex Hamiltonians, discretized using standard schemes (semi-Lagrangian, upwind-differences, Lax-Friedrichs). The causality property is not needed, in contrast with the fast marching method. The proposed approach simultaneously builds a numerical sub-solution u and super-solution u to the problem, and adapts the width of the narrow band based on their comparison. We prove that (1 + $ε$)u $\ge$ u at termination, where $ε$ > 0 is any given tolerance parameter, and that the worst case complexity is O(N | ln $ε$| ln(N/$ε$)), where N denotes the number of discretization points, and the underlying constant is explicit in terms of those associated with the scheme properties. Numerical experiments illustrate our results.

items.title: Michael-Simon inequality for anisotropic energies close to the area via multilinear Kakeya-type bounds
items.summary: Given an anisotropic integrand $F:\text{Gr}_k(\mathbb{R}^n)\to(0,\infty)$, we can generalize the classical isotropic area by looking at the functional $$\mathcal{F}(Σ^k):=\int_ΣF(T_xΣ)\,d\mathcal{H}^k.$$ While a monotonicity formula is not available for critical points, when $k=2$ and $n=3$ we show that the Michael-Simon inequality holds if $F$ is close to $1$ (in $C^1$), meaning that $\mathcal{F}$ is close to the usual area. Our argument is partly based on some key ideas of Almgren, who proved this result in an unpublished manuscript, but we largely simplify his original proof by showing a new functional inequality for vector fields on the plane, which can be seen as a quantitative version of Alberti's rank-one theorem, and we also remove a convexity assumption on $F$. As another byproduct, we also show Michael-Simon for another class of integrands which includes the $\ell^p$ norms for $p\in(1,\infty)$. For a general $F$ satisfying the atomic condition, we also show that the validity of Michael-Simon is equivalent to compactness of rectifiable varifolds.

items.title: A generalized Hurwitz stability criterion via rectangular block Hankel matrices for nonmonic matrix polynomials
items.summary: We develop a Hurwitz stability criterion for nonmonic matrix polynomials via column reduction, generalizing existing approaches constrained by the monic assumption and thus serving as a more natural extension of Gantmacher's classical stability criterion via Markov parameters. Starting from redefining the associated Markov parameters through an adaptive column-wise Lienard-Chipart splitting method, our framework constructs two structured matrices whose rectangular Hankel blocks are obtained via the extraction of these parameters. We establish an explicit interrelation between the inertia of column reduced matrix polynomials and the derived structured matrices. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the Hurwitz stability of column reduced matrix polynomials can be determined by the Hermitian positive definiteness of these rectangular block Hankel matrices.

items.title: A Note on Decomposable and Reducible Integer Matrices
items.summary: We propose necessary and sufficient conditions for an integer matrix to be decomposable in terms of its Hermite normal form. Specifically, to each integer matrix, we associate a symmetric integer matrix whose reducibility can be efficiently determined by elementary linear algebra techniques, and which completely determines the decomposability of the first one.

items.title: GV-subschemes and hyperelliptic Jacobians
items.summary: We provide a solution to the hyperelliptic Schottky problem: a principally polarized complex abelian variety whose theta divisor has singular locus of codimension three is a hyperelliptic Jacobian. As a key step towards this criterion for hyperelliptic Jacobians, we prove a conjecture of Pareschi and Popa which predicts that if the ideal sheaf $I_X$ of a subscheme $X$ of an indecomposable PPAV $(A, Θ)$ satisfies that $I_X(2Θ)$ is IT$_0$, then $X$ is a GV-subscheme. As a corollary of the main result, the base scheme of an ample line bundle on a complex abelian variety is generically reduced along every irreducible component of codimension $2$, confirming a conjecture of Debarre. This corollary completes the algebro-geometry proof by Arbarello-Codogni-Pareschi in \cite{ACP21, ACP25} of Novikov's conjecture, which characterizes Jacobians via the KP equation.

items.title: Statistical guarantees for signature kernel ridge regression
items.summary: Path signatures are a standard tool for learning functionals on path space. The main underpinnings of their application are universal approximation results. For a wide range of function classes on path space, these results state that any function in such a class can be approximated arbitrarily well by a linear functional of the path signature. Hence, linear functionals of the signature are in principle expressive enough for learning functions on path space. Nonetheless, these results do not provide insights into the statistical question of how much data is needed to identify a suitable signature functional. In this work, we study this question in the framework of kernel ridge regression with the signature kernel. The target is the conditional expectation $\E[Y|X]$, where $X$ is the observed path and $Y$ is a real-valued response. Under different assumptions on the moments of the signature kernel and the response, we provide finite-sample and consistency guarantees for the method. We supplement our theoretical analysis with numerical experiments that illustrate our results.

items.title: Poissonian Pair Correlation and Discrepancy Rates
items.summary: We prove the existence of a sequence in $[0,1)$ with Poissonian pair correlation (PPC) and optimal-order star discrepancy $D_N^*=O((\log N)/N)$, and further give a deterministic construction by applying a conditional-expectation rule to a nested dyadic random model. We also show that PPC imposes no universal discrepancy decay rate: for every positive sequence $ρ_N\to0$, there exists a PPC sequence with $D_N^*/ρ_N\to\infty$. Under suitable regularity and growth assumptions, we realize prescribed discrepancy asymptotics, including $D_N^*\sim c_βN^{-β}$ for every $0<β<1$, with $c_β>0$. We further construct a PPC sequence satisfying $D_N^*\asymp(\log N)/N$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

items.title: Traveling waves of NLS system arising in optical material without Galilean symmetry
items.summary: We study a nonlinear Schrödinger (NLS) system with cubic interactions arising in nonlinear optics, focusing on how the absence of Galilean symmetry affects solution dynamics. In the mass-critical case, we establish a new global existence result that contrasts with classical results. By exploiting the properties of traveling solitary waves, we obtain a condition on the initial data that relaxes the standard sharp assumptions. We also characterize the high-frequency limit of these traveling solitary waves as the frequency $ω$ tends to infinity.

items.title: Ehrhart Series and Transfer Matrices for Period-Two Polytopes with Consecutive Inequalities
items.summary: We study a family of period-two polytopes that can be naturally realized as lattice polytopes. In contrast to polytopes defined by a uniform system of inequalities, this family is characterized by consecutive coordinate inequalities whose bounds alternate between $s+1$ and $s$. The lattice points of these polytopes admit an explicit transfer-matrix formulation, which provides an effective framework for their enumeration and analysis. Furthermore, by considering fixed dilations, we investigate the associated dimensional generating functions and derive rational forms for the generating functions of the lattice points in the $m$-th dilates of the polytopes.

items.title: A solution to Petty's polar projection problem
items.summary: In 1971, Petty asked whether a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\geqslant 3$, must be an ellipsoid if its projection body is a dilate of its polar. In this paper, we give an affirmative answer to this question.

items.title: Improved Berezin--Li--Yau Bounds for Dirichlet Eigenvalues via Fourier Coupling and Frequency Concentration
items.summary: Let $0<λ_1\leqλ_2\leq\cdots$ be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of an open set $Ω\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$. We develop two Fourier-space refinements of the Berezin--Li--Yau argument. For every finite-measure open set, coordinate commutator identities and coupled scalar--vector projections lead to a one-dimensional variational constant $C_n^{\mathrm{new}}$ and the individual bound \[ λ_k\geq C_n^{\mathrm{new}}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{2/n}, \qquad \frac{n}{n+2}<c_n^{\mathrm{env}}<C_n^{\mathrm{new}}<1. \] Here $n/(n+2)$ is the classical Li--Yau individual coefficient and $c_n^{\mathrm{env}}$ is the coefficient associated with the uncoupled scalar envelope developed in our previous paper. Thus the displayed strict hierarchy separates the gain of the scalar energy envelope from the further gain supplied by the commutator coupling. For bounded open sets, a frequency-concentration operator, its first two traces, and the Ky Fan principle force Fourier mass outside the Li--Yau filling ball. A two-region bathtub argument then gives \[ \sum_{j=1}^kλ_j \geq \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω) \frac{n}{n+2}(2π)^2ω_n^{-2/n} |Ω|^{-2/n}k^{1+2/n}, \qquad \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)>1, \] where $\mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)$ is strictly decreasing in $k$ and converges to one, and \[ \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(Ω)-1\geq \frac{n+2}{2(n+1)^2} \left(\frac{ω_{n-1}}{ω_n}\right)^2 \left(\frac34\right)^{n-1}k^{-2/n}. \] Thus the sharp leading term in the Berezin--Li--Yau sum is supplemented by an explicit positive, volume-only correction of order $k$. Apart from boundedness in the concentration argument, no boundary regularity, convexity, or connectedness is assumed. These improvements do not prove Pólya's conjecture: the individual coefficient is below one, and the sum multiplier tends to one.

items.title: High-Dimensional Gaussian and Bootstrap Approximation: Near $1/\sqrt{n}$ Rates with General Covariance
items.summary: We consider Berry-Esseen bounds over rectangles for sums of $n$ random vectors in $\mathbb{R}^p$ that are i.i.d. A longstanding open question in high-dimensional probability and statistics is whether bounds of order $1/\sqrt n$ are attainable up to factors of $\log(pn)$ when the population covariance matrix is unrestricted. We answer this question affirmatively, provided that the random vectors have sub-Gaussian entries with non-zero variance. In addition, we provide analogous results for bootstrap approximation and Gaussian comparison, which make use of a special discrepancy measure between covariance matrices that enables improvement with respect to prior work. Taking an approach based on interpolation, the novel aspects of the proofs deal with bounding the interpolation derivatives in a way that is not sensitive to the covariance structure.

items.title: A converse to Littlewood-type theorem for random Dirichlet series
items.summary: This article investigates random Dirichlet series within the framework of Hardy and mixed norm spaces of Dirichlet series. For randomization methods by sequences of non-constant independent and identically distributed random variables, we completely characterize when the random symbol space of the Hardy space $\mathscr{H}^p$ (respectively, the mixed norm space $\mathscr{H}^{p,q}_α$) coincides with $\mathscr{H}^2$ (respectively, $\mathscr{H}^{2,q}_α$). We also obtain some integrability results when Dirichlet series belong to the corresponding random symbol spaces. The same methods also yield a complete characterization for mixed norm spaces on the unit disk in the range $0<q<4$, closing the gap between previously known necessary and sufficient conditions.

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions to semilinear elliptic problems on the exterior of a unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$
items.summary: We study the problem \begin{equation}\notag \begin{cases} - Δu &= λK(x) f(u) \hspace{.1cm} \mbox { in } B_1 ^c, \\ u(x)&=0 \hspace{1.5cm} \mbox { on } \partial B_1, \end{cases} \end{equation} where $λ$ is a positive parameter, $B_1^c:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^2:|x|>1\}$ is the exterior of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^2$, $K:B_1^c\rightarrow (0,\infty)$ is a $C^1$ radial function and $f:[0,\infty)\rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ is a $C^1$ concave function which is sublinear at infinity such that $f(0)<0$. We establish the existence and uniqueness of non negative radial solutions for large values of parameter $λ$. Moreover, we prove certain qualitative properties of nonnegative radial solutions for a class of problems in dimension 2. In contrast to the case $n\geq3$, where positive solutions decay to zero at infinity, we prove that non negative solutions are positive, radially increasing with the limit existing at infinity.

items.title: Yang-Mills-Higgs Limits of Reflexive Higgs Sheaves
items.summary: For stable Higgs bundles, Hermitian-Einstein metrics can be obtained as limits of the Yang-Mills-Higgs (Y-M-H) flow. We study the algebraic structure of subsequential limits of this flow for reflexive Higgs sheaves over compact Kähler manifolds, without assuming stability. We prove that the limiting reflexive Higgs sheaf is isomorphic to the double dual of the graded sheaf associated with the Harder-Narasimhan-Seshadri filtration of the initial sheaf.

items.title: The speed of convergence for propagation of chaos in the mean-field Ising model
items.summary: We derive sharp relative-entropy asymptotics for increasing propagation of chaos in the Curie--Weiss model at zero external field. For every fixed inverse temperature $0<β<1$, the relative entropy of a $k$-spin marginal with respect to the symmetric product measure is $$ \frac{β^2}{4(1-β)^2}\frac{k(k-1)}{N^2}+o\left(\frac{k^2}{N^2}\right),\qquad k=o(N). $$ At the critical inverse temperature $β=1$, the rate changes to $α_{\mathrm c}^2 k(k-1)/(4N)+o(k^2/N)$ in the regime $k=o(\sqrt N)$, where $α_{\mathrm c}$ is the second moment of the limiting quartic law of the rescaled magnetization. We also obtain asymptotics for sequences $β_N\uparrow1$ that interpolate between these two regimes. Crucially, the proof reveals that the pair correlations determine the leading correction to the likelihood ratio, providing precise control of both the chi-square divergence and relative entropy.

items.title: Well-Posedness of Semimartingale Optimal Transport with Partial Marginal Constraints for Model Calibration
items.summary: We study the well-posedness and stability of a semimartingale optimal transport problem with partial marginal constraints at several maturities, motivated by the calibration of financial models to finitely many option prices. We connect its probabilistic and Eulerian formulations within the Benamou--Brenier framework. Under convex-duality assumptions, we establish strong duality for every price vector in the extended-value sense and existence of a primal optimizer whenever the value is finite. Under additional PDE assumptions, we establish dual attainment on the relative interior of the admissible price set, together with uniqueness of the primal optimizer. Under further non-degeneracy assumptions, we show that this price set has nonempty interior, on which the dual optimizer is unique and depends locally Lipschitz continuously on the prices. The analysis combines convex methods with regularity and local strong convexity results for Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman solution maps established in a companion paper. For a fixed deterministic initial state, we also prove continuity of the optimal law on path space in the adapted Wasserstein distance of order two as prices vary within this interior. This stability concerns the optimizer over the full admissible class of semimartingale laws, allowing characteristics that depend on the past. The framework accommodates bounded uniformly continuous payoffs, including European puts in log-price coordinates, without payoff regularization or spatial truncation.

items.title: Short permutation pattern waves: The complete length-five classification
items.summary: For a permutation pi in Sk, a pi-wave is an increasing sequence of integers whose consecutive gaps have relative order pi. Let g(pi, n) be the maximum cardinality of a pi-wave-free subset of [n], and let P(pi, r) be the least integer N such that every r-coloring of [N] contains a monochromatic pi-wave. We determine the asymptotic orders of both functions for every permutation of length at most five. Existing upper bounds and weak-wave constructions provide sharp bounds for all but eight length-five patterns in S_5. For these eight exceptional alternating patterns, we establish g(pi, n) = Theta((log n)squared) and P(pi, r) = Theta(r(log r)squared).

items.title: The periodic Wulff problem in two dimensions
items.summary: We characterize the minimizers of the anisotropic perimeter in the two-dimensional flat torus under an area constraint. We show that, as the prescribed area increases, global minimizers undergo two phase transitions, changing from a droplet (a rescaled Wulff shape) to a flat band wrapping around the torus in a preferred direction determined by the anisotropy (lamellar phase), and finally to a bubble (the complement of a reflected and rescaled Wulff shape). The transition thresholds are given explicitly in terms of the area and the lattice width of the Wulff shape. For certain non-symmetric surface tensions, the lamellar phase is absent altogether. Finally, we characterize the surface tensions for which further minimizers appear: this may happen only in the lamellar regime, and exactly when the Wulff shape has a corner whose normal cone contains, in its interior, a direction realizing the lattice width; in this case there are infinitely many minimizers.

items.title: Chow Stability of Polarized K3 Surfaces with ADE singularities
items.summary: The asymptotic Chow stability of smooth polarized K3 surfaces is known through the existence of Ricci-flat metrics and Donaldson's theorem. We give a purely algebraic proof and extend the result to polarized K3 surfaces with at worst ADE singularities. The proof gives a uniform effective bound for the exponent, depending only on the degree of the polarization. Following the approach of Mumford and Morrison, we establish quantitative estimates for linear systems and their contributions to Chow weights, without restrictions on the Picard number.

items.title: $(r,s)$-Designs in the Nonbinary Johnson Scheme: Constructions and Linear Codes
items.summary: Using factorizations of complete graphs, we determine the existence conditions for $(2,1)$-designs in the nonbinary Johnson scheme where each $3$-element subset appears exactly once as a support. Furthermore, by utilizing large sets of Steiner triple systems, we construct designs with index $1$ that cannot be obtained from the known construction combining block designs and orthogonal arrays. For linear codes, we express multiplicative character sums over specified nonzero coordinates as sums over the codewords of the dual code. Using this identity along with the rank of a matrix formed by Krawtchouk polynomials, we provide a sufficient condition for the set of all codewords of a given weight to form an $(r,s)$-design. In this matrix, we can utilize not only the rows corresponding to weights absent from the code, but also the rows corresponding to weights for which the set of codewords already forms a design. Moreover, let $q>2$ be a prime power, and let $0 \neq C \subsetneq \mathbb{F}_q^n$ be a linear code with exactly two nonzero weights. For $t \geq 2$, the set of all codewords of weight $w \geq t$ forms a non-empty $(t,t)$-design if and only if the dual minimum distance is at least $t+2$. Consequently, this provides a negative answer to the Wu--Zhou problem concerning two-weight codes with a dual minimum distance of $3$.

items.title: The bias interval of the elephant random walk
items.summary: Guérin, Laulin, Raschel, and Simon conjectured that the initial biases giving the superdiffusive elephant random walk a bimodal limit law form an interval centered at one half, and they described the problem as challenging. We prove this. For every superdiffusive memory, strongly biased starts are unimodal, and the limit density has two local maxima exactly when the bias lies in a proper open interval. Outside it, including its endpoints, the density has a unique local maximum. The interval is nonempty exactly above a single memory threshold, numerically about $0.6688$, whose uniqueness follows from a positive-weight integral for the central curvature of the fair-start density. We control sign changes in the finite walk's first and second differences, including those created at the boundary, and pass them to the limit. The bias boundary is continuous and tends to zero at least quadratically fast as memory tends to one.

items.title: Fano-Enriques threefolds of Fano index $>1$
items.summary: We study $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano threefolds of Fano index greater than $1$ whose Weil divisor class group has nontrivial torsion. We give a complete list of their possible numerical types: there are $176$ of them, which refine to $182$ possible graded Hilbert series. At least $40$ numerical types are realised: $27$ by quotients of weighted complete intersections by cyclic groups, twelve by quotients of threefolds of codimension $4$ or $5$ and one by a quotient of the del Pezzo threefold of degree $5$. Seventy-two numerical types are shown not to occur. In particular the torsion subgroup need not have prime order, and the Weil and $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano indices can be $(1,2)$, $(1,3)$ or $(1,4)$.

items.title: On Samuels' Conjecture
items.summary: Let $0\leqμ_1\leq\cdots\leqμ_n$ and let $λ>\sum_{i=1}^nμ_i$. Let $X_1,...,X_n$ be independent nonnegative random variables satisfying $\mathbb{E}X_i=μ_i$, and write $D_i := λ-\sum_{k=1}^{i-1}μ_k$ for $1\leq i\leq n$. We prove that $$ \inf_{X_1,...,X_n} \mathbb{P}\left( \sum_{i=1}^nX_i<λ\right) = \min_{1\leq i\leq n} \prod_{j=i}^n \left( 1-\frac{μ_j}{D_i} \right). $$ The bound is sharp and is attained. This proves Samuels' conjecture. Feige's conjecture is thereby resolved, since it follows immediately from the equal-means case. The proof is self-contained.

items.title: Non-vanishing of central $\rm GL_3$ L-values in the level aspect
items.summary: We study non-vanishing of central standard $L$-values of spherical cuspidal $\mathrm{GL}_3$ newforms of prime level. A logarithmic Möbius mollifier with finite inverse Euler factors, combined with a conjugate term from the functional equation, gives a non-vanishing harmonic proportion of at least $1/2-\varepsilon$ for every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large prime levels. The required mixed moment is evaluated by an asymmetric approximate functional equation.

items.title: Explicit Planar Finite Element Elasticity Complexes and $C^1$ Elements on Barycentric Refinements
items.summary: We give a closed-form realization of the finite element elasticity complex associated with the Arnold--Douglas--Gupta family on barycentric refinements. Their construction implies the existence of minimal $C^1$ potential spaces, but does not provide explicit general-degree scalar enrichments. On each macrotriangle, we derive three divergence-free stress enrichments and their Airy potentials. For every degree $q\geq4$, the resulting potential space enriches $\mathbb P_q$ by three explicit functions. A geometric decomposition yields unisolvent degrees of freedom and $C^1$ assembly without vertex supersmoothness. The space attains the dimension bound for macroelements containing $\mathbb P_q$ with full polynomial boundary trace freedom. Its Airy image is the divergence-free subspace of the corresponding stress space, and global assembly gives an exact discrete elasticity complex on simply connected domains. The low-order spaces $U_2$ and $U_3$ recover the reduced and full Hsieh--Clough--Tocher spaces, respectively.

items.title: Goodman-type lower bounds for graph homomorphism densities
items.summary: For a finite graph $H$ with $v(H)$ vertices, chromatic number $χ(H)$, and chromatic polynomial $P_H$, define $Φ_H(p)=(1-p)^{v(H)}P_H((1-p)^{-1})$. This polynomial interpolates the homomorphism densities of $H$ in balanced complete multipartite graphons. We study the lower bound $t(H,W)\geΦ_H(p)$ on the homomorphism density of $H$ in graphons $W$ of edge density $p>1-1/(χ(H)-1)$, which generalises Goodman's triangle bound. We prove the inequality for chordal graphs whose maximal cliques have equal size, for trivially perfect graphs, and for joins of a clique and an odd cycle. The proofs use entropy along clique trees and a convexity criterion for adding a universal vertex. We also prove that a nonbipartite graph satisfies the inequality at all sufficiently high edge densities if and only if its girth is odd. For a graph on $n$ vertices whose girth is odd, the bound holds whenever $p>1-(72n^{12})^{-1}$. The proof combines Whitney's forest expansion with a spectral comparison of cycle densities. Finally, among the $117$ nonbipartite graphs on at most six vertices with no isolated vertices or isolated edges, exactly $94$ satisfy the bound. The main results are formally verified in Lean 4.

items.title: A constrained Onsager variational framework for parametric approximations of Willmore and Helfrich flows
items.summary: We develop a constrained Onsager variational framework for parametric finite element approximations of Willmore and Helfrich flows. The weak curvature relation is used as a PDE constraint to express the first variation of the bending energy in curvature-vector form. Onsager's principle then combines this variation with dissipation based on the normal velocity, while an independent relaxed minimal-deformation-rate (relaxed-MDR) constraint selects the tangential velocity. The resulting mixed formulation admits a semidiscretization by continuous piecewise linear elements that satisfies an exact energy-dissipation law and exactly preserves area and volume when the corresponding constraints are imposed. The framework accommodates constant spontaneous curvature and applies to both closed surfaces and open surfaces with fixed boundaries under Navier or clamped conditions. We also propose a linearly implicit fully discrete scheme, prove its unique solvability, and present numerical experiments demonstrating convergence, energy decay, constraint preservation, and effective mesh redistribution.

items.title: High-Dimensional Online Calibration from Harmonic Weights
items.summary: We study the online calibration of multidimensional forecasts over an arbitrary convex set $Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d$ relative to an arbitrary error norm $\|\cdot\|_L$. For forecasting $d$ binary outcomes simultaneously ($Y=[0,1]^d$), we give the first algorithm that achieves $\varepsilon$-calibration in a number of rounds that is polynomial in $d$ for every fixed accuracy. It requires $d^{O(1/\varepsilon)}$ rounds, exponentially improving the dimension dependence of previous bounds. For multi-class forecasting ($Y=Δ_d$), we obtain the same $d^{O(1/\varepsilon)}$ rate, improving the $d^{\widetilde{O}(1/\varepsilon^2)}$ bounds of Peng and Fishelson, Golowich, Mohri, and Schneider. Our algorithm is simple: on each round, it outputs a harmonically weighted distribution over harmonically smoothed past outcomes. The same algorithm works for every forecast set and error norm. More generally, it achieves $\varepsilon$-calibration after $\exp(O(γ(Y,L)/\varepsilon))$ rounds, where $γ(Y,L)$ is a geometric parameter defined by a matrix discrepancy problem. The harmonic weights are motivated by the fact that the discrete Hilbert transform matrix achieves the optimal discrepancy up to a universal constant, simultaneously for every $L$. This optimality result may be of independent interest. The same harmonic responses also yield an algorithm for high-dimensional Blackwell approachability. Its guarantees are governed by a sharpened geometric parameter that captures the joint geometry of the outcome and action sets.

items.title: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
items.summary: Monitoring maritime activities is important for safety and security, particularly for detecting illegal activities, but remains challenging due to the size and complexity of the maritime domain. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is commonly used for this purpose, despite its known vulnerabilities. In contrast, space-based radio frequency (RF) observations provide an independent source of vessel activity but lack ship identification and therefore cannot identify vessels on their own. Following the CRISP-DM process, this study applies a Pair Hidden Markov Model (PHMM) to align individual RF detections with AIS trajectories, using temporal and spatial information while modeling noise and timing discrepancies. We evaluate it on NOAA AIS data with synthetic RF detections against nearest-neighbor baselines and analyze its errors with bias tests on trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity and AIS--RF distance. The length-corrected Forward score reaches a top-1 precision of $0.7776$ on the validation split of multi-candidate detections, where errors are possible, and an AUC of $0.637$ for detecting dark vessels among the detections that pass the prefilter. With a single RF detection, the score mostly reflects the AIS trajectory itself, and its errors favor longer and more stationary trajectories. A log-odds score, which compares the full model with a null model without match transitions, raises precision to $0.8580$ and AUC to $0.852$. Its length-corrected variant no longer shows a significant bias towards stationary trajectories and short inter-message distances, but still favors candidates farther from the RF detection. A time-weighted nearest-neighbor baseline without fitting remains ahead (precision $0.9013$, AUC $0.904$), so this single-detection, hand-designed PHMM formulation approaches but does not beat it.

items.title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
items.summary: Recent advances in speech neuroprostheses have enabled new communication avenues for people who have lost the ability to speak due to neurological illness or injury. These systems can decode neural activity during attempted speech into text by relying on language priors to achieve high decoding accuracy. This performance currently comes at the cost of using a compute-intensive language modeling stack, presenting a major bottleneck for real-world use. Further, current language models incur highly variable and disruptive inference latencies, limiting communication throughput and preventing users from reliably participating in natural conversation. We introduce FETTUCCINE, an end-to-end brain-to-text framework that leverages the speed and portability of automatic speech recognition (ASR) models to address the aforementioned practical challenges, while achieving usable (<10%) word error rates (WER), efficient adaptation to neural non-stationarities, and reliable performance on mobile devices. When evaluated using publicly available data from an intracortical speech neuroprosthesis user, FETTUCCINE outperforms previous end-to-end methods, achieving as low as 4.39% WER. Most notably, our models successfully run on a commercially-available mobile device with throughput reaching up to 370x real-time, providing the first demonstration of brain-to-text decoding on a mobile device. We also show that our models can be successfully finetuned to extend usable performance to future days. Beyond performance, our approach enables localization of the neural features most relevant for decoding via gradient-based saliency maps, which we show align with well-established physiological priors across different ASR model families. Taken together, our results show that FETTUCCINE overcomes core infrastructural and computational barriers, yielding a new class of portable brain-to-text communication.

items.title: Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots
items.summary: Robot-use agents (RUAs) have emerged as a promising approach to general-purpose robot control. However, strong performance has so far been achieved only by frontier proprietary models such as GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.2, whereas open-weight models remain substantially less capable. We show that an open-weight 27B reasoning model can be trained to use real robots natively through reinforcement learning, entirely in simulation and without demonstrations. Like a computer-use agent (CUA), the model observes the environment, reasons in a chain of thought, and generates the next end-effector pose, without any harness. We build a Post-training Engine for Agentic Robotics (PEAR) and use it to train the model on simulated robot tasks at scale with robot-use reinforcement learning (RURL), mirroring how frontier models acquire computer use. We find that the skills acquired in simulation generalize well beyond the training tasks: they transfer to an unseen robot, to the real world, and to novel instructions. After training on LIBERO and RoboDojo in simulation, the model succeeds in 60% of our trials on a real dual-arm robot, whereas the base model succeeds in none. On LIBERO, training raises the success rate from 1.6% to 74.4%, approaching GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at maximum reasoning effort. Compared with $π_{0.5}$, a vision-language-action model fine-tuned on demonstrations, our model is substantially more robust to changes in the task itself. On LIBERO-Pro, $π_{0.5}$ succeeds in only 0.75% of episodes when assigned a new task in a familiar scene whereas our model succeeds in 57.4%. Finally, the model retains its general capabilities, with no measurable degradation on nine reasoning, coding and vision benchmarks. These results highlight robot-use reinforcement learning as a promising component of foundation-model post-training.

items.title: BAL: Bidirectional Autoregression in Latent Space for Learning Human Movement Representations
items.summary: Learning semantically meaningful human movement representations from 3D pose sequences is essential for human behavior modeling. Existing self-supervised methods derive supervision from artificial assumptions, e.g., invariance to augmentation within a certain range or recoverability of masked regions at a certain temporal scale, introducing heuristic hyperparameters that make the learned semantics sensitive to their settings. We propose BAL, a self-supervised framework that instead exploits supervision intrinsic to human movement: the natural ordering structure of everyday behavior. BAL autoregressively predicts in a semantically abstract latent space, analogous to how humans anticipate others' actions rather than their precise joint configurations. Bidirectional autoregressive prediction, both forward and backward in time, fully leverages these ordering constraints while enabling representation extraction using both past and future context at inference. To suppress representation collapse, BAL decomposes each prediction target into a global component capturing sequence-level semantics and a local component capturing context-independent movement. We prove that the local targets retain nontrivial angular diversity unless the representations are completely collapsed, preserving a meaningful training signal. Experiments on large-scale datasets demonstrate that BAL's representations are highly effective for motion captioning, forecasting, and interpolation, outperforming baselines on most evaluation metrics.

items.title: ArchSpace: Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing LLM Architecture Research
items.summary: Model architecture shapes the scaling behavior, training efficiency, and inference cost of LLMs, making it a central focus of both industry and academia. In industry, teams such as those behind DeepSeek, Qwen, and Kimi routinely introduce architectural innovations, yet public reports rarely document which ideas succeeded, which were abandoned, and why. In academia, limited compute and inconsistent baselines often restrict evaluations to small-scale, single-point comparisons, making it difficult to establish whether improvements hold at larger scales or translate into broader impact. ArchSpace addresses both gaps as a public platform for Recording, Reviewing, and Referencing Architecture Research: each proposal is recorded with its experiments and reasoning, reviewed by the community, and referenced by later work. To evaluate ideas before costly large-scale training, ArchSpace leverages scaling laws to predict model loss at larger scales from smaller experiments, a practice widely adopted in industry. We provide initial references that make the platform usable: Qwen3.5 and OLMo3 baselines, fitted scaling laws, and a reusable training recipe. Ideas validated through this review can in turn become new baselines, and ArchSpace thereby aims to broaden the range of ideas that shape the next generation of models.

items.title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
items.summary: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks across five tracks: reading, fixing and writing weights, recognizing edits that are impossible, and data-free compression. The networks whose weights the LLMs read and edit range from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models. Experimental benchmark results show that frontier agents can already read small networks and write working control policies without ever running them, but cannot yet patch language models, compress them without data, or tell an impossible edit from a hard one. On all 42 tasks, Claude Opus 5.5 reaches a macro score of 0.535 (Sonnet 5.5 0.466, Haiku 5.5 0.402, DeepSeek v4-flash 0.215); on the 38 tasks it was run on, GPT-6.1-sol reaches 0.568 against Opus's 0.546. Code, the task registry, our OS-level sandbox harness, and the live leaderboard are publicly available at https://github.com/Aayush-Marasini/WeightBench.

items.title: Restoring Diversity in Distilled Image and Video Generators by Probing Activations
items.summary: Distilling diffusion models into few-step student models substantially reduces sampling latency, but induces severe diversity collapse: samples generated from different random seeds show minimal variation. In this work, we investigate the root cause of this failure by probing the internal representations of student models relative to their teachers. We find that distilled students maintain total activation variance comparable to their teachers, but concentrate it into substantially fewer directions. This directional collapse is localized to an identifiable intermediate block at the initial denoising step. Consequently, diversity collapse stems from a misallocation of activation variance rather than an inherent loss of generative capacity. Guided by this finding, we propose ReDiverse to reinstate the missing variance directions. At training time, ReDiverse-FT fine-tunes a lightweight adapter that regresses student activations onto the teacher's, reviving the teacher's feature variance characteristic. At inference time, ReDiverse-TF introduces a training-free mechanism that steers activations along precomputed teacher principal directions. Across image and video distillation benchmarks, ReDiverse consistently restores sample diversity while preserving generation quality, further supported by the user study.

items.title: From Reading Code to Reading Spec: A Verified Layer for LLM-Driven Codebase Maintenance
items.summary: The rapid growth of LLM-generated code increases software complexity and the maintenance burden on engineers. While LLMs offer a potential automated alternative, this structural complexity hinders their ability to manage codebases directly. We introduce the Provable Representation Of Original Functionality (PROOF), which manages codebases indirectly via structured specifications. To enable full-lifecycle codebase management strictly through these specifications, PROOF abstracts codebase topology into a hierarchical natural-language representation. To establish absolute trust, the system proves semantic equivalence by reconstructing source code exclusively from this specification. This verified foundation drives maintenance requests, executing code modifications while synchronously updating itself to prevent semantic drift. Experiments on real-world repositories confirm the effectiveness of these specifications.

items.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
items.summary: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization to identify design choices that balance generation quality and computational efficiency. The resulting JVT design achieves generation quality competitive with latent diffusion baselines in both class-conditioned and unconditional settings. The pixel-space formulation of JVT also naturally supports joint generation of pixel-aligned modalities. We demonstrate this capability through camera-conditioned RGB-disparity generation, which improves camera following relative to RGB-only baselines and yields explicit scene geometry without an additional reconstruction model at inference. These results highlight the potential of simple DiT-style Transformers for pixel-space video diffusion, and we hope our findings offer useful insights and practical guidance for future research.

items.title: Bidirectional Information Flow (BIF) - A Sample Efficient Hierarchical Gaussian Process for Bayesian Optimization
items.summary: Hierarchical Gaussian Process (H-GP) models divide problems into different subtasks, allowing for different components to address each part, making them well-suited for problems with inherent compositional structure. However, existing H-GP frameworks typically employ one-way information sharing - either top-down or bottom-up - which limits sample efficiency and slows convergence. We propose Bidirectional Information Flow (BIF), which establishes continuous two-way communication. BIF retains the modular structure of hierarchical models - the parent conditions its own posterior on child summaries, treating them as structured priors - while introducing top-down feedback to softly decompose environment observations from the parent into sub-responses. This mutual exchange improves sample efficiency, enables robust training, and allows modular reuse of learned subtask models. We prove analytically the regret of a GP with a learned kernel scales linearly with the mismatch to the true kernel, tightening in the hierarchical case to the sum of child-level errors. Ablation shows removing the downward pathway collapses child $R^2$ by up to 58%. Across synthetic, neurostimulation, and HPO benchmarks, BIF achieves up to $4\times$ higher parent $R^2$ and roughly 100% AUC improvement over vanilla GPBO, and outperforms or is the runner-up in 38/40 tests compared to the state-of-the-art baselines while supporting modular child transfer to novel composite tasks.

items.title: Tracing 3D Anatomy in 2D Strokes: Can Projection-Derived Masks Replace 3D Segmentation for Cervical Spine Fracture Recognition?
items.summary: Cervical spine fractures require rapid and accurate diagnosis, yet automatic CT interpretation remains challenging as subtle injuries must be assessed across large 3D volumes. We ask whether full 3D vertebra segmentation is necessary for fracture recognition, or whether vertebra masks approximated from 2D projections preserve sufficient diagnostic context. In the proposed multi-stage pipeline, a YOLOv8 detector localizes the cervical spine from multi-view variance projections (3D mean Intersection over Union 94.45%). Multi-label vertebra segmentation is performed with a DenseNet121-Unet on energy-based sagittal and coronal projections (mean Dice 87.86%). The predicted 2D masks are back-projected and fused into approximate 3D masks per vertebra to extract volumes of interest from the original CT, which are analyzed by an ensemble of 2.5D spatio-sequential CNN-Transformer models. On the full RSNA 2022 cohort at native prevalence (2,019 patients, five-fold cross-validation), the pipeline yields vertebra-level and patient-level F1-scores of 68.15% and 82.28%, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 91.63% and 90.95%, and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC) of 75.64% and 92.00%. With the classifier architecture fixed, replacing 3D-segmentation masks by projection-derived masks changed vertebra-level and patient-level AUPRC by +1.03 and +0.65 points, and the pipeline differed from the reproduced RSNA 2022 winning solution by -0.55 and +0.15 points. No AUPRC difference was statistically significant, and fold-wise 95% confidence intervals excluded vertebra-level losses larger than 1.46 and 2.81 points, respectively. Explainability and interobserver analyses examine reliability. Projection-based mask approximation is therefore a viable proxy for 3D vertebra segmentation in cervical fracture recognition.

items.title: Modeling the Frictional Contact of Continuum Robots with Environments through Linear Complementarity Problem
items.summary: Accurate friction modeling in continuum robots is essential for precise motion control and path planning. However, current approaches make predictions only for the mechanism's internal friction that is limited by the boundary forces of the Coulomb friction cone, which fail to characterize the static friction and motion hysteresis. In this paper, we propose a novel friction model based on complementarity constraints under the Coulomb friction assumption. This model predicts various friction effects caused by environmental interactions, including both static and sliding frictions and hysteresis behavior, as well as the corresponding robot deformation induced by these interactions, which are crucial for the practical motion planning and control of continuum robots. Additionally, real-time implementation of this model can be achieved, meeting the demand for computational efficiency in robotic applications. Experimental validations demonstrated that this model is able to reduce the maximum tip position error from 45.4 mm in the frictionless model to 5.85 mm in our friction-included model with a 287.9 mm-long tendon-driven continuum robot.

items.title: Shortcut Mitigation via Spurious-Positive Samples
items.summary: Shortcut mitigation strategies commonly rely on training data annotations, group-balanced held-out data or the presence of all groups, i.e., all combinations of (spurious) attributes and classes, in the training data. However, these requirements are rarely met in practice. We instead propose a method for targeted model analysis to identify a small set of instances in which the model relies on spurious attributes. Using that set and following ``this feature should not be used for prediction'' reasoning, we identify highly relevant neurons in an intermediate layer and regularize their impact. This ensures that models learn to depend on informative features rather than being right for the wrong reasons, thereby improving robustness without requiring additional balanced held-out data or annotations.

items.title: Tight Bounds for k-Median++ and Improved Bounds for k-Means++
items.summary: The popular $k$-means++ algorithm, or $D^\ell$-sampling, is a fundamental primitive in both the theory and practice of clustering. In the bi-criteria setting, the algorithm samples $k+Δ$ centers ($Δ\ge0$), and its cost is compared with the optimum using $k$ centers. Despite extensive study over the past two decades, its exact approximation ratio and tight bi-criteria guarantees remain unknown. We give a unified analysis for every distance exponent $\ell>0$, every $k\ge1$, and every $Δ\ge0$. For metric $k$-median, our bounds are tight for all $k$ and $Δ$. Without extra centers, the exact approximation ratio is $2(1+H_{k-1})$ (also in Euclidean space), improving the previous upper bound by a factor of $2$ ($H_j$ denotes the $j$th harmonic number). This tight analysis reveals that even one extra center improves the approximation ratio by an additive $Θ(\log\log k)$, whereas previous bounds show no improvement. For every $\ell>0$, our analysis gives upper bounds with the same dependence on $k$ and $Δ$ as our tight bound for metric $k$-median, with leading constants depending only on $\ell$ and whether the metric is Euclidean. Beyond the improved dependence on $Δ$, our leading constants are smaller than those in previous analyses. In particular, for the widely used Euclidean $k$-means objective, our upper bound without extra centers is $(1+\varphi)(1+H_{k-1})$, where $\varphi\approx1.618$ is the golden ratio, improving upon the previous constant of $5$. With oversampling, a constant fraction of extra centers is known to provide a constant-factor approximation. For example, with $10\%$ extra centers, our guarantee is $5.7$, compared with the best previous guarantee of $25.9$.

items.title: Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Demonstrations are an effective way to accelerate single-agent reinforcement learning (RL), but extending this idea to multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) is non-trivial as it is difficult and often impossible for a single person to teleoperate multiple agents simultaneously. Round-Robin Behavior Cloning (R2BC) addresses this by letting a single demonstrator control one agent at a time while the others execute their current policies. However, the resulting imitation policies are limited by the quality of the demonstrations. We propose Imitation Bootstrapped Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (IBMARL), a framework that extends Imitation Bootstrapped Reinforcement Learning (IBRL) to cooperative teams and uses R2BC to train the imitation policies. At each time step, every agent receives one action proposal from its imitation policy and one from its RL policy, and an ensemble of centralized critics selects among the per-agent combinations of the two. A gated imitation penalty, a soft Q-filtered behavior cloning loss, regularizes each RL policy toward its imitation policy only where the critics value the imitation action more, so that after training each agent executes its RL policy alone, without the centralized critics. On four cooperative multi-agent RL benchmarks, IBMARL surpasses its imitation policies $2.6$-$4.2\times$ faster than demonstration-based baselines on two tasks, is the only method to surpass it on the other two, and exceeds the demonstrator itself on two of the four. With real human demonstrations IBMARL still surpasses imitation learning alone, and does so more than twice as fast as the best baseline.

items.title: Generating Concept Lexicalizations via Dictionary-Based Cross-Lingual Sense Projection
items.summary: We study the task of automatically expanding WordNet-style lexical resources to new languages through sense generation. We generate senses by associating target-language lemmas with existing lexical concepts via semantic projection. Given a sense-tagged English corpus and its translation, our method projects the annotated synsets onto aligned target-language tokens and assigns the corresponding lemmas to those synsets. To generate alignments and ensure their quality, we augment a pretrained base aligner with a bilingual dictionary, which is also used to filter incorrect sense projections. We evaluate the method on multiple languages, comparing it to prior methods, as well as dictionary-based and large language model baselines. Results show that the proposed project-and-filter strategy improves precision while remaining interpretable and resource- efficient. We release our code, documentation, and generated sense inventories at https://github.com/UAlberta-NLP/ExpandNet.

items.title: Elliptic Sampling: Optimal Interpolant Schedules for Gaussians and Beyond
items.summary: Generative modeling based on stochastic interpolants requires specifying two key choices: an interpolant schedule bridging the initial and target distributions, and an efficient discretization of the resulting probability-flow ODE. In this work, we introduce a new framework for joint schedule/discretization design based on the analyticity properties of the (complexified) ODE trajectories, which in turn ensure good numerical behavior. Our formulation can be solved exactly via conformal mapping, yielding a natural family of variance-preserving elliptic schedules, parametrized by Jacobi elliptic functions. Pairing an elliptic schedule with a tailored discretization, we obtain Zoloflow, a new sampling algorithm closely connected to Zolotarev's optimal rational function approximants. Crucially, both the elliptic schedule and Zoloflow explicitly incorporate the condition number $κ$ of the target distribution and reduce to the classical trig schedule in the limit $κ\rightarrow 1$. For Gaussian targets, Zoloflow achieves minimax optimality among all oblivious score-span algorithms, attaining total-variation error $\varepsilon$ using $Θ(\logκ\,\log(\sqrt d/\varepsilon))$ (exact) score queries. For the log-concave case, the elliptic schedule allows sampling with at most $\varepsilon$ 2-Wasserstein-error by requiring merely $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{d} \, \mathrm{polylog}(κ, 1/\varepsilon))$ score evaluations. Complementing these theoretical results, we empirically evaluate the elliptic schedule on general (non-log-concave) target distributions, including detailed comparisons with alternative schedule proposals on both synthetic benchmarks and existing image generation datasets.

items.title: Why Finite Intelligence Works in an Infinite World: A Mathematical Theory
items.summary: An information system often has to learn before it knows what it will be asked. A finite representation can succeed without recording an infinite environment in full when those asks share collective structure, rather than demand unrelated facts scattered arbitrarily across it. We formalize this phenomenon through future-task information, the minimum retained information needed to preserve decision value relative to the available evidence. A joint decision-regret state records posterior comparisons among actions for every permitted task. Under compactness assumptions, every retained representation admits a calibrated replacement based on this state, preserving all task regrets without increasing information; the resulting information-regret curve equals an operational coding rate. Two exact boundaries govern finite preservation: weak-star closure for a fixed action count, and the singular mass of the source-evidence law when all finite action menus are admitted. Collective structure determines information requirements beyond individual-question difficulty. Families with identical source laws, pairwise task metrics, and individual-task rates can have different high-resolution exponents. Covariance-identical coordinate and parity families have different exact rate-distortion curves, with optimal parity retention characterized by a sharp Fourier-entropy inequality. For balanced nested task families, refinement sizes and weighted reach determine the rate within an additive constant, attained by prefix coding under explicit decay conditions. Nonlinear learning and computational separations distinguish preservation from efficient discovery and use. The proposed mathematical theory identifies which shared decision requirements allow finite information to remain useful for infinitely many possible purposes.

items.title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
items.summary: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) increasingly relies on a harness, the scaffold around the model that decides what it sees of its own interaction and what guidance it receives. Most existing approaches train under a hand-written harness that stays fixed throughout.
