Many video inpainters also depend on future frames and cannot operate online. We present TransGHOST, a causal reference-guided reconstruction pipeline whose non-generative safe mode operates in real time. Every restored value is obtained by resampling a recorded frame using geometric transforms fitted only to visible regions. The system provides per-pixel confidence and provenance and marks unsupported pixels as abstentions. We evaluate TransGHOST on a new veterinary clinical corpus of canine cataract surgery with pixel-level instrument and anatomy labels. Only the occluded region is scored, and each scoring target is verified to differ from the reference supplied to the system. Safe mode reaches 31.89 dB masked PSNR and 0.915 masked SSIM at 51.7 ms median and 85.5 ms 95th-percentile latency. On a pre-declared held-out cohort using instrument cutouts excluded from segmentation training, it reaches 29.83 dB masked PSNR, while matched-mask evaluation on validation shows a 3.45 dB advantage over LaMa. Region-aware reference selection improves masked PSNR by 3.60 dB over recency when candidate references can themselves be occluded. Reference-age analysis further defines the operating interval for the brief, repeated occlusions targeted by TransGHOST.

items.title: DiffusionSSD: Achieving Extreme Visual Compression with Dual-stage Diffusion and Cross-level Near-Data Processing
items.summary: Growing visual data overwhelms storage on resource-constrained edge devices, making compression essential. Traditional codecs offer inadequate rate-distortion performance, motivating the exploration of diffusion codecs. Diffusion codecs face two limitations: (1) At the algorithm level, diffusion decoders preserve perceptual quality under extreme compression, but require substantial computation. (2) At the architecture level, in NPU-centered devices, neural codecs occupy the NPU, interfering with other AI applications. Meanwhile, the complex codec pipeline incurs long I/O paths, leading to additional overhead and energy cost. To address these issues, we propose DiffusionSSD, a cross-level near-data processing framework for extreme visual data compression on edge devices, using an algorithm-architecture co-design method. Specifically, (1) at algorithm level, we present Dual-stage Diffusion, a lightweight solution tailored for diffusion codecs that employs patchification and single-step diffusion, reducing computation cost while preserving perceptual quality; (2) at architecture level, we introduce a Cross-level Near Data Processing architecture that integrates the proposed computational universal flash storage (cUFS) and LPDDR-PIM, enabling codecs to be entirely offloaded to data side while reducing visual-data movement and avoiding SoC redesign; (3) at system level, combining both the algorithm and the underlying architecture, we propose a Patch-Workload co-aware scheduling scheme to enable more efficient system-level execution. Experiments show that Dual-stage Diffusion maintains comparable perceptual quality while reducing computation cost by up to 92.7%. Compared with NPU+DRAM and near-data-processing design such as SmartSSD, cUFS+PIM improves coding throughput by 2.32 times and 2.91 times on average, respectively.

items.title: System-wide Dynamic Performance Metric for Converter-Dominated Power Systems
items.summary: Fast controller dynamics in Inverter-Based Resources (IBRs)-dominated power networks couple frequency and voltage, making traditional decoupled analysis inadequate. We introduce a unified system-wide metric---the complex frequency of system losses-to evaluate dynamic performance and synchronization. Composed of device- and network-driven terms, it expresses voltage and injected-current phasor variations weighted by bus complex powers. Validated on an IBR-modified IEEE 39-bus system and the Irish transmission grid, the framework effectively assesses R/X sensitivities, dynamic support limits, and data-center load impacts.

items.title: Contract-Based Decomposition of Temporal Logic Specifications for Networked Systems under Arbitrary Partitions
items.summary: Computational complexity is an inherent limitation of formal synthesis for networked systems, and decomposing the global specification into local ones relaxes this limitation at the cost of conservatism. Since the granularity of the partition governs this trade-off, it is reasonable to treat the partition as a design variable, which calls for local specifications that remain correct for every partition. To this end, this paper gives each agent a local specification, written as an assume-guarantee contract that the agent can establish from local information. We first derive a necessary and sufficient condition for these contracts to decompose the global specification under a given partition. Building on this, we then present a condition under which the decomposition is correct for every partition, so that the partition becomes a free design variable. For linear dynamics and signal temporal logic formulas with affine predicates, we further synthesize a controller for each coalition by a tube-based approach. Finally, simulations on a network of input-coupled tanks show how the choice of partition trades computational cost against conservatism.

items.title: Anomalous Sound Detection Using Separation Features and Paired-Mixture Representation Learning
items.summary: Acoustic condition monitoring often relies on normal recordings with limited operating-condition information. This study proposes an anomalous sound detection system that learns from normal recordings without external pre-training and uses machine-type information to organize training and normal references. A separator learns target-component estimation from mixtures of normal target and non-target recordings. With the separator frozen, regional attention and multi-stage fusion are trained on paired mixtures sharing a target, using contrastive and target-reference consistency objectives. Paired-mixture embedding differences provide covariance statistics for correction with normal-reference centering, followed by cosine nearest-neighbor scoring. On Task 2 development-test data from the 2022 Detection and Classification of Acoustic Scenes and Events challenge, the two-block, 64-channel system achieves an overall harmonic mean of 64.56% on average across three independent training and evaluation runs, with a sample standard deviation of 0.33 percentage points. This mean exceeds that of direct paired-mixture learning by 2.23 percentage points and is 0.31 percentage points below that of the evaluated distillation system using an externally pre-trained teacher. For the learned embeddings, cosine nearest-neighbor scoring outperforms the evaluated Mahalanobis scorers based on global normal statistics. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining separation-based representation learning, interference-based correction, and local normal-reference scoring for anomalous sound detection without detailed operating metadata.

items.title: PLL-Less Synchronization of Grid-Following Converters Using a Voltage-Driven Frenet Frame
items.summary: In grid-following converters, the synchronization path can transmit voltage disturbances to the current loop under weak or unbalanced grid conditions. This paper develops a Frenet-frame controller that derives its axes from the integral curve of the measured voltage at the point of common coupling. The tangential current governs active power, while the normal and binormal currents govern the transverse components of non-active power. Feedforward terms derived from the output filter model compensate curvature and torsion coupling, yielding identical nominal current dynamics across the axes. The controller operates without a phase-locked loop or sequence extraction. A reduced transverse model accounts for the finite bandwidth of geometric rate reconstruction and predicts a reduction in low-frequency coupling from voltage disturbances to current. Controller hardware-in-the-loop tests using real-time simulation of a three-phase four-wire converter show the shortest settling time after an active power reference step and the smallest peak power deviations during balanced voltage disturbances among the tested controllers. Under single-phase voltage unbalance, the method reduces peak binormal current and maximum phase-current total harmonic distortion relative to both benchmarks. It also settles to the commanded power in a weak-grid connection test where the phase-locked loop benchmark exhibits sustained oscillations.

items.title: Protection-Oriented Assessment of Machine Learning-Based Fault Detection in Power Systems
items.summary: Machine learning (ML)-based fault detectors are increasingly proposed for power system protection, yet aggregate metrics can obscure the consequences of false and missed trips. We present a protection-oriented assessment of three ML detectors and a sequence-current reference on PROTECT-90, comprising 9,022 simulated fault episodes on a 90 kV double-circuit line. The assessment combines five window conditions, causal window-end labelling, episode-grouped cross-validation, and operating-point selection under a fixed security budget. It reports security, dependability, detection timing, decision margins, and episode-level nuisance assertions. Gradient-boosted trees, a convolutional neural network, and logistic regression achieve AUC-ROC values above 0.999, yet at a security budget of $10^{-3}$ their developed-fault missed-trip rates range from 0.007% to 1.99%. Post-clearing false-trip rates of approximately 0.12-0.16% per window coexist with nuisance assertions in 11.3-19.1% of episodes. Among the analysed physical descriptors, missed trips are most consistently associated with higher fault resistance within the sampled range. An analytical current proxy suggests a fault-current gradient only partly reproduced by waveform-derived current (rank correlation 0.62). No single topology state or faulted phase consistently dominates within the sampled domain. Because PROTECT-90 contains fault episodes only, security is assessed on pre-fault and post-clearing windows rather than independent non-fault disturbances.

items.title: Implicit discretization of PID-like sliding-mode control with third-order output accuracy
items.summary: A digital PID-like sliding-mode controller is proposed for a double integrator with a Lipschitz matched disturbance. A proper implicit discretization, matched to the exact sampled dynamics of the plant, attains the accuracy of the continuous-time controller without discretization chattering. Global finite-step convergence to a discrete-time sliding mode is established for two gain designs and every sampling time, using an implicit Lyapunov function and a computer-assisted certificate in exact arithmetic. The resulting controller provides third-order output accuracy, second-order accuracy for its derivative, and exact finite-time rejection of constant matched disturbances. These accuracy orders are proved to be optimal among deterministic causal controllers using the same sampled information.

items.title: OrbitWeaver: LLM Agent Planning with Simulation Feedback for Optically Interconnected Orbital GPU Clusters
items.summary: Space-based data-center designs increasingly consider GPU computing formations connected by inter-satellite optical links. With limited neighboring connections, jobs assigned disjoint GPUs can still contend on shared relay paths. Rank placement and communication priorities jointly affect this contention and the readiness of downstream computation. We present OrbitWeaver, an offline large language model (LLM) agent planner that jointly optimizes rank placement and communication order. Guided by communication structure, execution dependencies, and simulation feedback, the agent constructs and refines plans that coordinate shared-link access with computation progress. This coordination reduces contention and dependency blocking, shortening mean job completion time (JCT). Simulation experiments on optically interconnected orbital GPU clusters show that OrbitWeaver reduces aggregate mean JCT by 6.2-33.5% relative to the state-of-the-art baselines CASSINI, Crux, and Symphony. These results demonstrate the value of LLM-guided planning for efficient concurrent computing in orbital GPU clusters.

items.title: An iterative tangential interpolation algorithm for model reduction of MIMO systems
items.summary: We consider model reduction of large-scale Multi-Input, Multi-Output (MIMO) systems using low-rank barycentric tangential interpolation on the frequency axis. Our scheme is related to the recently-developed Adaptive Antoulas--Anderson (AAA) algorithm, which is an iterative algorithm that uses concepts related to the Loewner framework. One feature of our algorithm is optimization of the interpolation weight matrices to minimize a proxy for the \(L_2\) system error. We use the freedom in interpolation point selection to provide multiple minimum-error-based algorithms with trade-offs between computational complexity and approximation performance. We prove that a weighted \(L_2\) norm of the proxy error system is non-increasing as interpolation points are added, and that the reduced-order system is stable whenever the original system is. Computational results are provided demonstrating the closeness of the proxy system and true system \(L_2\) errors. Comparisons with prior work demonstrate performance on par with standard model reduction methods.

items.title: Stealthy, High-Impact False Data Injection Attacks in Smart Grid Using Physics-Constrained GAN with Limited System Knowledge
items.summary: False data injection (FDI) attacks can distort power system state estimation while retaining plausible measurement patterns. Existing FDI methods trade stealth for impact or vice versa. They often assume access to internal grids, all-bus sensing, or defender models. In this paper, we propose a detector-agnostic physics-constrained generative adversarial network (PCGAN) that learns decoupled power-flow sensitivities from historical measurements of deployed sensors. The learned active-power-angle and reactive-power-voltage-magnitude relationships guide perturbations restricted to compromised channels, while adversarial training promotes realistic spatiotemporal patterns. We implement PCGAN and seven existing FDI attacks on the IEEE 300-bus system using one year of observed hourly demand from PJM Interconnection, a regional transmission organization in the United States, and synthetic bus-level load profiles. We compare their performance across 10%, 30%, 60%, and 100% compromised sensors. Attack stealth is assessed against ten machine-learning (ML) detectors and conventional bad-data detection (BDD) methods, while physical impact is quantified through nonlinear alternating-current weighted least-squares state estimation. PCGAN achieves 84.28% mean ML evasion and 22.31% mean spatial load misperception across the four scenarios. Its mean stealth-impact trade-off score reaches 18.69%, compared with 5.61% for the strongest competing attack. PCGAN also achieves 83.45% chi-square BDD evasion and 86.02% largest-normalized-residual BDD evasion. These results demonstrate a favorable stealth-impact balance under varying sensor-access levels and provide challenging attack cases for evaluating FDI detectors.

items.title: Improved Closed-Form Identification of the Air-Gap Permeance in Magnetic Equivalent Circuits of Rotor-Eccentric Electric Motors
items.summary: Fast and accurate simulation of electric motors is essential for their design, fault diagnosis and control. Magnetic equivalent circuits (MECs) offer a computationally efficient alternative to the finite element method (FEM), yet their flux tube representation poorly captures the air-gap field. This creates a challenge, as the air gap stores most of the magnetic energy and governs the electromagnetic torque and, in rotor-eccentric motors, the unbalanced magnetic pull (UMP). Existing air-gap permeance expressions vary widely in their results for torque ripple and UMP and account for tooth-normal eccentricity only. This paper proposes the dual-term air-gap permeance (DTAP) model, a closed-form expression for the air-gap permeance between a stator and a rotor tooth that accounts for tooth-normal and tooth-tangential eccentricity, with and without rotor skew. Its parameters are identified from a FEM model of the air gap and the complete set of tooth heads, which includes the shielding by the neighbouring teeth. For three motors, DTAP reproduces the FEM air-gap permeance with a 2.8-4.8 times smaller error than the state of the art, at a comparable computational cost. Implemented in the MEC of an eccentric induction motor, it reproduces the torque ripple within 1.6% and the peak UMP within 1.3% of the reference, i.e., with 2.8 and 27 times smaller deviations than the state of the art. DTAP thereby enables MEC to predict the torque pulsations and bearing loads of eccentric motors more accurately without sacrificing computational speed.

items.title: Integrating Planning and Predictive Control Using the Path Feasibility Governor
items.summary: The motion planning problem of generating dynamically feasible, collision-free trajectories in non-convex environments is a fundamental challenge for autonomous systems. Decomposing the problem into path planning and path tracking improves tractability, but integrating these components in a theoretically sound and computationally efficient manner is challenging. We propose the Path Feasibility Governor (PathFG), a framework for integrating path planners with nonlinear Model Predictive Control (MPC). The PathFG manipulates the reference passed to the MPC controller, guiding it along a path while ensuring constraint satisfaction, stability, and recursive feasibility. The PathFG is modular, compatible with replanning, and improves computational efficiency and reliability by reducing the need for long prediction horizons. We prove safety and asymptotic stability with a significantly expanded region of attraction, and validate its real-time performance through simulated case studies of unicycle and quadrotor navigation in cluttered environments. \c{opyright}2026 IEEE. items.title: Sensing-Aided Beam Selection for UAV Networks
items.summary: Fast and low-overhead beam management is essential for the practical deployment of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication networks operating at millimeter-wave and higher frequencies. In this paper, we propose a radar-assisted beam selection framework for UAV networks that exploits spatial sensing information, including angle-of-departure and distance estimates, to efficiently identify communication beams. Specifically, a digitally beamformed radar array with a relatively small number of antennas provides rapid, coarse UAV localization, while an analog-beamformed communication array, requiring fewer radio-frequency chains, exploits coarse localization to narrow the beam-search region and establish a communication link with the UAV. To provide theoretical insight into the expected overhead, we conduct a probabilistic analysis in which an approximation of the nearest-first beam selection overhead under idealized conditions is proposed and its statistics are derived for a Gaussian error model. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed radar-assisted beam selection significantly reduces the number of beams that need to be examined, requiring on average at most 1.64 candidate beams even under per-element radar phase errors of up to 100°.

items.title: Coordinated Cooling and Compute Management for AI Datacenters
items.summary: The AI datacenters are currently being deployed on a large scale to support the training and deployment of power-intensive large-language models (LLMs). Extensive amount of computation and cooling required in datacenters increase concerns about the energy use and carbon emissions of AI datacenters. Although current state-of-the-art has examined the energy efficiency of LLM inference, most prior research focused on optimizing compute-side scheduling without considering thermal objectives or constraints. Since GPU-intensive inference generates substantial heat that can degrade datacenter performance, ignoring thermal effects can increase total energy consumption and reduce the efficiency of LLM serving. To fill this gap, we profile the characteristics of GPU servers under varying cooling and AI jobs, and develop a joint cooling and computing modeling approach for AI datacenters. Built upon such workload and thermal dynamics models, a novel hierarchical control framework is proposed to co-optimize computing and thermal management by identifying the optimal GPU parallelism, frequency (DVFS), and cooling control knobs. Using real Azure inference traces and detailed GPU profiling, our model balances serving latency and thermal constraints in AI datacenters while significantly improving AI datacenters' energy efficiency.

items.title: Inferring Sensitive Events in Multi-Mode Cyber-Physical Systems via Scheduling Side Channels
items.summary: Many cyber-physical systems (CPS) are multi-mode: they switch between operating modes with different tasksets and timing parameters in response to physical events or user activity. We show that these mode changes create a timing side channel: by altering the interference experienced by co-running tasks, they let an unprivileged co-resident observer infer sensitive events, such as a homeowner's arrival or a vehicle's route, from its own execution timing and, on multicore platforms, its core assignment. Existing schedule-based attacks and defenses miss this channel because they assume single-mode systems or target a specific, known victim task. We present STAMP, a lightweight attack that needs no knowledge of task parameters or scheduling policy, and works whether or not the system exposes its modes. On a ZoneMinder home-security deployment, STAMP identifies the modes with 94.7% accuracy on unseen hardware, using under 0.5% of one core. On ROS 2 AMCL with the Oxford RobotCar dataset, it identifies which of seven route segments a vehicle traversed with 86.0% accuracy on unseen platforms. A schedule-randomization defense lowers detection recall to 0.53, at which setting only 53.9% as many jobs finish on time. At higher noise ($ε=10$), on-time job completion reduces to 14.4%, while introducing new leakage in 14.1% of the tasksets.

items.title: Graph Neural Network Prediction of Frequency Nadir and RoCoF Under Topology Variations
items.summary: Accurate prediction of frequency dynamics under varying network topologies is essential for rapid frequency security assessment, whereas repeated electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulations are computationally intensive. This paper develops a topology-aware graph neural network with a radial basis function Kolmogorov-Arnold network (RBF-KAN) regression head, termed RK-GNN, to predict frequency nadir and maximum absolute rate of change of frequency (RoCoF). Scenarios combine load scaling, regional load redistribution, and generator redispatch with intact, N-1, and N-2 transmission topologies. After checks for network connectivity, generator reference limits, and numerical consistency, the retained scenarios are simulated in PSCAD to construct the reference dataset. The RK-GNN is evaluated against a conventional deep neural network (DNN) and a baseline GNN. On the IEEE 39-bus system, the RK-GNN reduces the mean absolute errors (MAEs) of nadir and RoCoF by 48% and 59% relative to the DNN and by 42% and 61% relative to the baseline GNN. Incorporating the bridge indicator and disturbance hop distance yields further MAE reductions of 27% and 54%. These results show that the proposed topology-aware architecture provides accurate prediction of both frequency metrics under varying topologies and substantially reduces the need for repeated EMT simulations.

items.title: GigaEdge Spench: An SDK for Practical Streaming Speech Enhancement
items.summary: We present GigaEdge Spench, an open-source SDK for streaming speech enhancement on CPU servers, mobile devices, and in browsers. Applications can build enhancement channels from neural denoising, normalization and dynamics blocks, sample-rate conversion, and acoustic echo cancellation where supported. These stages can be combined, while normalization can also run without a neural model. The release includes an 8 kHz INT8 denoiser and discriminative and hybrid 48 kHz FP32 models. A shared C++ core supports ONNX Runtime and TensorFlow Lite through native interfaces, Android and iOS SDKs, and WebAssembly integration. Independent stream contexts share model resources, and consecutive frames from one stream can be processed in a single inference call. We evaluate the released models on EARS-WHAM v2 and compare their quality and processing costs with RNNoise and DPDFNet2. All tested native and Web configurations process files faster than real time, although larger chunks require more time to collect input. We also measure how many streams a shared model can process on a CPU. Our contribution is a configurable deployment system and an experimental study of how model choice, chunk size, and execution environment affect its use. All reported SDK timing uses ONNX Runtime. Index Terms: speech enhancement, streaming inference, cross-platform deployment, temporal frame grouping, computational efficiency

items.title: X-Strata: Separating Aneurysms and Overlapping Vessels into Layers from 2D X-ray Angiography
items.summary: An X-ray angiogram sums every structure along a ray into one pixel. When vessels cross an aneurysm, they obscure part of it and mix their contrast into its filling curve. We present X-Strata, a network that separates a cine angiogram into three layers: the complete aneurysm sac, the vessels in front of it, and the vessels behind it. Contrast timing indicates how much each layer contributes to a pixel, and parallax between two views indicates their order, which a single view cannot determine. X-Strata first estimates the layers and their contrast curves, then uses the second view to assign vessels to the front or back layer, and lifts all layers into 3D. It learns from layer labels projected from same-session 3D rotational angiography, but needs only 2D cine runs and their acquisition geometry at inference. On 220 held-out patients from three centers (122 external), two-view X-Strata ranks first among 14 baselines, including VGGT and C$^2$RV, in recovering the sac where vessels overlap it (Dice 0.693 internal, 0.641 external) and in ordering the layers (balanced accuracy 0.703, 0.659). Its order accuracy exceeds that of all 11 end-to-end baselines by at least 4.1 points internally and 3.3 externally (Holm-adjusted $p < 0.001$) and grows with view separation. Recovered 3D sac surfaces have a median Chamfer distance of 0.34 mm on the internal cohort. X-Strata may therefore provide layered aneurysm and vessel information, including 3D sac shape, for patients who undergo only 2D angiography.

items.title: Integrate the Reward, Don't Sample It: Window Likelihood for Interruptions and Backchannels in Full-Duplex Speech Models
items.summary: When a user talks over a full-duplex dialogue model, it must decide whether the user is interrupting (stop) or backchannelling (carry on). Post-training can improve this discrimination or change how readily it stops. In our GRPO runs the second dominates: no configuration lowers both error rates on more than one model, and two released checkpoints discriminate no better than their bases. We trace this partly to how the reward is estimated. The probability of stopping inside a short window is a known function of a few stop probabilities the policy emits, yet GRPO estimates it by sampling. A group of rollouts that all agree gives no gradient, even when all fail; the push on the stop threshold is strongest where the model is unsure, whichever outcome is right; and whole-rollout credit reaches decisions the reward never judges. Confining the credit to the window removes only that leakage. Window likelihood (WL) samples the words but integrates over the stop decisions, so the probability of the correct outcome is computed exactly and its logarithm maximised. On HumDial-FDBench, across four open models, WL gives the best F1 and lowers both error rates by more than their confidence intervals, without talking into silence.

items.title: State-of-Charge Targets for Storage Participation in Two-Settlement Markets: Reliability, Price, and Compensation Impacts
items.summary: As energy storage assumes a larger role in electricity systems, market operation must coordinate its use across time to support reliability during periods of system stress. Minimum state-of-charge (SOC) targets provide a means of preserving energy for these periods, but their design shapes reliability, operating efficiency, and storage compensation. This paper evaluates alternative SOC target designs in a California-based day-ahead and real-time electricity market model. The comparison examines targets based on day-ahead schedules or rolling centralized dispatch, enforced at the individual-resource or system level, across seasons, stress conditions, and participant information settings. The results show that retaining more energy does not necessarily reduce load shedding: targets that restrict discharge can limit storage support during shortages. Under critical summer conditions, individual targets derived from rolling centralized dispatch reduce weekly load shedding by approximately 83--84\% relative to operation without targets. Lower RT clearing costs and average prices can coexist with higher storage compensation, reflecting the role of day-ahead positions and real-time deviations in determining settlement outcomes. These findings highlight the importance of coordinating energy retention with timely discharge and network deliverability when designing SOC requirements for storage participation in electricity markets.

items.title: uhd-rfsoc: Bringing Off-the-Shelf RFSoC Boards to Unmodified UHD Applications
items.summary: Next-generation wireless research relies on software-defined radios (SDRs) with more channels and larger bandwidth. The USRP family is one of the most widely used SDR platforms, and much of the wireless software ecosystem is built on top of the USRP hardware driver (UHD). However, each USRP model comes with a fixed channel count, bandwidth, and streaming capability. Off-the-shelf radio frequency system-on-chip (RFSoC) boards, on the other hand, integrate up to 16 analog-to-digital converters (ADCs) and 16 digital-to-analog converters (DACs) operating at several gigasamples per second (GS/s), but existing UHD applications cannot directly use them. We present uhd-rfsoc, an open-source FPGA design and host software stack that turns these boards, including the 16-channel ZCU216 and the RFSoC 4x2, into standard UHD devices without modifying UHD. Through standard UHD calls, applications can configure the carrier frequency, channel count, the per-channel I/Q sample rate, and the wire format. uhd-rfsoc combines timestamped, flow-controlled sample transport in the FPGA with data plane development kit (DPDK) packet processing and vectorized sample conversion on x86 and Arm hosts. The built bitstreams for a number of RFSoC board configurations with varying RF data converter rates, channel counts, I/Q sample rates, and wire formats all successfully pass UHD's built-in streaming benchmarks. We further demonstrate compatibility with unmodified GNU Radio flowgraphs, a custom GPU-accelerated transceiver digital signal processing pipeline, as well as the OCUDU and Duranta 5G radio access network stacks using both software and commodity user equipment.

items.title: A Tumour-Aware Multimodal Framework for Explainable Prediction of IDH Mutation in Gliomas from Multi-Sequence MRI
items.summary: Accurate prediction of isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation status is essential for glioma diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment planning. Although recent deep learning approaches have demonstrated promising performance, many rely on whole-brain feature extraction and provide limited interpretability. This study proposes a tumour-aware multimodal framework for explainable, non-invasive prediction of IDH mutation status from multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The proposed framework integrates four MRI sequences (T1, T1CE, T2, and FLAIR), tumour subregion segmentation, quantitative radiomic descriptors, and clinical information within a unified deep learning architecture. An ablation study was conducted to evaluate the contribution of tumour-aware learning, radiomic features, and clinical variables. Model performance was assessed using multiple complementary evaluation metrics, including accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, balanced accuracy, receiver operating characteristic analysis, confusion matrix evaluation, and Grad-CAM visualisation. Experimental results demonstrated that the proposed multimodal framework consistently outperformed the baseline MRI-only model, with the Clinical Fusion model achieving the strongest overall predictive performance. The integration of tumour-aware learning, radiomic descriptors, and clinical information progressively improved classification performance, while Grad-CAM visualisations indicated that the model predominantly focused on biologically relevant tumour regions. These findings suggest that tumour-aware multimodal feature integration enables accurate, interpretable, and non-invasive molecular profiling of gliomas and provides a promising foundation for future clinical decision support in precision neuro-oncology.

items.title: Cross-Linguistic Acoustic Biomarkers of Cognitive Impairment Across Interactive and Single-Speaker Speech Tasks
items.summary: Multilingual dementia detection is essential for scalable and equitable screening. In recent years, automated speech analysis has emerged as a promising approach for supporting dementia detection by enabling non-invasive and scalable assessment of cognitive function. However, existing studies that use automated speech analysis often rely on one type of task, such as picture description, and use black-box models. These studies often neglect the role of task and language. To address these gaps, we performed a cross-linguistic and cross-task acoustic analysis that integrates a conversational dataset with structured speech tasks across four languages (Spanish, Mandarin, English, Japanese). We applied statistical, linguist-/clinician-guided, and machine learning model-based feature selection to derive compact acoustic feature sets while maintaining classification performance. This enabled systematic comparison of cognitive impairment-relevant features across datasets and tasks. Our results revealed that acoustic features did not generalize uniformly across tasks and languages. Temporal features remained robust across all datasets, consistently capturing timing disruption regardless of language or task. In contrast, speech rate showed strong task dependence -- emerging as informative mainly in single-speaker tasks with externally anchored content and pacing, but becoming less reliable when speech content was highly individualized. Pitch-related features further exhibited language-specific patterns, favoring chroma-related features in tonal languages (e.g., Mandarin) and F0-related features in non-tonal languages. These findings caution against indiscriminate pooling of heterogeneous speech data and underscore the need for interpretable, context-aware approaches to multilingual dementia detection using automated speech analysis.

items.title: Frequency-Security-Aware Real-Time Economic Dispatch with Data Center UPS Flexibility for Inertia and Primary Frequency Response Services
items.summary: The increasing penetration of renewable energy and the rapid growth of AI data centers are introducing significant challenges to power system frequency security. There is an urgent need to identify grid-compatible resources capable of providing fast frequency support. This paper proposes a frequency-security-aware real-time economic dispatch (RTED) model that enables data center (DC) uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems to provide steady-state power balancing, inertia response, and primary frequency response (PFR) services. Specifically, tractable analytical frequency-security constraints are derived and incorporated into the RTED framework through second-order cone programming (SOCP) formulation. The proposed model jointly optimizes energy, reserve, and inertia to minimize system operation cost while preventing under-frequency load shedding (UFLS). Numerical validation on a modified IEEE 39-bus system demonstrates that the proposed RTED model with UPS flexibility can economically support system operation and significantly improve frequency security under active-power deficit disturbances.

items.title: Orbit-AWARE: From Onboard AI Deployment to Sustainable In-Orbit Intelligence
items.summary: The growing role of space computing in time-critical satellite services makes the long-term reliability of onboard artificial intelligence (AI) a mission-level requirement. Model drift can undermine this reliability through critical-observation suppression or noncritical priority flooding, displacing both mission information and evidence for model correction. To address this drift-induced evidence displacement, this article presents Orbit-AWARE, a safeguard-first lifecycle management (LCM) architecture. A comparison of existing approaches motivates cooperative Data, Cognitive, and Trust Planes for continuous monitoring, event-triggered agentic orchestration, and deterministic governance. The architecture retains a model-independent sample stream before degradation is confirmed and coordinates evidence selection and exchange for diagnosis and ground-assisted adaptation. Candidate updates are verified before control over data disposition is restored. In an xBD-based emergency Earth observation (EO) case study, Orbit-AWARE delivers 14.3\% more critical observations and achieves 8.3\% higher sustainable mission utility than the Rule-Based Drift Loop under a common 10\% downlink budget. Finally, we discuss future research directions for extending LCM through task-aware reliability assessment, memory- and tool-enabled onboard agents, and evidence-centric space networking. This work makes evidence availability and recovery authorization explicit design objectives for dependable onboard AI services.

items.title: Efficient Design of Flag Sequence Sets for Delay-Doppler Estimation via Riemannian Optimization
items.summary: This letter investigates the design of a Flag sequence set with peak-curtain auto-ambiguity functions to enable low-complexity delay-Doppler estimation. Given the predefined Curtain sequences, the Flag sequence set design problem is formulated as the minimization of the weighted integrated masked sidelobe level. To solve this problem, we first reformulate it as an unconstrained optimization problem on the unimodular manifold. Then, a tailored unimodular manifold conjugate gradient (UM-CG) algorithm is developed. Compared with the existing define algorithm, the proposed UM-CG algorithm reduces computational and storage requirements. Moreover, the global convergence of the proposed UM-CG scheme is theoretically derived under mild conditions. Numerical results demonstrate the superior optimization performance of the proposed UM-CG algorithm and show that the designed Flag sequences exhibit nearly ideal peak-curtain properties.

items.title: A Control Barrier Function-Constrained Model Predictive Control Framework for Safe Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Ensuring safety under unknown and stochastic dynamics remains a significant challenge in reinforcement learning (RL). In this paper, we propose a model predictive control (MPC)-based safe RL framework, called Probabilistic Ensembles with CBF-constrained Trajectory Sampling (PECTS), to address this challenge. PECTS jointly learns stochastic system dynamics with probabilistic neural networks (PNNs) and control barrier functions (CBFs) with Lipschitz-bounded neural networks. Safety is enforced by incorporating learned CBF constraints into the MPC formulation while accounting for the model stochasticity. This enables probabilistic safety under model uncertainty. To solve the resulting MPC problem, we utilize a sampling-based optimizer together with a safe trajectory sampling method that discards unsafe trajectories based on the learned system model and CBF. We also derive a finite-horizon exit-probability bound using tail information for centered barrier increments. We validate PECTS in various simulation studies, where it outperforms baseline methods.

items.title: Brain-inspired Beam Selection for mmWave RIS Communication
items.summary: Beam selection at large passive reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) requires either full channel knowledge or beam training, both of which entail unwanted overhead. On the other hand, learned models that predict the optimal codeword from channels sampled at a few active elements avoid both, at the cost of energy-demanding multiply-and-accumulate operations. In this paper, we propose spiking neural network (SNN)-based beam selection for a semi-active RIS assisting a mmWave multiple-input single-output communication system. Direct and sigmoid rate coding are compared against a multi- layer perceptron (MLP) of identical architecture. Energy analysis further reveals that the input layer dominates SNN energy consumption.

items.title: Feasibility of Pareto-Improving Damping Control of Forced Oscillations: The Active-Power Case
items.summary: Damping control of a forced oscillation may reduce amplitudes at certain locations while increasing them elsewhere. This paper introduces Pareto improvement as a criterion for assessing such control: at least one nodal oscillation amplitude decreases, while none increases across all other nodes. The analysis considers active-power forcing sources and active-power control injections in connected swing networks with positive inertia and damping. Necessary conditions for Pareto improvement feasibility are derived from the normalized nodal responses. It is proven that for every network with a single oscillation source and a single actuator, at least one positive forcing frequency is shown to preclude Pareto improvement, regardless of the amplitude and phase of the control input. A three-node counterexample shows that this limitation does not persist with multiple actuators. PSS/E simulations of a 6-bus benchmark system and a modified IEEE 39-bus system validated the analysis. These findings suggest the value of assessing control effects across the network and further investigating multi-actuator damping control.

items.title: When to Move: Online Repositioning of Movable Antenna Arrays Under a Long-Term Actuation Energy Budget
items.summary: Movable antenna (MA) arrays improve multiuser throughput by repositioning their elements, but mechanical movement reduces transmission time and consumes actuation energy. Changes in user configurations create nonuniform demand for repositioning over time, while each movement determines which positions are reachable in subsequent slots. Thus, online control must decide when to spend a limited actuation-energy budget, not only where to position the antennas. We formulate causal effective-throughput maximization under displacement-dependent movement delay, inter-slot reachability, and a long-term average actuation-energy constraint. We propose Lyapunov-based online movable-antenna repositioning (LOMA), which adjusts the price of movement through a virtual queue and solves the resulting nonconvex position problem via proximal minorization--maximization, accounting for nonsmooth movement delay and promoting sparse antenna updates. We establish monotone ascent of the smoothed per-slot objective, a finite-horizon sample-path energy bound, almost-sure long-term budget feasibility under a Gaussian fading model with bounded large-scale gains, and a state-matched throughput comparison separating temporal energy allocation from per-slot optimization error. Simulations show that LOMA concentrates actuation after intermittent user changes and improves effective throughput over optimized fixed arrays and a per-slot-budget counterpart, while continuous channel drift favors more frequent incremental repositioning. Additional simulations with pilot-based channel estimates in sparse millimeter-wave channels show that LOMA retains most of the throughput benefits of online repositioning while operating near its prescribed long-term actuation-energy budget.

items.title: A Theory of Information Architecture for Networked Decisions: Freshness, Locality, and Coordination
items.summary: A broader view of a network can help agents coordinate, but collecting that view takes time. When is a fresh local observation more useful than an older view of the whole network, and when should an agent look only partway across it? We study agents that repeatedly minimize a shared quadratic cost in an environment that evolves independently of their actions. An information architecture specifies what each agent observes and how old those observations are. Each agent uses a synchronized neighborhood snapshot, so extending its scope also ages the nearby readings used in the decision. We assume that the optimal action with complete information is affine in the state, and that the conditional mean of the current state equals the old state scaled by a common exponential decay factor. Using the classical Marschak--Radner decomposition, we derive the delay threshold beyond which fresh local information outperforms a complete but older global view. This comparison allows non-Gaussian states and nonlinear decision rules. We then determine how far an agent should look by balancing the benefit of additional observations against their greater age. In a Gaussian spatial model on a line, we derive the optimal observation radius: looking beyond the local node pays only when information travels more than twice the spatial correlation length in one coherence time. The preferred information architecture also depends on the decision being made. On a fixed 64-node ring, increasing only the reach of the decision weights from 0.7 to 6 hops shifts the optimal observation radius from one to five hops.

items.title: Symbolic-Permutation-Based Direct Sparse Jacobian Assembly for Accelerated Power-Flow Analysis
items.summary: The repeated assembly of the sparse Jacobian matrix constitutes a primary computational bottleneck in the Newton-Raphson power-flow analysis. Through an algebraic operator equivariance analysis of the Jacobian matrix, this paper formalizes the reduction process and proposes a direct sparse Jacobian assembly method based on symbolic permutation. By pre-applying the permutation to the admittance matrix during a fast one-time symbolic phase via its sparse prefix-sum property, the runtime bus-type projection overhead and indirect mapping caches are entirely eliminated. Consequently, complex Jacobian differentiation and global matrix assembly fuse into a single operation, yielding a single-pass, branchless algorithm that streams values directly into contiguous memory. The proposed algorithm is implemented in the open-source RustPower solver. Benchmarks on IEEE test systems and PEGASE 9241 demonstrate that the proposed assembly is 28.1-37.9 times faster than the MATPOWER-style baseline and 8.9-9.7 times faster than the in-house Schäfer-Braun-inspired assembly (V1); on PEGASE 9241, it outperforms optimized traditional C++ assembly routines by 3.72 times in cold construction and 2.59 times across iterations. End-to-end, the iteration-loop solve time with KLU is 1.16-1.97 times faster than the native C++ LightSim2Grid and up to 95.5 times faster than pandapower, while leaving numerical results and convergence behavior unchanged. The method extends directly to general problems where a sparse Jacobian inherits its structure from a static network operator, including transient stability analysis, EMT simulation, and OPF Hessian assembly.

items.title: Battery Energy Storage Sizing in PV Ramp-Rate Smoothing using Constraint-Aware Reinforcement Learning-Based Controller
items.summary: This paper presents a constraint-aware reinforcement learning (CARL) controller for battery energy storage system (BESS) sizing and photovoltaic (PV) ramp-rate smoothing. Rapid PV power fluctuations caused by cloud transitions can introduce operational and stability challenges in power systems. To mitigate these impacts, grid codes impose ramp-rate limits (RRL) on PV power injected to the grid. BESSs can support such grid codes by absorbing or supplying power during rapid variations. However, the extent to which BESSs can reduce PV-induced variability depends on (i) the BESS power and energy capacities; and (ii) the adopted controller. Thus, BESS sizing and controller design are coupled. Conventional moving-average control can increase battery usage due to filter-induced lag, while ramp-rate control is reactive and does not account for the long-term impact of actions on battery state of charge and future ramp events. Optimization-based methods can reduce BESS requirements by anticipating future PV variations, but their performance depends on accurate PV forecasts. To address these limitations, the CARL controller learns a causal state-feedback policy from historical PV data without requiring forecasts during deployment. Ramp-rate, converter-power, and state-of-charge constraints are incorporated into a causal feasibility interval that guarantees feasible actions by definition. A full-horizon input-convex neural network (ICNN)-based optimization is developed as a noncausal benchmark for the minimum achievable BESS requirements. Evaluation using three real-world PV datasets shows that, at a 10\%/min ramp-rate limit, CARL reduces peak BESS power by 8.7--10.4\% and energy capacity by 47.5--62.6\% relative to conventional ramp-rate control while maintaining the grid-codes compliance.

items.title: Fair and Efficient Distributed EV Charging Coordination Using Threshold Cryptography and Machine Learning
items.summary: Distributed coordination of electric vehicle (EV) charging with the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) keeps EV constraints private but assumes that every participant follows the algorithm. This assumption fails in practice, where a biased operator or a man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacker can send inconsistent signals to different EVs, and compromised EVs can deviate from their prescribed updates. We first prove that attacks by such arbitrarily malicious, i.e., Byzantine, participants do not prevent convergence and therefore remain undetected, and derive the most damaging attack in closed form. We then propose a framework that combines a threshold-signed broadcast with upload recomputation, which detects every deviation without false alarms at linear instead of quadratic communication cost. To keep the optimization running, each affected EV recovers locally with a certified, fleet-aware machine learning price forecast, and we prove that the optimization remains convergent with a recovery cost bounded by the shape of the forecast error. Simulation results with real-world load, price, and charging data show that a biased operator raises the annual cost of disadvantaged EVs by 132.7% and lowers that of advantaged EVs by 49.3% without changing the aggregate load, whereas the defense limits all cost changes to 2.6%. An external MITM attacker raises the cost of its victims by 57.6%, the peak load by 5.8%, and the grid cost by 15.8%, whereas the defense keeps them within 1.1%, 0.2%, and 0.3% of benign operation. With up to 70% of the EVs attacked, the recovery converges in at least 97.8% of the runs.

items.title: Natural Swing-Up of an Underpowered Double Pendulum
items.summary: Robots with weak motors must ride their natural dynamics rather than fight them. We swing up a direct-drive planar two-link robot, whose motors deliver only about 6\,\% of its shoulder gravity torque, along its nonlinear normal modes, two-dimensional invariant manifolds consisting of periodic orbits. On a non-strict mode, injecting energy necessarily moves the state off the manifold, so pumping and stabilization compete for the same bounded torque. We split the input torque into a power-neutral steering component and a scalar pumping input, the only component that changes the energy. The allocation then becomes a linear program in two variables: maximize pumping subject to the torque limits and one control-Lyapunov constraint. The constraint uses the model-based rate of the error, so no stabilizing feedback gain is needed. Experiments in hardware show swing-ups along both modes and compare the allocation with summing-and-clipping and with prioritized stabilization.

items.title: Symbolic Control for Stochastic Systems via Finite Parity Games
items.summary: We consider the problem of computing the maximal probability of satisfying an omega-regular specification for stochastic nonlinear systems evolving in discrete time. The problem reduces, after automata-theoretic constructions, to finding the maximal probability of satisfying a parity condition on a (possibly hybrid) state space. While characterizing the exact satisfaction probability is open, we show that a lower bound on this probability can be obtained by (I) computing an under-approximation of the qualitative winning region, i.e., states from which the parity condition can be enforced almost surely, and (II) computing the maximal probability of reaching this qualitative winning region. The heart of our approach is a technique to symbolically compute the under-approximation of the qualitative winning region in step (I) via a finite-state abstraction of the original system as a 2.5-player parity game. Our abstraction procedure uses only the support of the probabilistic evolution; it does not use precise numerical transition probabilities. We prove that the winning set in the abstract 2.5-player game induces an under-approximation of the qualitative winning region in the original synthesis problem, along with a policy to solve it. By combining these contributions with (a) a symbolic fixpoint algorithm to solve 2.5-player games and (b) existing techniques for reachability policy synthesis in stochastic nonlinear systems, we get an abstraction-based algorithm for finding a lower bound on the maximal satisfaction probability. We have implemented the abstraction-based algorithm in Mascot-SDS (Majumdar et al., 2020), where we combined the outlined abstraction step with our recent tool FairSyn. We evaluated our implementation on the nonlinear model of a perturbed bistable switch from the literature. We outperform a recently proposed tool for solving this problem by a large margin.

items.title: Sub-Synchronous Control Interaction Risk of Large Data Center Loads: A Frequency-Scan Assessment with Cross-Model Validation
items.summary: Data centers are now one of the fastest-growing loads on the bulk power system, and most of their demand reaches the grid through power converters inside uninterruptible power supplies (UPS). Whether these loads can take part in sub-synchronous control interaction (SSCI), as wind and HVDC converters do, has not been studied extensively. We examine this question with impedance-based frequency scans at the point of common coupling (PCC). Using a detailed proprietary model (INS-ISU), we scan the motor, variable-frequency-drive (VFD), lighting, and UPS-fed information-technology (IT) branches of a representative facility separately. Only the UPS in double-conversion mode shows negative resistance; it covers the whole sub-synchronous band and continues up to about 170 Hz. The other branches, and the UPS in bypass mode, stay passive. We then repeat the scans on three public models from PNNL, TAMU, and NLR. None of them shows negative resistance in bypass mode, while three of the four models do in double-conversion mode. Lowering the load from rated to light load makes the negative resistance deeper, as expected for a constant-power load, so a lightly loaded facility in double-conversion mode is the worst case. Raising the UPS DC-link capacitance pushes the negative resistance into a narrow band around the fundamental. These findings give a basis for screening data centers for SSCI during interconnection studies.

items.title: What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation
items.summary: Continual learning treats any drop in performance on previously seen data as forgetting, a convention inherited from settings where the prediction target is stationary. World models violate this assumption: their target is the environment, which changes, so knowledge that was accurate when learned can later become false, and revising it is correct behavior rather than a defect. Non-stationary ground truth is well studied in the concept drift literature and in the temporal factuality of language models, but it has not been formulated for world models, which are distinctive in that they also encode structural knowledge, such as physical laws and object permanence, that must never be degraded. We argue that continual world models need retention stratified by invariance timescale, the time over which knowledge stays true: invariants should be refined but never degraded, while instance-level facts should be revised once the environment changes. We show that standard forgetting metrics, used alone, count correct revision as forgetting and so rank a frozen model highest. We propose differential retention, which reports two quantities separately: invariant retention, checked after every adaptation round, and revision latency, the number of observations a model needs to pick up a change.

items.title: Learning monotone game-theoretic linear MPC
items.summary: We propose a method to learn a game-theoretic model predictive control (GT-MPC) law by imitation from input and output data of a running multi-agent system. By interpreting the recorded inputs as the first moves of the equilibria of a game played by the agents, we learn the GT-MPC weights under hard input constraints and soft output constraints, without requiring the agents to reveal their objectives. We also impose that the resulting generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) problem is strongly monotone, which ensures the existence and uniqueness of the equilibrium and, hence, that the learned GT-MPC law is well defined and can be evaluated efficiently online by variational GNE-seeking algorithms for linear-quadratic games. Moreover, strong monotonicity implies that the equilibrium is almost everywhere differentiable with respect to the references and the weights, which enables automatic differentiation for gradient-based optimization. In addition, we promote closed-loop stability of the unconstrained equilibrium feedback by incorporating a penalty that involves a jointly learned quadratic Lyapunov function. Learning a GT-MPC formulation enables us to explain the agents' objectives, reproduce their behavior in simulation in new scenarios, optimize their set-points, design mechanisms, and enforce additional constraints. A numerical example illustrates the approach.

items.title: PF-Exec: Large-Scale UAV Relay Load Balancing with an Anchored Potential Direction Decider and a Per-Dimension Gain-Learning Executor
items.summary: Relay load balancing in large-scale UAV networks requires joint decisions on association, bandwidth, power and hovering position, while the dimension grows with the number of UAVs and each UAV sees only its local state. This paper splits the decision into two layers. An anchored potential direction decider emits a closed-form target at every instant and returns its direction only. A gain-learning executor maps a local observation into a positive gain per dimension, composes gain and target, and clips the action against the physical single-step bound; the two layers form PF-Exec. The unit gain is the default start, so the executor reduces to the pure potential policy before training. The load is first-order homogeneous in bandwidth, making the bandwidth target closed form, and the position target is the demand-weighted centroid of the served users. The system uses a two-hop access and millimetre-wave backhaul link with soft association, a 3GPP UMa-AV channel with two shadowing layers, an OU-type social-force crowd and a quadrotor physical layer. Evaluation spans all fleet sizes, two crowd scenarios, independent seeds, the published baselines in their own settings and a degraded-information line. In the highest-pressure burst setting the fixed-step comparison breaks down on part of the seeds, losing fairness and mean load at once, while PF-Exec holds fairness near one. Among the ten comparison methods only the greedy heuristic survives that setting; its load variance stays far higher. Under stale global state and position noise the fairness index stays high at both largest-scale scenarios. Flight energy is nearly identical between the learned and the fixed-step executor, and three constants are fixed once across all settings. The convergence properties of both layers, from the truncated gain iteration to the perturbed tracking bound, are proved in the companion analysis.

items.title: Convergence Properties of PF-Exec: Homogeneous Structure, Anchored Closed Form, and Gain Dynamics
items.summary: This paper establishes a layered mathematical char acterisation of PF-Exec, the algorithm of the companion system paper. Demand-proportional bandwidth allocation yields an exact first-order homogeneous decomposition, from which the equal-load bandwidth target and its feasibility bound follow in closed form. The logarithmic knee view preserves strict load order and shares its global optimum with the Jain fairness index, while the demand-weighted centroid minimises the position potential. The damped softmax association block possesses a fixed point on the product of simplices. The truncated one-dimensional gain iteration admits a complete characterisation, with geomet ric convergence below the critical gain, initial-value-dependent bounded oscillation at it, and a family of bounded two-state cycles above it. A global invariant error ball and an explicit tracking recursion complete the execution guarantee. A numerical audit confirms the structural identities on every measured state and quantifies the local amplification of the coupled association and resource dynamics. Together, the results explain how closed form recovery directions and bounded adaptive gains provide stable execution without requiring a global Euclidean contraction assumption.

items.title: RAZeR: Representation Aware Zonotope Reduction
items.summary: Reachability analysis is a popular technique for verifying the safety of a dynamical system under uncertainty, where the uncertainty is often represented by zonotopes. As the size of the zonotope representation typically grows as the reachability analysis progresses, it must be repeatedly reduced at the cost of additional conservatism. While various methods exist to reduce the size of the representation, combined advantages are not fully leveraged as only a single reduction method is typically used throughout the analysis. In this work, we show how dynamically choosing which method to use can yield significantly tighter results, thereby easing verification. This is realized by introducing a heuristic, derived from model predictive control, that accounts for upcoming propagation of the current zonotope. We argue that order reduction is not merely a post-processing step after propagation but also a pre-processing step that shapes how the zonotope evolves under the system dynamics. We evaluate our approach, RAZeR, on nonlinear benchmarks taken from the ARCH-COMP, where we demonstrate that RAZeR produces tighter zonotopes at a negligible performance overhead.

items.title: Expert-Guided Online Reinforcement Learning for Stable and Sample-Efficient Control of Dynamical Systems
items.summary: Online reinforcement learning (RL) often requires extensive interactions with the environment, which makes the training costly. Additionally, exploration can destabilise the dynamical system, which may be unsafe. On the other hand, offline learning from expert demonstrations avoids unsafe exploration but is limited by the quality and coverage of the offline dataset. In this paper, we propose a model-free RL approach that combines expert demonstrations with limited online interactions. Specifically, we optimise a policy objective consisting of an online performance term and a behavioural cloning regulariser computed from offline expert demonstrations. The regulariser encourages the learned policy to stay close to expert behaviour, reducing the need to explore unfamiliar actions. Expert demonstrations guide policy learning and reduce the need for many online interactions and exploration. For stochastic linear time-invariant (LTI) systems, we establish conditions for linear convergence of exact policy gradient updates and for all intermediate policies to remain stabilising. Although our theoretical analysis focuses on linear systems, we also evaluate the proposed approach on nonlinear systems to demonstrate its effectiveness beyond the linear setting. \rev{Numerical results show that the proposed method reaches comparable performance in fewer gradient steps and with less number of samples than a purely online RL baseline.

items.title: Physical-Risk-Aware Decentralized Agents for Constrained Vehicle Communications
items.summary: Decentralized V2X resource control is challenging because each vehicle has only local observations, while reliability depends on network-wide interactions. We develop a physical-risk-aware spatio-temporal graph attention (PA-STGAT) framework for agentic V2X control. Each vehicle perceives its local interaction graph, retains short-term temporal context, and independently selects its PC5 resource and power. Network outcomes are used during centralized training to refine the shared policy. Transmitter-specific credits map reliability failures to individual vehicles. A dual-priced graph term further converts network violations into coordination signals for discrete resource selection, with higher priority on short time-to-collision links. Experiments show higher raw-policy reliability than the tested graph-based baselines. Under filtered execution, PA-STGAT meets the nominal empirical communication requirements across all five seeds, with tradeoffs among utility, delivery reliability, resource occupancy, and filter-induced repair. Compared with GNN+MATD3, it requires fewer resource repairs but achieves lower utility and mean delivery reliability. Mechanism ablations show that removing dual-priced graph coordination causes resource-selection collapse. Density and mobility tests characterize the operating limits of empirical constraint satisfaction.

items.title: DiSKO: Distribution Steering for Nonlinear Systems using the Koopman Operator
items.summary: This paper studies the problem of data-driven covariance steering for stochastic, nonlinear dynamical systems. We utilize Koopman operator theory to learn, directly from data, an approximate linear representation of the nonlinear dynamics in a lifted space of observable functions of the state. By exploiting this linear model, we design controllers for the mean and covariance of the underlying nonlinear system by utilizing linear distribution steering algorithms. To account for approximation errors in the learned dynamics and the ambiguity in the disturbance distribution induced in the lifted space, we formulate the problem as a distributionally robust covariance steering problem. Furthermore, we leverage a deep neural network (DNN) to simultaneously learn the Koopman observables and the linear model parameters, thus eliminating the need for manual observables basis selection while also reducing the dimensionality of the lifted representation. Additionally, we can promote desirable model properties, such as stability, during DNN training. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework via numerical simulations.

items.title: Dual Flow: Joint Image-Measurement Interpolation for Inverse Problems
items.summary: Generative model-based approaches to linear inverse problems typically use the acquired noisy measurement to condition or guide sampling in the image domain. In this work, we introduce Dual Flow, a novel joint-flow model for solving linear inverse problems by jointly estimating the clean image and corresponding noise-free measurement from the observation. Specifically, Dual Flow formulates image reconstruction and measurement denoising as a coupled estimation problem, using coupled flows in the image and measurement domains. The acquired noisy measurement is used only to initialize the measurement state; thereafter, image and measurement states are jointly updated based on their current values. By construction, the final image and measurement estimates are guaranteed to satisfy the underlying forward model. We derive the sampling updates for the joint-flow which involves the conditional mean of the clean image given the joint state. We further derive a closed-form expression for a sufficient statistic of the joint state and show that the required conditional mean can be obtained by solving an image-domain Gaussian denoising problem involving operator-dependent, correlated noise. We train a velocity-prediction network using this formulation to estimate the conditional mean from the derived sufficient statistic. Extensive experiments across various linear inverse problems and image datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in both distortion metrics and perceptual quality. Dual Flow requires no hyperparameter tuning beyond the number of inference steps and achieves shorter reconstruction times than competing methods. Additional analyses assess robustness to model mismatch, as well as the ability to generate diverse plausible reconstructions and characterize reconstruction uncertainty.

items.title: Fictitious Play When Agents Are Not Expected-Utility Maximizers: A Geometric Analysis in $2$-Action Games
items.summary: Fictitious play (FP) is one of the earliest and most fundamental learning procedures in games, where each agent independently chooses a best response to the empirical distribution of opponents' past actions by maximizing the expected payoff with respect to it. However, learning agents may not always be expected-utility maximizers: they may use nonlinear evaluation functionals to account for the uncertainty induced by the opponents, e.g., via risk measures. In this work, we study nonlinear fictitious play (NL-FP), in which each pure action is evaluated by a general, possibly nonlinear functional of the payoff distribution induced by the opponent's empirical belief. To analyze NL-FP, we first identify a single-crossing property (SCP) of evaluation functionals that preserves the classical geometry of FP in $2\times2$ games. Furthermore, we conduct a novel geometric analysis of the convergence behavior of NL-FP in $2\times2$ games, even when the SCP fails. Beyond $2\times2$ games, we show that the convergence of NL-FP in $2\times n$ ($n\ge3$) games may fail even for continuous-time NL-FP, when the two-action player uses conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) in a $2\times3$ game. In addition, we identify a finite-crossing condition that ensures convergence of the selected continuous-time dynamics and the discrete-time iterates in general $2\times n$ games, which also provides new insights into the global landscape of continuous-time classical FP in such games.

items.title: Stability Despite Misalignment: Model Predictive Game Controllers with Objective Misspecifications
items.summary: Predictive control requires the controller to possess an embedded prediction model. In multi-agent control, this prediction model must consider the behavior that emerges from other agents' strategic decisions. Game theory offers a natural model for the emergent collective behavior of self-interested agents. Model predictive games (MPGs) are a class of controllers in which an agent iteratively solves a finite-horizon game to predict the behavior of a multi-agent system and synthesize their own control action. When all agents use the same game model to select their control action, conditions have been found that guarantee the closed-loop stability of the multi-agent system. However, when multiple agents implement their own MPG controllers, their respective game models may be misspecified due to inaccurate estimates or conjectures about other agents' objectives. This paper analyzes the consequences of these prediction misalignments on the system's behavior. We show that existing stability conditions for homogeneous MPG controllers do not extend to the heterogeneous setting, even when they hold for each agent's individual game. We provide sufficient conditions for the stability of multi-agent dynamical systems with heterogeneous MPG controllers adopting linear-quadratic (LQ) games. We also show that misaligned game models can destabilize a system that reaches stability when all agents share the same game model, using a financial duopoly simulation.

items.title: Data Archive for 2D and 3D Electrical Impedance Tomography with moderate conductivity contrast phantoms
items.summary: This document describes open Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) measurement data that were collected from biomedical imaging inspired phantoms with moderate conductivity contrasts. The data were collected with the KIT4 and KIT5 EIT measurement devices at the University of Eastern Finland, and are intended for EIT image reconstruction algorithm development and testing. The data from thoracic imaging inspired cylindrical and chest-shaped phantoms are suitable for 2D algorithms, and the data from an intracerebral hemorrhage imaging inspired head-shaped phantom with resistive skull are suitable for 3D algorithms. In addition to the measurement data, computational meshes and example reconstruction codes are provided and sample reconstructions included.

items.title: FanCyqlone: A Parallelized Solver for Multi-Horizon Optimal Control
items.summary: Multi-horizon optimal control aims to select optimal control sequences simultaneously for several possible future scenarios, ensuring consistency at the first stage. While this enables advanced model predictive control schemes that explicitly handle prediction uncertainty, solving these problems tends to be costly. We introduce FanCyqlone, a linear solver that exploits parallelism across both time steps and scenario branches. The method builds on Cyqlone to compute the contribution of each branch and combines these results through a shared root problem. We integrate FanCyqlone into QPALM to develop FanCyQPALM, a solver for multi-horizon optimal control problems with general linear stage-wise constraints. We compare its performance with state-of-the-art solvers on spring-mass and quadruped control benchmarks.

items.title: Admissibility-Preserving Control for Block Strict-Feedback Systems Under Time-Varying Asymmetric Actuator and State Constraints
items.summary: This paper addresses the tracking control of block strict-feedback nonlinear systems subject to time-varying asymmetric actuator and full state constraints. To that end, we develop a time-varying Admissibility-Preserving Control (APC) framework, in which the Admissibility-Preserving Input Realization (APIR) generates the plant input through a dynamic realization. The APIR guarantees input admissibility under the moving actuator set whenever each actuator bound contracts slower than the decay rate of the realization, and a closed-form lower bound on its gain is derived. The state constraints are handled by a logarithmic barrier coordinate at every backstepping step, with widths measured from the virtual control to the moving envelope of the corresponding state. We prove that every state lies inside its envelope, with each virtual control only required to remain inside the envelope of the next state, while the tracking error converges to zero exponentially. Simulations demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed safety-critical control scheme.

items.title: Generalized Gated Recurrent Neural Networks for Nonlinear System Identification
items.summary: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) networks are the two most widely adopted recurrent neural networks for black-box nonlinear system identification, yet they are invariably treated as mutually exclusive structural choices. To move toward a general framework that inherits the properties of both networks, we introduce the Generalized Gated Recurrent Neural Network (GGRNN), a unified architecture that embeds the exact GRU and LSTM network dynamics through homotopies between their respective gating mechanisms. Each homotopy continuously deforms one mechanism into the other, with a vector of homotopy parameters blending the contribution of the GRU and LSTM counterparts. Since benchmark comparisons report no consistent winner between the two architectures, the gating mechanism best suited to a given system is unlikely to coincide with either endpoint. We thus let each recurrent unit learn its own position along these homotopies, obtaining gating behaviors that neither endpoint can express. We pair the GGRNN with a two-stage training methodology: in Stage 1 we co-train all shared and network-specific parameters in parallel at the GRU and LSTM endpoint architectures, while in Stage 2 we freeze the network parameters and optimize only the homotopy parameters. Experiments on the Wiener-Hammerstein and Nano-Drone benchmarks show improved simulation accuracy over the co-trained GRU and LSTM networks on most output groups, and over the reference black-box baselines in nearly all comparisons.

items.title: A Tutorial on Gaussian Process Learning-based Model Predictive Control
items.summary: This tutorial provides an accessible and implementation-oriented introduction to Gaussian process learning-based model predictive control (GP-MPC), which combines probabilistic residual modeling with receding-horizon control. Its central tutorial contribution is a detailed, step-by-step derivation of multi-step mean and covariance propagation for GP-augmented prediction models. The derivation shows how commonly used propagation formulas follow from the laws of total expectation and total covariance, and clarifies the roles of the GP posterior mean, GP posterior covariance, uncertain inputs, and query-output cross-covariances. Building on this foundation, the article distinguishes mean-only unconstrained GP predictive control from uncertainty-aware constrained GP-MPC, clarifies regulation and output-tracking formulations, and provides concise implementation and computational-complexity guidance, including practical software-tool references and discussion of the scope of closed-loop guarantees. Mobile-robot path-following examples illustrate mean-only unconstrained implementations, whereas mixed-vehicle platooning illustrates uncertainty-aware constrained GP-MPC with uncertainty-dependent safety-distance tightening.
