The tutorial is intended to help researchers and practitioners understand, implement, and critically evaluate GP-MPC designs for robotic and autonomous systems operating under modeling uncertainty.

items.title: Convergence and stability of Q-learning in Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning promises, among other benefits, to efficiently capture and utilize the temporal structure of a decision-making problem and to enhance transfer learning capabilities, but theoretical guarantees lag behind practice. In this paper, we propose a Feudal Q-learning scheme and investigate under which conditions its coupled updates converge and are stable. By leveraging the theory of Stochastic Approximation and the ODE method, we present a theorem stating the convergence and stability properties of Feudal Q-learning. This provides a principled convergence and stability analysis tailored to Feudal RL. Moreover, we show that the updates converge to a point that can be interpreted as an equilibrium of a suitably defined game, opening the door to game-theoretic approaches to Hierarchical RL. Lastly, experiments based on the Feudal Q-learning algorithm support the outcomes anticipated by theory.

items.title: TuMAP: A Dual-View, Morphotype-Aware Pathomics Pipeline for Quantifying Renal Tubular Remodeling
items.summary: Quantifying disease-associated renal tubular remodeling is challenging because tubular appearances are heterogeneous. We introduce TuMAP (Tubular Morphotype-Aware Pathomics), a pipeline combining (1) dual-view foundation-model representations and provisional morphotype annotation, (2) compositional and within-morphotype pathomics, and (3) patient-level statistical inference. From 456,158 tubules in 358 PAS-stained kidney biopsy slides, TuMAP identified eight image-based morphotypes, seven of which showed stable subsampling assignments. Across 219 patients in six diagnostic groups, diabetic nephropathy (DN) and tubulointerstitial nephritis/acute tubular injury (TIN/ATI) each differed from minimal change disease in seven morphotype proportions, while IgA nephropathy differed in six. DN showed reduced nuclear solidity and increased eccentricity across all eight morphotypes. Area-normalized nuclear density exposed additional within-morphotype differences. TuMAP provides a framework for separating changes in tubular morphotype composition from phenotypic differences within morphotypes.

items.title: Speed-to-Power Dominates Energy Costs for AI Data Centers: Technoeconomic Analysis of Powering AI in the Continental United States
items.summary: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence is driving demand for new data centers at large scale and on short deployment timelines. To power them, firms connect to the commercial grid or contract generation directly, but interconnection and gas-turbine delays now incentivize on-site generation. We compare grid-connected and off-grid data center energy infrastructure (AC- and DC-coupled solar-plus-storage, islanded natural gas, and grid interconnection) across the continental U.S. Using an open-source technoeconomic framework built on empirically calibrated AI training loads, climate-driven cooling, stage-by-stage power conversion, and physics-based battery degradation, we model designs providing equivalent energy services. Our central contribution is a speed-adjusted cost of energy that values the compute unlocked by faster construction, making options with different deployment timelines directly comparable on one physically consistent basis. We find DC coupling reduces lifetime energy costs by 18% ($0.09/ kWh) on average versus AC counterparts by eliminating inverters and improving efficiency. Though rarely cheapest on unadjusted energy cost, DC-coupled microgrids' faster deployment makes them the lowest-cost modeled option in 85% of U.S. locations once foregone compute is valued, or 55% under accelerated natural gas timelines. For AI infrastructure, deployment speed rather than unit energy cost determines the economically preferred path to power.

items.title: Total Energy Shaping of Underactuated Systems via Gravity Compensation at the Desired Equilibrium
items.summary: This paper investigates total energy shaping of underactuated mechanical systems with gravity compensation evaluated at the desired equilibrium instead of throughout the online closed-loop operation. Within the interconnection and damping assignment passivity-based control (IDA-PBC) framework, sufficient conditions for local asymptotic stability are established in terms of integrability of a vector field and positive definiteness of an augmented potential energy. The approach is also combined with a reformulation of potential energy matching that replaces a nonhomogeneous partial differential equation with a homogeneous one and introduces an additional design term. Analytic constructions for the TORA system and a class of two-degree-of-freedom systems illustrate how the matching and integrability requirements can be addressed. The proposed control law avoids online evaluation of the configuration-dependent gravity term; offline controller synthesis and verification can still require knowledge of the gravity model.

items.title: GRID-MRI: Resilience Assessment of Power Systems under Coordinated Cyber-Physical Attacks
items.summary: The increasing penetration of inverter-based resources and growing cyber-physical interdependencies expose electrical power systems to disturbances that challenge conventional resilience assessments. Existing approaches often evaluate resilience dimensions independently, overlooking the non-additive effects of coordinated disruptions and the influence of exogenous stressors. To address this gap, this paper proposes a Grid Multidimensional Resilience Index (GRID-MRI) that integrates endogenous disruption severity, coordination effects, and climatic and economic-regulatory conditions. The framework quantifies physical, cyber, and operational degradation, identifies interaction effects through counterfactual (i.e., what-if), simulations of individual and coordinated attacks, and incorporates exogenous stressors as scenario-dependent scaling factors. Its application to a modified IEEE 39-bus system under three escalating cyber-physical attack scenarios, informed by the December 2025 Polish cyberattack incident, reveals that coordinated attacks induce system collapse despite stable individual and additive responses. The corresponding resilience losses are 3.72 and 4.09 times their additive estimates, while GRID-MRI increases from 0.062 to 1.188 and reaches 6.081 under additional exogenous stress. These findings demonstrate the limitations of additive assessments and establish a quantitative basis for distinguishing the dominant mechanisms of multidimensional resilience degradation.

items.title: Capacity-Constrained Delayed Feedback for Online Conformal Risk Control
items.summary: Online conformal risk control (OCRC) enables reliable uncertainty quantification in machine learning by converting model outputs into prediction sets with long-term risk guarantees. These guarantees, however, hinge on the assumption that the loss of each round is revealed immediately and losslessly. In practice, feedback may be delayed, and limited resources may prevent tracking all pending predictions, causing some feedback to be lost. To address this challenge, we develop capacity-aware OCRC (CA-OCRC), a framework that jointly determines how to allocate limited tracking feedback capacity and how to construct prediction sets. CA-OCRC is based on a randomized tracking policy that samples a proxy delay to decide whether, and for how long, feedback for the current round is tracked. CA-OCRC updates the prediction sets via inverse probability weighting, compensating for the possibility of feedback lost due to delays and limited tracking capacity. We analyze risk bounds for both arbitrary and stochastic delays, revealing a trade-off between receiving more feedback and avoiding capacity saturation. Building on these bounds, we optimize the proxy delay distribution, showing scaling laws for the tracking capacity that ensure the same long-term risk as OCRC with unlimited feedback. Experiments on medical imaging, natural language processing, computer vision, and wireless communications show the effectiveness of CA-OCRC as compared to existing OCRC mechanisms.

items.title: Robust Control Design for LTI Systems with Sampling-Time Jitter
items.summary: Sampling-time jitter makes a sampled-data control loop time-varying, so standard LTI robust-control synthesis does not apply directly. This paper reformulates dynamic output feedback design under bounded, unmeasured sample-to-sample jitter as a robust-control problem. The exact zero-order-hold model is decomposed into a nominal time-invariant plant and a memoryless, time-varying uncertainty block with a norm bound representing the sampling-time jitter. As the block is memoryless, the operator small-gain condition for the time varying loop reduces to a standard robustness test with a matrix norm bound. It is shown that the same test also guarantees uniform exponential stability for every admissible jitter sequence. Embedding the decomposition into a generalized plant with performance channels serves two synthesis objectives with standard robust-control tools: Robust stability with optimized nominal performance through structured H-inf synthesis, and robust performance through mu synthesis with constant scalings. A numerical example shows that jitter can destabilize a control loop with a nominal H-inf controller, whereas both robust designs remain stable and the robust-performance design is less sensitive to jitter at the cost of nominal performance.

items.title: Control-Gibbs Distribution: Sampling for Optimal Control and Diverse Actions
items.summary: While conventional optimal control selects an optimal input sequence, probabilistic control assigns probability mass over all possible inputs and exploits a distribution of control sequences. Control distributions help enable exploration, capture diverse solutions, and solve deterministic optimal control problems. This work reviews an important probabilistic model for control distributions, the control-Gibbs distribution, i.e., the Gibbs distribution with an optimal control objective as the energy function. We point out its fundamental role in various probabilistic control frameworks, e.g., maximum entropy control, control-as-inference framework, model predictive path integral control, and energy-based models for control. This provides a model-central perspective to unify these probabilistic control frameworks. We also review the associated extensions of dynamic programming for computing closed-loop control distributions. To sample the control-Gibbs distribution, we consider projected Langevin sampling and develop non-asymptotic guarantees. The guarantees show the dual benefits of sampling the control-Gibbs distribution: obtaining diverse control solutions and solving the deterministic optimal control problem. We provide a numerical example where diverse arm trajectories are sampled from a control-Gibbs distribution.

items.title: An Integrated Architecture for Data-Efficient Real-Time Neural Imitation of Nonlinear Time-Optimal Model Predictive Control
items.summary: Nonlinear time-optimal model predictive control (TOMPC) enables highly performant control of constrained systems, but its computational cost prohibits real-time use on fast dynamical systems. Neural network imitation of the TOMPC control law can reduce online computational costs, yet existing work mostly targets quadratic cost formulations in simulation and addresses the challenges of neural controllers in isolation. This work imitates a long-horizon nonconvex TOMPC with hard terminal constraints, whose high computational cost limits training-data generation. We present (i) \emph{self-informed sampling (SIFS)}, a data-efficient expert-sampling strategy that uses a learned time-to-go to query the expert only where the policy deviates from time-optimal behavior, (ii) a complete training and control architecture that jointly addresses dataset correlation, suboptimal expert labels, covariate shift, constraint satisfaction and model mismatch, and (iii) real-world validation on a Furuta pendulum. SIFS matches standard dataset aggregation performance in roughly one-third of the training time and with less than half the training data. The resulting controller matches the region of attraction of the expert TOMPC while raising the control frequency from 1.4~Hz to 1~kHz. On hardware, the controller swings up and stabilizes the pendulum along trajectories closely matching the expert TOMPC solution.

items.title: Channel-Chart-Driven Antenna Activation for Energy-Efficient Cell-Free Massive MIMO
items.summary: Cell-free massive MIMO (CF-mMIMO) can provide uniformly high system performance across the coverage area through distributed cooperation. However, keeping all antennas active leads to high circuit and fronthaul power consumption. This paper studies energy-efficient uplink reception through antenna activation, where only a subset of distributed antennas is selected to serve the users. To enable network-wide activation with low signaling overhead, each access point (AP) maps its locally estimated channel state information (CSI) into a lowdimensional channel-chart (CC) embedding and forwards this representation to the central processing unit (CPU) instead of the full CSI. Based on the received embeddings, we formulate a binary antenna-activation problem for network EE maximization and propose three low-overhead strategies: (i) direct embeddingdomain activation using a proxy EE metric without CSI reconstruction, (ii) nearest chart-point CSI approximation, which estimates CSI from a reference chart database for greedy EE optimization, and (iii) decoder-based CSI reconstruction using a pre-trained autoencoder. The proposed approaches further enable a systematic comparison of antenna activation techniques in terms of achieved performance, computational complexity, and signaling overhead. Numerical results show substantial EE gains over the all-active baseline, with only a minor degradation in sum spectral efficiency and a significant reduction in signaling overhead. Moreover, the proposed greedy framework achieves EE performance close to that of the simulated annealing baseline, confirming its effectiveness for low-complexity antenna activation.

items.title: Integrating Sensing into Covert Communications: Opportunities and Challenges
items.summary: Covert communications aim to hide the existence of wireless transmissions from unauthorized adversaries. However, conventional designs based on blind interference or passive uncertainty can be ineffective in dynamic propagation environments. This article investigates sensing-empowered covert communications, where adversary and environmental information are used to guide transmission and jamming control. We show how sensing changes covert system design from passive concealment to state-aware decision-making, while also introducing new challenges related to exposure and resource consumption. We further discuss several intelligent sensing paradigms that extract task-relevant information with limited active probing. A case study in low-altitude wireless networks illustrates that sensing-assisted beamforming can improve spatial resource utilization and the reliability of covert data delivery in time-varying channels. Finally, several open issues are discussed to support more adaptive covert wireless systems.

items.title: CT-RespGeomLib: Deterministic reconstruction of CT airway masks into editable,port-matched lumen geometry
items.summary: Patient-specific airway modelling requires geometrically consistent lumen surfaces with identifiable boundaries and support for controlled anatomical modifications. We present CT-RespGeomLib, a deterministic framework that converts CT airway masks into two complementary representations: an editable assembly of semantically labelled pipe and junction blocks connected through canonical shared ports, and a fused lumen surface reconstructed from tapered implicit primitives with validated port-to-boundary loop correspondence. The parametric representation further enables localised modelling of airway stenosis and dilation without re-segmentation. Evaluated on 42 reference airway masks from ATM22 (15 cases) and AeroPath (27 cases), the framework produced 37 topologically accepted reconstructions, with a median port-to-loop distance of 0.123 mm across 2174 matched ports. Reconstructed and reference equivalent radii showed strong agreement ($R^2 = 0.976$), with a mean bias of -0.414 mm arising primarily from the circular, inscribed-radius representation. Controlled pathology modelling generated 40 variants across five patient-specific geometries, including 25-75% stenosis and 50% dilation at tracheal and main-bronchus locations. Prescribed radius changes were reproduced with a mean absolute ratio error of 0.0056, while the median 95th-percentile deviation outside the modified region was 0.111 mm. Downstream applicability was demonstrated through volume meshing and an OpenFOAM simulation with individually prescribed model-based resistance conditions at 62 outlets. Although additional surface preparation may be required for numerical meshing, CT-RespGeomLib provides a reproducible framework for CT-derived airway reconstruction, quantitative boundary validation and controlled geometric pathology modelling.

items.title: Efficient Multi-Organ Segmentation Using SpatialConfiguration-Net with Low GPU Memory Requirements
items.summary: Even though many semantic segmentation methods exist that are able to perform well on many medical datasets, they are often not designed for direct use in clinical practice. The two main concerns are generalization to unseen data with a different visual appearance, e.g., images acquired using a different scanner, and efficiency in terms of computation time and required Graphics Processing Unit (GPU) memory. In this work, we employ a multi-organ segmentation model based on the SpatialConfiguration-Net (SCN), which integrates prior knowledge of the spatial configuration among the labelled organs to resolve spurious responses in the network outputs. Furthermore, we modified the architecture of the segmentation model to reduce its memory footprint as much as possible without drastically impacting the quality of the predictions. Lastly, we implemented a minimal inference script for which we optimized both execution time and required GPU memory.

items.title: Survivability Guarantees for Delayed Serial Supply Chains under Demand Shocks
items.summary: When demand exceeds the maximum production capacity of a supply chain, it can be satisfied only for a finite time, determined by the inventory stored along the chain. Existing control methods ensure indefinite constraint satisfaction under bounded demand, but provide no guarantees on how long a supply chain can withstand a shock in which demand goes beyond production capacity. We address this gap for a serial supply chain with transportation delays and flow constraints. Under a specified flow policy, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions on the inventory distribution that guarantee a prescribed lower bound on the exit time from the set where demand is served. We use these conditions to compute inventory targets that minimize holding costs via a quadratic program. Then, we propose a two-mode controller that builds reserves under ordinary demand and depletes them during the shock. Simulations illustrate this approach.

items.title: A Modulation Strategy for Bidirectional Integrated Onboard and Wireless EV Charging
items.summary: Integrated electric vehicle chargers reduce cost by sharing power conversion hardware between the onboard charger (OBC) and the wireless charger (WC). A previously proposed dual active bridge (DAB)-based OBC/WC shares the rectification stage between the OBC and WC; however, the modulation required to realize its wireless operation has not yet been reported. This paper details a modulation strategy that enables the operation of the integrated OBC/WC topology. Differential-mode operation is used for the OBC, and common-mode operation is used for the WC. In OBC mode, the shared full-bridge produces differential-mode voltage for wired power transfer while ideally generating zero common-mode voltage on the wireless charging path. In WC mode, the same full-bridge produces common-mode voltage for wireless power transfer while ideally generating zero differential-mode voltage on the onboard charging path. The method preserves conventional DAB phase-shift power control and enables bidirectional power transfer in wired and wireless charging modes without additional contactors. Design considerations for the OBC transformer and WC coils are derived based on the resulting square-wave voltage amplitudes. Offline PLECS simulations demonstrate power tracking and decoupled charger operation at $\pm$7.4 kW. Hardware-in-the-loop simulations using a PLECS RT Box and an external Texas Instruments microcontroller further validate the proposed modulation method.

items.title: Kezek: Splitting Mono Two-Person Conversations into Per-Speaker Tracks for Full-Duplex Dialogue Data
items.summary: Full-duplex spoken dialogue models learn turn-taking, overlaps and backchannels from conversations recorded with one channel per speaker, but most available conversational audio is a single mono mix. We present Kezek, a model that turns a mono recording of exactly two people into one track per person with the original length and timing; overlaps and short replies ("yeah", "mm-hm") stay on the track of the person who said them. Kezek decides who speaks when and who is who once for the whole recording (stage 1: a two-voice activity model guided by a speaker fingerprint trained to be insensitive to phase), and a conditioned time-domain separator only carries out that decision (stage 2), with outputs that always sum to the input. Standard separation metrics miss the failures that matter for dialogue data, so we report short-reply retention, leakage onto the other person's solo, channel swaps and coverage. Against the open pipeline pyannote -> DialogueSidon on the same recordings, Kezek keeps more short replies (0.83 vs. 0.69 on Open Yap test; 0.80 vs. 0.71 over the other's speech on unseen telephone speech from CallHome English), mostly because it returns the whole recording while the external pipeline drops part of it (on the audio both return, reply retention is about the same: 0.859 vs. 0.865 on Open Yap); it also leaks less, swaps channels less often, and runs 4-5 times faster (about 230 hours of audio per GPU-hour). We also report negative results and an ideal-mask ceiling that locate the remaining gap: quiet replies under a louder voice. Code and weights are released under permissive licences.

items.title: Improved Single-Input Space Vector for DC-Biased Sinusoidal Current Control in Battery Cyclers
items.summary: This paper presents improvements to the single-input space vector (SISV) concept for current control in a battery cycler based on a two-phase interleaved buck converter. The cycler is controlled to output a dc-biased sinusoidal current, enabling investigation of second-harmonic ripple effects on lithium-ion cell aging. A modified SISV generation scheme is introduced to track current references containing both dc and sinusoidal components, and an impedance-angle compensation method is proposed to decouple the d and q control axes without disturbing dc tracking. A dq phase-portrait visualization method is also introduced to evaluate transient performance for both SISV and proportional-integral-resonant (PIR) control methods. Simulation and experimental results validate dc-biased sinusoidal current tracking using PIR control and SISV control with different decoupling schemes. The phase-portrait framework allows for straightforward evaluation of transient performance for both SISV and PIR control methods and supports controller tuning to obtain desired trajectories. The results demonstrate the feasibility of SISV-based current control as an alternative to PIR control for battery-cycler applications. The proposed improvements support the development of battery cyclers capable of controlling both dc and sinusoidal current components.

items.title: Physics-informed structured learning of a class of recurrent neural networks with guaranteed properties
items.summary: This paper proposes a physics-informed learning framework for a class of recurrent neural networks tailored to networked systems. The approach aims to learn control-oriented models that preserve the structural and stability properties of the plant. The learning algorithm is formulated as a convex optimisation problem, allowing the inclusion of linear matrix inequality constraints to enforce desired plant features. Furthermore, when the plant exhibits structural modularity, the resulting optimisation problem can be parallelised, requiring communication only among neighbouring subplants. Simulation results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

items.title: SAGAS: Semantic-Aware Graph-Assisted Stitching for Offline Temporal Logic Planning
items.summary: Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) provides a rigorous framework for specifying long-horizon robotic tasks, yet existing approaches face a trade-off: model-based synthesis relies on accurate labeled transition systems, whereas learning-based methods often require online interaction, task-specific rewards, or specification-conditioned training. We study LTL-specified robotic planning and execution in an offline, model-free setting, where the agent is given only fixed, task-agnostic trajectory fragments, with no dynamics model, task demonstrations, or online data collection. To address this setting, we propose SAGAS, a framework that combines the compositionality of symbolic synthesis with the data-driven reachability structure learned from offline trajectories. SAGAS first learns a reusable latent reachability graph and a frozen goal-conditioned executor from fragmented offline data. For each new LTL formula, it performs task-time semantic graph augmentation to ground state-defined propositions on the learned graph and applies Büchi product search to synthesize a cost-aware accepting prefix--suffix waypoint plan executed by the frozen executor. This separation of learning and planning enables zero-shot generalization to unseen LTL formulas and new predicates supported by the offline data, without task-specific rewards, additional data collection, or policy retraining. Experiments on LTL task suites constructed from OGBench locomotion domains show that SAGAS achieves higher success rates and lower execution costs than baselines on diverse unseen tasks, with further evaluation in OGBench Scene demonstrating its applicability to robotic manipulation.

items.title: Automated PD-L1 Tumor Proportion Scoring with Uncertainty-Guided Triage in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer
items.summary: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) tumor proportion score (TPS) informs immunotherapy selection in non-small cell lung cancer. Near the 1% and 50% cutoffs, the score should also indicate when closer review is warranted. We designed a three-stage framework to follow the sequence of TPS assessment. Stage 1 identifies tumor regions and excludes macrophage-rich patches. Stage 2, a dual-branch cell counting network (D2Count-Net), counts PD-L1-positive and PD-L1-negative tumor cells in these regions to calculate TPS. Stage 3, TPS-Guard, an uncertainty-guided triage mechanism, reports model uncertainty as the disagreement among independently trained models, refers the most uncertain slides, and flags scores near the 1% or 50% cutoff when model estimates disagree across that cutoff. Flags state the reason for referral or alert the pathologist to possible scoring errors on auto-reported slides. In a retrospective, single-center study, 154 whole-slide images were scored by three pathologists, and the model and each pathologist were compared in turn with the mean of the other two. On the 114 slides unseen in training, model mean absolute error (MAE) was 6.96 percentage points, within the range of the three pathologists (4.24 to 8.29), and model uncertainty correlated with absolute TPS error (Spearman rho = 0.77) and inter-pathologist disagreement (rho = 0.71). After referral of the 15% most uncertain slides, model and pathologist MAE both decreased. Applied without retraining to an external, publicly available dataset, TPS-Guard still directed review to higher-error cases, and referring more uncertain cases raised sensitivity at the 50% cutoff. TPS-Guard provides reasons for reviewing individual automated scores and identifies slides that also produce greater disagreement among pathologists. Prospective reader studies should assess TPS-Guard's effect on TPS reporting.

items.title: Mode-in-Variance Participation Factors under Stochastic Excitation
items.summary: This paper investigates how the dynamic modes of a power system contribute to the stationary variance of its variables under continuous stochastic excitation. Using a modal decomposition of the covariance matrix, the variance of each state or algebraic variable can be resolved into components associated with individual modal responses and their interactions. These components are shown to correspond to within-mode variance and cross-modal covariance, respectively, and the corresponding normalized contributions are termed mode-in-variance participation factors (PFs). The proposed PFs can be used to identify modes governing the variability of important system quantities such as frequency and voltage, quantify the effect of modal interactions, and reveal control dynamics that can be targeted to reduce their stochastic variability. These capabilities are demonstrated through case studies based on the Kundur two-area and IEEE 39-bus systems.

items.title: A New Analytical Method and Interpretation of Loss-of-Load Counts
items.summary: This paper establishes the relationship between loss-of-load expectation (LOLE) and loss-of-load frequency (LOLF). We show why LOLE generally does not measure distinct-event frequency, mean event duration, or shortage magnitude. We identify conditions under which peak-based LOLE admits a frequency interpretation as the expected count of deficient daily peaks per horizon and distinguish this quantity from LOLF. We also derive an analytical formulation for frequency-and-duration indices that combines a convolution-derived generation probability-and-frequency model with chronological load changes. Under stationary generation, it uses the prescribed load profile directly, without constructing a separate load model or discretizing load magnitudes. Studies using generation and load data from the 24-bus IEEE RTS reveal different event frequencies and mean event durations at identical peak-based LOLE, motivating their separate assessment. Numerical comparisons demonstrate the accuracy advantage of the proposed analytical calculation over the conventional analytical implementations, quantifying the LOLF errors incurred by load discretization.

items.title: Adjacent Heat Transfer Effects Can Bias Savings Estimates When Controlling Only Part of a Multi-Zone Building
items.summary: Field demonstrations of advanced heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning control often operate a few thermal zones within a larger building and report savings for those zones alone. A recent theorem showed that this practice overestimates whole-building savings, because heat drawn from the neighboring zones is paid for by their equipment and is not counted. The error grows with the thermal conductance between the controlled and uncontrolled zones, with how much colder the controlled zones run over the test, and with the price of the heat their neighbors supply. For one controlled zone with one neighbor, a single thermal price, and slowly changing prices, the relative error reduces to the ratio of two conductances, a screening number that can be evaluated from the two conductances before a demonstration begins. This paper tests how far that reduction can be taken. A two-story house with one thermal zone per floor is simulated over a 90-day heating season in West Lafayette, Indiana, with receding-horizon model predictive control on the first floor and setpoint control on the second, under four combinations of electricity tariff (time-of-use or flat) and heating plant (heat pump or electric resistance). The exact correction from the theorem recovers the true savings in every case, and the full theorem, evaluated from the controlled zone's temperatures, the prices, and the building parameters, reproduces the measured relative error in every case. The conductance ratio bounds that error from above in all four cases, tightly under a flat tariff, within 3%, and loosely under a time-of-use tariff, where most of the controller's savings come from shifting load through the thermal mass rather than from lowering the temperature.

items.title: Transmission-Mode Multispectral Imaging for Estimation of Microcystis spp. Cell Concentration and ELISA-Equivalent Microcystin Concentration in Water
items.summary: Harmful algal blooms dominated by Microcystis spp. threaten freshwater systems through proliferation and microcystin (MC) production. Conventional measurements of cyanobacterial abundance and MC concentration commonly require laboratory processing, specialized instrumentation, or assay reagents. Because MC concentration cannot always be reliably inferred from cell abundance, complementary optical approaches for estimating both quantities are of interest. This study proposes and evaluates a transmission mode multispectral imaging (MSI) framework for estimating Microcystis spp. cell concentration and ELISA-equivalent MC concentration from culture derived dilution samples. A custom built MSI system acquiring twelve spectral bands from near-ultraviolet to near-infrared wavelengths measured transmitted light spectral responses. Following principal component analysis based dimensionality reduction, spectral variation was quantified using an aggregated Wasserstein distance descriptor for regression based prediction. Cell concentration estimation yielded $R^2=0.9819$ for calibration and $R^2=0.9754$ on held-out intermediate dilution levels, while ELISA-equivalent MC estimation yielded $R^2=0.9788$ for calibration and $R^2=0.9786$ on held-out intermediate dilution levels. These results demonstrate the feasibility of transmission-mode MSI as a dual output optical calibration framework for estimation of Microcystis spp. cell concentration and ELISA-equivalent MC concentration in water.
authors: K. A. D. S. A. Perera
A. D. S. N. P. Athukorala
H. A. D. R. P. Sirimanna

items.title: Asymptotic SINR Analysis of Linear Detectors in Uplink Massive NTN MIMO Transmissions
items.summary: This paper examines the performance degradation of receivers caused by imperfect channel state information (CSI), arising from training-based and semi-blind channel estimation techniques. We focus on the uplink of massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems operating in time-division duplexing (TDD) mode, considering the asymptotic regime where the number of base station (BS) antennas grows large while the number of users remains fixed. Leveraging random matrix theory (RMT), we analyze the asymptotic behavior of the signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) under linear MRC and MMSE detection schemes. We derive closed-form approximations of the achievable rates, prove their asymptotic tightness, and validate their accuracy through simulations for systems of finite dimensions. Numerical results under realistic non-terrestrial network (NTN) conditions further demonstrate that semi-blind channel estimation enables MRC and MMSE receivers to outperform their training-based counterparts, while also quantifying the number of pilot symbols required to achieve a desired SINR level.

items.title: On the Nyquist Criterion and the Scaled Relative Graph for SISO systems: A Generalized Circle Criterion
items.summary: Scaled Relative Graphs (SRGs) provide a novel graphical frequency-domain method for the analysis of nonlinear systems. However, existing SRG-based methods are limited to stable open-loop dynamics and can lead to false conclusions when applied to unstable Linear and Time-Invariant (LTI) components. In this paper, we identify the source of this pitfall and resolve it by introducing the extended SRG, which augments the SRG of an LTI system with the encirclement information of the Nyquist criterion. We show how the extended SRG can be used for stability and $H_\infty$-performance analysis of LTI systems and the computation of SRGs for unstable LTI systems. Building on these results, we derive graphical stability and incremental $L_2$-gain conditions for three canonical nonlinear feedback interconnections: the Lur'e system, the controlled Lur'e system, and an LTI plant with Lur'e controller. As a corollary, we derive a user-friendly generalized circle criterion that relates the $L_2$-gain directly to separation between the Nyquist curve and the critical disk from the classical circle criterion, requiring SRGs only for the proof, not its statement. The proposed approach is validated on several examples involving unstable LTI dynamics and nonlinearities, demonstrating applicability beyond the capabilities of existing SRG methods.

items.title: Quantum Network Flows That Solve Linear Equations
items.summary: We develop a distributed quantum network flow for solving linear equations from locally stored row data. Local pumping enforces each node's equation constraint, while neighboring registers interact through swaps. The node marginals obey an exact, closed flow combining consensus with local constraint enforcement. For consistent equations, all node states converge exponentially to a common state supported on the solution space; a unique solution yields full-network convergence to the product solution state. For inconsistent equations of full column rank, scaled encoding and readout recover the least-squares solution through successive large-gain and small-scale limits. For consistent systems, the marginal convergence rate is nondecreasing and concave in the swap gain, approaching a graph-independent limit for fixed local dissipators. Its leading finite-gain correction couples graph topology and row placement through the Laplacian pseudoinverse, enabling semidefinite optimization of edge rates under a fixed total swap-rate budget. For invertible systems, a dissipative HHL-type construction using the same pumping law provides a comparison of solution-state encodings, decay rates, and row-update locality under squared-row-norm pumping. Numerical examples are provided to validate the presented results.

items.title: FlatSeek: LLM-Driven Symbolic Discovery of Flat Outputs via Backward Data Generation
items.summary: Differential flatness enables efficient planning and control, but discovering explicit flat outputs for general nonlinear systems remains difficult due to the lack of general methods and supervised data. We propose FlatSeek, a framework combining backward data generation with task-specific large language model (LLM) training. By reversing the defining reconstruction of flatness, we generate system-flat-output pairs with known certificates, then fine-tune an LLM to propose symbolic flat-output candidates for unseen dynamics. On literature and synthetic benchmarks, FlatSeek outperforms both the traditional symbolic methods and the untuned reference models in flat-output discovery success, and uncovers alternative symbolic flat outputs not reported in the literature.

items.title: CODE-PIF: Convex/Deep (CODE) Multiview Pseudoinvariant Features for Multitemporal Multispectral Surface Reflectance Imagery
items.summary: Multitemporal multispectral surface reflectance imagery exhibits radiometric and spectral variability due to atmospheric effects, sensor differences, and actual surface changes, complicating the identification of pseudoinvariant features (PIFs). The SOTA DeepMGCCA captures nonlinear dependencies across acquisition dates, but similarity in its learned feature space does not directly establish consistency in the original reflectance domain. Meanwhile, we believe that the PIFs extracted by DeepMGCCA preserve essential structural characteristics, providing an effective prior to guide subsequent refinement. Therefore, we propose the CODE-PIF architecture, an unsupervised convex/deep (CODE) framework that refines the coarse PIF from DeepMGCCA using convex optimization. Specifically, CODE-PIF uses the data-fitting term to integrate reflectance deviations, correlation-weighted spectral angles, and temporal reference change information to promote radiometric and spectral consistency between predicted PIFs and observed data. Moreover, the regularization term uses a mathematically simple Q-quadratic norm to incorporate information from the coarse PIF estimate into the refined solution. The resulting convex optimization problem is solved using the ADMM optimizer, which decomposes it into simpler subproblems and provides convergence guarantees under standard assumptions. Experiments across four distinct ROIs show improved average radiometric and spectral agreement relative to DeepMGCCA.Averaged across these regions, the RMSE decreases from 0.0192 to 0.0164, PSNR increases from 35.91 to 37.44 dB, and the between-date spectral angle decreases from 3.77 to 2.97 degrees. Although structural similarity and Pearson correlation do not improve in every scene, the results suggest that using observed data helps select PIFs with more consistent reflectance values and spectral shapes across dates.

items.title: Structure-Preserving Learning for Nonlinear Nonholonomic Dynamics
items.summary: Learning the dynamics of mechanical systems subject to nonlinear nonholonomic constraints is challenging, as data-driven models may violate the underlying physical constraints, leading to inconsistent predictions. To address this problem, we develop a constraint-preserving learning framework based on the Lagrange-d'Alembert-Chetaev equations and tangency to the constraint submanifold, which together define an affine space of admissible accelerations. Using the kinetic-energy metric and the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, we construct a metric projector and the corresponding Chetaev correction. Embedding this geometric structure directly into a Gaussian process prior ensures that both prior and posterior dynamics satisfy the acceleration constraints exactly. We characterize the resulting reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS), derive an adapted-coordinate representation, and establish nonexpansiveness and consistency transfer. Numerical experiments on a three-dimensional directional flocking system with up to 50 agents demonstrate exact constraint preservation and robustness to constraint-incompatible observations.

items.title: ScrewSense: Mapping the Invisible - Anomaly Detection and Error Classification in Screwdriving Processes
items.summary: The growing volume of process data generated by screwdriving systems, combined with advancements in computing power, data storage, and algorithms, is facilitating the application of artificial intelligence in this field. Accurately detecting and classifying screwdriving errors is crucial for ensuring product quality, avoiding costly rework in manufacturing, and supporting sustainability by facilitating the maintenance, reuse, and recycling of screw-connected products. In this context, machine learning approaches offer a promising alternative to traditional monitoring techniques, such as window-based methods or envelope curves. This study examines the use of deep learning techniques for anomaly detection and error classification in screwdriving processes. The data corpus consists of multivariate time series capturing process parameters, such as torque and rotation angle. For anomaly detection, the embedding space of a vector quantized variational autoencoder was analyzed. In terms of error classification, four different model architectures were evaluated. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of anomaly detection and confirm that deep learning models can distinguish between multiple error categories beyond traditional binary classification. This extends the capabilities of conventional monitoring approaches, achieving accuracies of up to 100%. Additionally, real-world data material was examined in order to further demonstrate model robustness. Overall the results indicate strong generalization capability and highlight the practical potential of the developed models for use in industrial screwdriving processes, eliminating the need for expert knowledge in error identification and significantly reducing manual effort and analysis time.

items.title: MESH: Multi-receiver Evaluation of Spatial Hearing across Egocentric and Allocentric Views
items.summary: Spatial hearing in multi-receiver environments requires identifying who speaks, where they are, and how they move. Existing benchmarks evaluate spatial prediction, transcription, tracking, and distributed speech processing, but offer limited evaluation of whether speech signal remains associated with the correct physical source across receivers and motion. We introduce MESH, which evaluates this association through egocentric and allocentric views of shared acoustic scenes. The egocentric view uses local recordings and peer metadata, while the allocentric view combines synchronized recordings from multiple receivers in a shared 3D world frame. MESH contains nearly 40,000 questions across 13 static and dynamic localization and spatial transcription tasks. We evaluate eleven audio-model configurations and a language-model agent using specialist tools. The best static distance-estimation and dynamic direction-tracking accuracies are only 21.90% and 41.54%, respectively, while the lowest word error rates across four transcription tasks range from 59.15% to 73.10%. Ablation studies and additional experiments reveal that existing models are not yet able to effectively leverage peer information and struggle to handle multi-speaker and dynamic scenarios. These findings highlight the gap between access to distributed acoustic information and its effective use for spatial speech understanding. We release the dataset and evaluation code to support further research on collaborative and distributed spatial hearing.

items.title: RadarML: A Multi-Channel Over-the-Air Dataset of Common Radar Waveforms for ES Evaluation
items.summary: This paper introduces "RadarML", a publicly available dataset of modulated radar pulses recorded over-the-air across multiple semi-independent receiver channels. The dataset was generated using the UCL ARESTOR platform which is a Radio Frequency System on a Chip (RFSoC) based Software Defined Radio (SDR). The dataset contains a library of around two million waveforms with varying centre frequencies, bandwidths, pulse widths and modulations, with 1,000 examples of each signal variation per receiver channel. The goal of this dataset is to enable comparative analysis of radar modulation classification techniques on real data and stimulate research into multi-channel signal detection and modulation classification methods.

items.title: MusicRWKV: A Multimodal RWKV Framework for Music Representation Learning
items.summary: Recent music foundation models have achieved remarkable progress in music representation learning, yet most existing approaches rely on Transformer architectures whose quadratic attention complexity introduces substantial computational and memory overhead when modeling long-duration music recordings. In this work, we propose MusicRWKV, a multimodal music representation learning framework built upon the RWKV architecture. MusicRWKV jointly models waveform, spectrogram, and metadata information within a unified self-supervised learning framework. To improve efficiency for long musical sequences, we introduce an invertible compression module that reduces sequence length while preserving reconstruction capability. A FiLM-based conditioning strategy is employed to facilitate modality-aware representation learning without introducing expensive cross-attention operations. We further investigate the integration of Soft ROSA as a differentiable retrieval mechanism for neural-symbolic interaction. Experimental evaluation across a diverse collection of Music Information Retrieval (MIR) benchmarks demonstrates that the proposed RWKV-based architecture can be effectively adapted to heterogeneous music understanding tasks. A controlled pretraining ablation shows that Soft ROSA improves validation performance, while layer-wise telemetry analysis reveals a progressive transition from distributed retrieval to selective retrieval in deeper network layers. These results suggest that RWKV provides a promising architectural alternative to Transformer-based models for multimodal music understanding.

items.title: Directionally Supervised Neuromorphic Protection for Distribution Systems Using Local Measurements
items.summary: Reliable protection under varying power system operating conditions requires rapid fault detection while preserving selectivity against external faults and non-fault disturbances. This requirement is particularly challenging in communication-free schemes, where relays must determine trip conditions solely from local electrical measurements. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a directionally supervised neuromorphic protection scheme that integrates disturbance-responsive leaky integrate-and-fire dynamics with a direction-dependent firing threshold to distinguish internal faults from reverse-direction events. The unified relay architecture combines local disturbance detection, directional discrimination, and spike-based trip generation without requiring inter-relay communication. Its performance is evaluated under grid-connected and islanded conditions using a ring microgrid and the IEEE 13-node distribution feeder. Across 240 evaluated fault scenarios, the framework achieves median operating times of 5.4--7.6 ms across the two networks, with 78% of cases operating within 10 ms and 95% within 20 ms. It also maintains protection security during load disturbances, while fault-resistance analysis confirms its response under high-resistance faults. Controller-hardware-in-the-loop (CHIL) experiments using an RTDS simulator and an external dSPACE controller demonstrate trip-command assertion in approximately 10 ms and 5 ms for the tested single-line-to-ground and three-phase-to-ground faults, respectively. The results establish real-time feasibility within the evaluated conditions and characterize operating-time variability across fault types and resistance levels for different network configurations.

items.title: Velocity-Free Funnel Control of Euler-Lagrange Systems: An Artificial-Delay Approach
items.summary: Classical funnel control keeps the tracking error within a prescribed, time-varying envelope by increasing the feedback gain as the error approaches the boundary. For mechanical systems, this guarantee typically relies on velocity measurements. We show that it can be retained for fully actuated Euler--Lagrange systems using only position measurements. The proposed controller replaces the velocity error with a difference quotient of the position error over a fixed delay, while preserving the classical unbounded gain. It requires no plant model, reference derivatives, observer, or filter states. The central challenge is to reconcile the averaging inherent in delayed feedback with a gain that can grow without bound near the funnel boundary. We resolve this by establishing an a priori bound on the gain along closed-loop trajectories, independent of the delay. This bound yields a computable delay threshold that guarantees tracking within the prescribed funnel and boundedness of all closed-loop signals. The threshold depends only on bounds on the inertia, forces, and reference. Simulations demonstrate tracking accuracy comparable to full-state funnel control and tolerance of delays substantially longer than certified. With quantized position measurements, the controller also requires substantially less torque than an existing derivative-free funnel controller.

items.title: Transferable Neuromorphic Protection for Distribution Networks
items.summary: Protection of converter-dominated distribution networks is challenging due to limited fault currents, operating-mode transitions, bidirectional power flow, and heterogeneous network configurations. This paper proposes a scale-invariant neuromorphic protection framework to enable transferable protection decisions across such networks. The framework integrates asset-based normalization, multi-domain disturbance representation, event-driven spike encoding, leaky integrate-and-fire (LIF) dynamics, adaptive threshold regulation, and directional supervision within a unified mathematical formulation. Local voltage, current, active power, and reactive power measurements are transformed into dimensionless disturbance representations, while latency encoding and membrane integration capture disturbance intensity and temporal evolution. The framework is evaluated across four heterogeneous network configurations: a two-DER inverter-interfaced microgrid, an islanded ring microgrid, the IEEE 13-node feeder, and the CIGRE European medium-voltage benchmark. Across 480 cases, it achieves a median operating time of 7.6 ms, with 94.2 % of cases operating within one power cycle. The results demonstrate selective protection across different electrical ratings and network topologies using a common parameterization without network-specific retuning, highlighting the potential of neuromorphic processing for physically interpretable, communication-free protection of converter-dominated distribution networks.

items.title: Energy system device sizing under closed-loop operation with imperfect forecasts
items.summary: The value of renewable energy devices depends on their operation, which must adapt to weather and demand using limited, imperfect forecasts that update over time. Conventional energy systems planning practices assume unlimited foresight in a single-level formulation, potentially leading to long-term investment in suboptimal device sizes. Accounting for realistic operation corresponds to a bi-level problem: the upper level selects device sizes, while the lower level contains closed-loop operation under evolving forecasts. We solve this problem using backpropagation MPC (BP-MPC), a gradient-based method, with a deterministic MPC as the lower-level controller. Using forecast errors generated by a parameterized martingale model of forecast evolution, we investigate how forecast accuracy affects the benefits of operation-aware energy systems planning and the resulting device sizes. In a case study of an energy system comprising photovoltaics, a battery, a heat pump, and thermal storage with uncertain weather and energy demands, accounting for closed-loop operation yields higher average cost savings as forecast error increases. The resulting designs achieve these savings by progressively shifting investment from battery storage to solar generation and thermal storage, which buffers forecast mismatches.

items.title: ARIA: Anti-diagonal Reduced-cost Index-masked Adaptive BLMS Algorithm
items.summary: The block least-mean-square (BLMS) algorithm supports high-throughput adaptive filtering but incurs high computational cost as the filter length and block size increase. This letter proposes anti-diagonal reduced-cost index-masked (ARIA) adaptive BLMS, which reduces coefficient-update multiplications through anti-diagonal index masking and tap-wise step-size scaling while keeping the filtering exact. Mean-square error (MSE) analysis establishes an explicit step-size bound, and misadjustment. An extension, ARIA-MF (ARIA with masked filtering), also applies the mask during filtering; its analysis shows that the excess MSE is redistributed across block rows while its block average is approximately preserved. Simulations validate the analysis and shows very good agreement with the estimates

items.title: Measurement-Calibrated Synthetic Pretraining for Rapid Adaptation of UAV Channel Predictors
items.summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) links can change faster than route-specific channel data can be collected, so a channel predictor must often be adapted from only a short target-flight calibration segment. This paper studies measurement-calibrated synthetic pretraining as an offline source prior for rapid adaptation of channel state information (CSI) predictors. The synthetic source is calibrated to flight-only power evolution, temporal shape variation, frequency selectivity, and phase disturbance, and is then combined with measured source-flight fine-tuning before target-flight adaptation. Under chronological held-out flight splits, synthetic-to-real (S2R) fine-tuning reduces the measured-data budget needed to reach useful prediction in the low-data regime. For 50 ms-ahead prediction, it crosses a latest-channel-estimate persistence baseline with 50 measured training windows, roughly 0.5 s of 10 ms-spaced supervised windows, whereas training from scratch requires 600 windows. A target-prefix adaptation study further shows that a lightweight gated recurrent unit predictor can reuse the pretrained source prior with one prediction-layer update epoch, positioning measurement-calibrated synthetic pretraining as a reusable prior for scarce target-flight measurements.

items.title: Empowering AI towards 6G: Realistic UAV Channel Data Acquisition using Open-Source Solutions
items.summary: The "sim-to-real" gap introduced by hardware impairments motivates realistic experimental platforms for AI-native research in Non-Terrestrial Networks (NTN). This paper presents an open-source UAV-to-Ground measurement testbed built on the OpenAirInterface (OAI) stack and commodity Software Defined Radios (SDRs), enabling direct extraction of raw Sub-6 GHz Channel State Information (CSI) synchronized with flight telemetry. Through real-world flight campaigns, we observe a velocity-bandwidth decoupling effect: under unguided, measurement-only ridge extraction, dominant spectral ridges deviate strongly from the theoretical kinematic Doppler trajectory, whereas guided tracking substantially reduces this mismatch. This indicates that Doppler information is present, but not dominant, in the raw observable dynamics of commodity SDR-based measurements. We further benchmark representative deep learning predictors on this hardware-inclusive dataset and show, through a case study, that their behavior differs substantially from idealized expectations. By open-sourcing the testbed and dataset, we provide a realistic foundation for training and evaluating AI models for practical aerial network deployments.

items.title: Optimized Mirabbasi-Martin Pulse Shaping Filter for Higher-Order Modulation in Zak-OTFS
items.summary: The performance of Zak-OTFS modulation depends critically on the delay-Doppler (DD) domain pulse shaping filter, which must support both accurate channel estimation and reliable data detection. Filters reported in the Zak-OTFS literature fall short in bit error rate (BER) performance for higher-order modulation due to sensitivity to model-free channel estimation errors and pilot-data interference. Motivated by this, in this paper, we introduce a separable two-dimensional Mirabbasi-Martin (MM) filter for Zak-OTFS and propose a filter coefficient optimization framework that minimizes the aggregate sidelobe energy while preserving the compact structure of the MM prototype. By trading exact Nyquist nulls for high localization, the optimized MM filter exhibits no sidelobes with the narrowest $-40$ dB DD domain pulsewidth compared to sinc, Gaussian, and GS pulses. This compactness of the optimized filter tightly confines the pilot energy within the pilot region of the embedded frame, ensuring that the full response is captured for model-free channel estimation while significantly reducing pilot-data interference. This yields both an improved estimation performance and a significantly improved BER performance for higher-order QAM. For the proposed filter, we derive closed-form expressions for the effective DD domain channel and the covariance of the receive-filtered noise, which drastically reduce simulation run times. Our simulation results demonstrate that the optimized MM filter achieves significantly better uncoded/coded BER performance for higher-order QAM compared to that of sinc, Gaussian, and GS filters. For example, for 64-QAM with M=32, N=48, rate-1/2 convolutional code, and TDL-A channel model with fractional DDs, the optimized MM filter achieves a coded BER of 3x10^{-4} at an E_b/N_0 of 40 dB, while the sinc, Gaussian, and GS filters exhibit error floors above 10^{-2}.

items.title: The Unseen Threat: How Complementary Combinations of Acoustic Features Compromise Speech Privacy
items.summary: The interaction of acoustic features in leaking private information remains underexplored. This work focuses on time-domain features, i.e., broadband RMS level and pitch, alone and combined with temporally smoothed and subsampled Mel spectrograms. Privacy is assessed using informed automatic speech recognition and speaker-verification attacks, while utility for conversational analysis is evaluated using voice activity detection and speaker diarisation. RMS level and pitch alone exposed limited information, but fusion with 500 ms-smoothed Mel spectrograms enhanced utility while substantially increasing speech-content leakage. Specifically, the combination with RMS level showed that fine-grained temporal dynamics can amplify leakage from coarsely sampled spectral features. Speaker-identity protection remained limited for all tested features. Overall, these findings indicate that privacy assessments performed on individual acoustic features may underestimate leakage after feature fusion.

items.title: Certified Dynamic Subspace Optimization for Bayesian ISAC Design
items.summary: Full-space covariance optimization is costly in large-array Bayesian integrated sensing and communication (ISAC). A fixed transmit subspace can reduce this cost, but the resulting optimality loss depends on the posterior distribution. In this paper, a certified dynamic subspace method is developed for angle Bayesian Cramér-Rao bound (BCRB) minimization under joint angle and complex-gain uncertainty. For uniform linear arrays, exact response preservation over a nondegenerate posterior angular interval requires the full antenna space. Subspace sufficiency is therefore assessed through full-space objective-gap bounds. A communication-feasible basis is initialized from the user-channel span and local BCRB sensitivity. Restricted semidefinite programs are then solved. Primal restoration and dual repair yield gap bounds that remain valid after lossless user-beam recovery. When an accurate restricted solve does not certify the requested tolerance, the basis is expanded using a direction identified from the covariance dual slacks. Under a strict communication-power margin, joint uniqueness of the restricted optimal dual multipliers is established. With exact restricted solves, this uniqueness guarantees strict BCRB improvement after certificate-driven expansion. Numerical results validate the bounds against full-space references for the sampled problems. Compared with a fixed Fisher ordering, the proposed method can reach the same certificate target with fewer dimensions. On large arrays, total runtime is reduced relative to the full-space and factorized baselines at matched certificate targets.

items.title: A Dual-Branch Graph and Convolutional Network for Interpretable Movement EEG Classification
items.summary: Decoding upper-limb movements from scalp electroencephalography (EEG) is an important problem for brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but many deep learning models provide limited insight into the brain regions underlying their predictions. We propose a two-branch architecture that combines an LGGNet-inspired local-global graph branch with an EEGNet-style convolutional branch for movement-versus-rest classification. The graph branch groups 61 EEG electrodes into anatomically informed regions and learns their spatial relationships, providing a direct representation of the regions emphasized by the model. We evaluate the proposed architecture using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation on the Ofner upper-limb movement dataset. The model achieves a mean F1-score of 0.74 +/- 0.06 across subjects. Beyond classification performance, we analyze the learned graph structure to identify the regions with the strongest connectivity. Across all held-out subjects, the highest connectivity is consistently observed in the Parietal Left Low region, corresponding to electrodes P1 and P3. This region is opposite to the performed right-arm movements and lies within the posterior parietal area previously associated with upper-limb movement processing. These results show that incorporating a region-based graph into the decoder can provide an anatomically interpretable representation while maintaining effective movement classification, offering a practical approach toward more transparent EEG-based BCIs.

items.title: Ramping Procurement and Bid-Cost Recovery in Real-Time Market
items.summary: We study ramping procurement co-optimized with economic dispatch under net-demand uncertainty. We examine two flexible ramp product designs implemented by grid operators: single-interval and multi-interval co-optimization. Both rely on rolling-window stochastic optimization with binding and advisory interval decisions. We develop analytical frameworks to evaluate generator profits, consumer payments, bid cost recovery (BCR), and operational efficiency. In particular, net-demand uncertainty may lead to generator under-compensation, requiring discriminatory BCR. While operational efficiency is invariant to energy and ramp prices, producer profits and consumer payments depend critically on pricing. We examine locational marginal pricing (LMP) and two uniform pricing: maximum dispatch cost pricing (MDCP) and maximum temporal locational marginal pricing (MTLMP). With out-of-market BCR, LMP yields discriminatory energy prices, whereas MDCP eliminates BCR and MTLMP does so in most cases. This property enables us to establish truthful bidding incentives for price-taking generators under MDCP. Our analysis highlights trade-offs between single- and multi-interval co-optimization and pricing designs: multi-interval energy-ramp co-optimization outperforms single-interval co-optimization when ramping forecasts are accurate and ramping needs are tight, but its advantage diminishes under large forecast errors and moderate ramping needs. Empirical results on CAISO and ERCOT data show that MDCP and MTLMP increase producer profits with negligible BCR, albeit at the expense of higher consumer payments relative to LMP.

items.title: Can STATCOM and UPS-Based Voltage Support Mitigate Fault-Induced Reductions in AI Data Center Grid Power Draw?
items.summary: Artificial intelligence data centers (AIDCs) are rapidly increasing in number and capacity. These large electronic loads are interfaced through power electronic devices and can sharply reduce grid power intake during fault-induced voltage sags. Disturbances exceeding equipment ride-through capabilities may also trigger protective disconnection, posing risks to power system security. Static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs) and appropriately controlled AIDC uninterruptible power supply (UPS) rectifiers can provide reactive power support during voltage sags. This paper compares the individual and combined effectiveness of STATCOM and UPS-based voltage support in mitigating fault-induced reductions in grid power intake through electromagnetic transient simulations of a 1 GW AIDC connected to an IEEE nine-bus system. Simulation results show that STATCOM support better preserves short-term intake in milder tested faults, whereas UPS coordination maintains rectifier operation under deeper sags by reducing active intake to reserve reactive current capacity. Combined support improves auxiliary load retention and recovery in selected cases. However, severe tested sags still cause substantial grid-demand reductions even with combined support.

items.title: Medical Image Segmentation based on Deep Active Contour and Mean Curvature Loss Function
items.summary: Pixel-level supervision in medical image segmentation ignores the geometric priors of the target region. Chan-Vese losses restore region-level priors and boundary regularity but do not characterise local boundary geometry. We propose the Deep Active Contour and Mean Curvature (DACMC) loss, which embeds the mean curvature of the predicted boundary in the Chan-Vese region functional; a fixed fourth-order-accurate convolution kernel evaluates curvature without explicit differentiation. The loss adds no trainable parameters and no inference cost, increases training time by 4.8%, and uses one hyper-parameter lambda = 10^-3 shared by all settings. We evaluate DACMC on liver CT, spleen MRI and ISIC dermoscopy images with U-Net and CE-Net backbones, four metrics (DSC, HD95, JS, ASD) and four competing losses under an identical protocol, together with a five-point lambda sweep, a wall-clock cost measurement and a five-seed replication with paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. DACMC ranks first or second in Dice in five of the six dataset-backbone settings, most consistently in distance metrics. On spleen MRI it reduces HD95 and ASD to 16.28 and 1.90 mm, and on ISIC dermoscopy it reduces HD95 to 7.08 mm. Dice varies by 0.0023 across five lambda values spanning three orders of magnitude; degradation appears only when curvature dominates. Five-seed replication shows that curvature stabilises training and removes occasional severe failures, although mean differences from the closest competing loss do not reach statistical significance at five seeds. DACMC imposes second-order geometric regularity on segmentation boundaries at low overhead, with the clearest benefit for small or scale-varying targets. Limitations include dataset size and partitioning, classical backbones and losses, and restriction to 2-D single-organ images.

items.title: Delta-Iterations: A General-Purpose Linear Regression Solver for Huber's Penalty, $ε$-Insensitive Loss, and Other Moreau Envelope-Based Loss Functions
items.summary: A general-purpose linear regression solver for a class of smooth loss functions is presented. The method applies to loss functions of the Moreau envelope type, which are continuously differentiable and have Lipschitz-continuous first derivatives. This class includes piecewise-defined cost functions consisting of constant, linear and quadratic segments, such as Huber's loss, insensitive least squares, one-sided least squares. The convergence guarantee provided by the associated proximal operator, the simplicity of the method and its versatility in handling various cost functions within a unified framework are its main advantages. MATLAB code for reproducing the numerical results presented in this article is provided.

items.title: Incremental Model Predictive Control for Reference Tracking of Nonlinear Anesthesia Dynamics
items.summary: Anesthesia dynamics are commonly described by Wiener models, consisting of linear dynamics followed by a static nonlinearity. This nonlinear output complicates the derivation of theoretical guarantees on closed-loop stability and convergence. Model Predictive Control (MPC) is particularly suitable for anesthesia control, as it explicitly accounts for constraints in the control design. In this paper, we propose an incremental MPC formulation for tracking a desired reference. The proposed approach exploits the structure of the nonlinear output equation to reformulate the control problem within a linear framework. An incremental model is then employed to avoid the explicit computation of steady states and inputs, which may be inaccurate in the presence of model uncertainties. The proposed controller is evaluated through simulations involving 1000 virtual patients and compared with a benchmark MPC formulation. Results show improved steady-state reference tracking while maintaining satisfactory disturbance rejection.

items.title: A Joint LLM and Optimization Agent Solution for Drone Scheduling in Victim Search Missions
items.summary: Victim search in wilderness areas is time-critical. Drones enable rapid area search, but scheduling them is challenging because victims may continue moving, detection results are uncertain, and effective decisions must combine structured mission information with unstructured contextual clues and domain knowledge. To address this, we propose an agent-aided drone scheduling system. The system employs an agent at the ground control station (GCS) to coordinate multiple drones over successive search cycles. In each cycle, the agent applies a scheduling policy that combines a large language model (LLM) for reasoning about where to search with an optimizer for determining how to dispatch the drones under energy constraints. Simulation results show that the proposed system consistently completes the victim-search mission, whereas none of the six non-LLM baselines does so and direct LLM scheduling is considerably less reliable. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/1643204431/llm-uav-victim-search.

items.title: PiLLVD: A Real-World Low-Light Video Dataset for Dynamic Scenes Captured with Off-the-Shelf Cameras
items.summary: Low-light image and video enhancement has received increasing attention in recent years. However, most existing enhancement methods are developed and evaluated on still images, while progress in low-light video enhancement remains limited by the lack of real-world paired video datasets. Acquiring paired low-light and normal-light video sequences is challenging because it requires spatially and temporally aligned captures while avoiding motion blur, exposure mismatch, and correspondence errors in dynamic scenes. To address this gap, we introduce PiLLVD, the Pi-based Low-Light Video Dataset, a paired low-light video dataset captured using an accessible Raspberry Pi-based multi-camera system with off-the-shelf cameras. PiLLVD provides paired low-light and aligned normal-light reference sequences for dynamic indoor and outdoor scenes, including diverse human and object motion under varying illumination conditions. Unlike existing datasets that are often image-based, static, synthetic, or limited to simple motion patterns, PiLLVD focuses on motion-rich scenes where frame-to-frame stability and motion-related artefacts are important for evaluation. In addition to presenting the dataset and acquisition pipeline, we benchmark representative pre-trained low-light video enhancement methods on PiLLVD under a zero-shot setting. The results show that existing methods do not generalise uniformly across the proposed sequences, highlighting the challenges posed by the proposed dataset and its value for both benchmarking existing methods and supporting the development of future low-light video enhancement algorithms.

items.title: Input-output characterization of robotic grasping: Connecting design parameters to grasp behavior through the admittance
items.summary: Low-impedance grippers make the dynamics of a grasp matter. Current grasp metrics, however, are static: they describe how a held object resists constant loads, not how it responds to time-varying ones. To quantify this, we rely on small-signal analysis to characterize a grasp by its admittance, the transfer matrix relating load perturbations to object displacements around an equilibrium. This transfer matrix recovers the stiffness and stability of the grasp at zero frequency and captures its natural frequencies and peak gain under time-varying loads. We apply this characterization to a planar two-finger gripper under proportional-derivative control. We show that two grasps of the same object in the same position and with the same contact forces can differ in stiffness by two orders of magnitude. Likewise, two grasps that share the same stiffness can exhibit very different resonances. Nonlinear simulations confirm the effectiveness of our small-signal analysis in capturing the dynamic behavior of grasping.

items.title: ART for Diffusion Sampling: A Reinforcement Learning Approach to Timestep Scheduling
items.summary: We consider time discretization for score-based diffusion models to generate samples from a learned reverse-time dynamic on a finite grid. Uniform and hand-crafted grids can be suboptimal given a budget on the number of time steps. We introduce Adaptive Reparameterized Time (ART), which controls the clock speed of a reparameterized time variable to redistribute computation along the sampling trajectory while preserving the terminal time, with the objective of minimizing the aggregate Euler discretization error. We derive a randomized companion ART-RL that recasts ART as a continuous-time reinforcement learning problem with Gaussian policies, and prove a two-directional bridge between the two: the deterministic ART optimum lifts to an optimal Gaussian policy, and conversely any optimal Gaussian policy must recover the ART control through its mean. This bridge turns continuous-time actor--critic learning into a principled, rather than heuristic, route to the deterministic timestep optimum. Within the official EDM pipeline, ART-RL improves FID on CIFAR--10 across a wide range of budgets; after one-time offline training, the distilled deterministic schedule transfers without retraining to AFHQv2, FFHQ, and ImageNet at no extra inference cost.

items.title: FACE: Few-shot Adapter with Cross-view Fusion for Cross-subject EEG Emotion Recognition
items.summary: Cross-subject EEG emotion recognition is challenged by significant inter-subject variability and intricately entangled intra-subject variability. Existing works have primarily addressed these challenges through domain adaptation or generalization strategies. However, they typically require extensive target subject data or demonstrate limited generalization performance to unseen subjects. Recent few-shot learning paradigms attempt to address these limitations but often encounter catastrophic overfitting during subject-specific adaptation with limited samples. This article introduces the few-shot adapter with a cross-view fusion method called FACE for cross-subject EEG emotion recognition, which leverages dynamic cross-view fusion and effective subject-specific adaptation. Specifically, FACE incorporates a cross-view fusion module that dynamically integrates global brain connectivity with localized patterns via subject-specific fusion weights to provide complementary emotional information. Moreover, the few-shot adapter module is proposed to enable rapid adaptation for unseen subjects while reducing overfitting by enhancing adapter structures with meta-learning.
